Blake is confident enough that he would be happy to be homed as an only dog as long as his adopter had plenty of time to spend with him, but he does get along really well with other dogs and could be homed with a kind resident dog who won't mind his enthusiastic personality. We would consider homing him with dog savvy teenagers aged 13+ and he would be best suited to a home with adopters who have dog experience.

Blake has never lived in a home before, so his adopters will need to be patient and understanding as he learns all about home life, including house training.

He can walk on a lead and would love to find an active home with adopters who can keep him busy, enjoy adventures with him and understand his bouncy nature. Blake has already been showing us just how clever he can be and has recently learned to play fetch, even bringing the ball back! He even already knows how to sit on command. He is an eager-to-please boy with so much love and enthusiasm for life, and he is more than ready to find a family of his own.

We have been told the breeder that Blake requires a grain free diet, so this will need to continue in his new home. Our vet has noticed that he has narrow ear canals, but this does not seem to bother him.

Blake has been given the Gift of Life by Nicola McNamee

name: Otis
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden with 6ft+ fences.

I have started harness training, but this is still new to me!

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I am neutered and ready to find my forever home!

Otis has come to us from a breeder to find his forever home. He is an extremely nervous boy who is still finding the world a very scary place and is utterly petrified of human touch. When he first arrived, he would do everything he could to avoid being touched, frantically running around the yard to escape contact. Although he was interested in people, he simply didn't feel brave enough to let them close.

Otis is now making small but lovely steps forward, although he is still extremely worried about touch, with those who he knows very well he will tentatively accept chin tickles, though is still very worried about this. He still needs to build his confidence, and getting him comfortable with human hands will be a slow process that is likely to continue well into his new home. His adopters must be prepared to work at his pace, without rushing or putting pressure on him.

Although he is still quite worried, he can be quite unsettled when people leave his kennel and so may develop separation anxiety in his home. He will need adopters who are happy to work with him on this, helping him to feel more comfortable and gradually building up the time he can be left alone. With patience, consistency and lots of reassurance, we hope he will soon learn that he is safe and doesn't need to worry when his people leave him.

At just one year old, Otis has plenty of typical Labrador puppy character waiting to shine through. He loves tennis balls and soft toys and is still figuring out how to play fetch! As his confidence grows, we're beginning to see more of his funny, silly personality, and we hope there is lots more to come.

Otis absolutely adores other dogs and takes great comfort and reassurance from their company. He will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in his new home to help him feel safe and guide him as he learns about life in a home. Having a canine friend by his side will be particularly important while he continues to build trust in people.

Otis will need a calm, quiet, adult-only home with adopters who have experience with scared ex-breeding dogs and understand the time and patience they need. He has never lived in a home before, so he will need help learning all about home life, including house training. He will also need a secure garden with fencing of at least 6ft to keep him safe while he gains confidence.

Otis has started harness training with his kennel mummy, and this will need to continue in his home at a slow and comfortable pace. This will need to be introduced gradually, starting in a safe environment and allowing him to progress at his own pace.

Otis is a special little boy who is trying so hard to be brave. With patient, understanding adopters and a confident canine companion, we believe he has the potential to blossom into a fun, loving and rewarding companion. He will need a family willing to celebrate the smallest steps forward and give him the time he needs to discover that the world can be a wonderful place.

Otis has been given the Gift of Life by Nic Johhston

Otis is a few weeks into his stay at Many Tears and honestly, he’s breaking my heart. That being said, he is progressing slowly, in his own funny way.

Otis is utterly petrified of human touch and when he first arrive he would do literally anything to get away from me. I mean truly frantic to avoid being touched. He would bolt away in the yard and do laps to avoid any contact. He wouldn’t take treats from my hand despite being a massive foodie! Yet when I turned around he would show interest to me and would nibble my hand through the gates. He so wanted to be brave and just didn’t know how.

We are slowly getting there, it’s not much of a progression to most people but he will freeze with me now and tentatively accept chin tickles. Small baby steps, we are already seeing progress! Desensitising Otis to human hands is not going to be a quick fix and will likely continue into his home life. He does now take treats from my hand, even in the yard but after each treat he does a little lap of the yard to ramp himself up for the next one! He really is such a funny little guy.

At just 1 years old, he has so much of your typical Lab puppy in him, but he just doesn’t feel safe enough to fully let it out. He loves a tennis ball and is still coming to grips with how fetch works. He loves soft toys and ADORES the company of other dogs and seeks so much comfort and support from them.

Once Otis is more comfortable being handled, our next milestone will be getting him in a harness to begin the road to exploring the world on walks!

He is such a character & the more confident he becomes, the more we get to see his funny, silly side. I really do believe he will settle into the most fulfilling, fun dog you could hope for & will make his future adopters very happy!

Otis has come to us from a breeder to find his forever home. He is a very nervous boy who is feeling very overwhelmed by all the changes in his life and is finding his surroundings quite scary at the moment. He is very worried about being handled and it is clear that he has not had much socialisation before, so he is in need of lots of patience, kindness and TLC.

Otis will be looking for a calm and quiet, adult only home with adopters who have experience with scared ex-breeding dogs and understand that he will need plenty of time to settle in and build his confidence at his own pace. He will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in his new home to be his friend and companion and help show him the ropes. Having a confident canine friend by his side will be very important as Otis begins to learn that the world is not such a scary place.

Otis will also need a secure garden with 6ft+ fencing to keep him safe while he gains confidence. He has never lived in a home before, so his adopters will need to be kind and understanding as he learns all about home life and new skills such as house training.

Otis doesn't yet walk on a lead and harness and this will need to be introduced very gradually by practicing first in the garden, allowing him to gain confidence before venturing further afield.

Otis is a very worried boy who needs someone special to give him the time and understanding he deserves. With a calm environment, a confident canine companion and lots of patience and love, we hope that little by little he will begin to feel safe and discover the happy boy hiding underneath all those worries.

She has started to learn all about walking on a lead and harness and though this is still new to her, she is doing well. Sunny is an amazing lady who has so much to look forward to and will make a wonderful addition to a loving and accepting home.

Sunny has arrived with an undershot jaw that does not seem to bother her, but will need to be monitored in her new home. She has had 4 teeth removed at the time of her spay.

Sunny has been given the Gift of Life by Victoria Charlton

Sunny has been on my section for more or less the whole time she’s been at the rescue, and I know we’re not supposed to have favourites, but I just love her so much! She’s SO comical and has such an infectious energy. She can make me laugh and smile by doing absolutely nothing. I can’t explain it, she’s just funny!

She absolutely loves toys and lights up every morning when I bring them to her kennel. She checks on every one and then will pick her favourite one and carry it into bed with her. So sweet! She also loves being in bed. Especially when she’s snuggled up with one of her kennel friends. Her favourite thing in the whole world though, is definitely food. She is such a greedy little monster when it comes to treat time or breakfast or dinner time. She will do pretty much anything if she knows she’ll get a yummy snack out of it. I’ve recently started harness training with her and this has been a huge help. I always have liver paste on hand and she’s doing so well with it. We’re still only walking around quiet places of the rescue currently, so she’s definitely not a pro yet, but she’s getting there!

If you have a house full of toys, love and cosy beds, please consider welcoming this cheeky little darling.

name: Iggy
description:
I can live with older, dog savvy teenagers, aged 13+ who respect my space.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I am new to lead walking, and would like to continue this once I have settled in.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have Grade 3 bilateral luxating patellas.

Iggy is a scared little lady who has come to us from a breeder. She has now been with us for almost two months and, although she has made some lovely progress, she has had very little interest so far.

Iggy's biggest fear is being touched. When someone reaches for her, she can crouch down and tremble with fear, but she is slowly learning that people can be kind and that she is safe. She is beginning to show more interest in people and, by watching the other dogs around her, has started running towards her carers' hands and giving them a little boop! She has also started taking treats, which is a huge step forward for this very special girl.

Iggy takes great comfort from her kennel friends and will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home to help her build confidence, learn to trust and discover the joys of home life. She absolutely loves being out in the yard with her friends and enjoys nothing more than rolling around in the sunshine.

As Iggy has never lived in a home before, her adopters will need to be patient while she learns about house training and settles into a new routine. She is still new to lead walking and will need continued, gentle encouragement as she learns. She will need adopters with experience of ex-breeding dogs who understand how frightened she can be and are prepared to give her plenty of time and patience.

Iggy can live with older, dog-savvy teenagers aged 13+ who are sensible and able to allow her to settle at her own pace.

Iggy has been assessed by our vets and has Grade 3 bilateral luxating patellas. These are not causing her any issues at present and may improve with gentle exercise as she builds muscle. They will need to be monitored by her adopters and their vet, and they should be aware that any future treatment relating to her luxating patellas will not be covered by insurance.

Iggy is a wonderful girl who has already shown us that, with the right canine companion and plenty of patience, she can take those important little steps forward. We hope the right family will give her the chance to continue blossoming and discover how lovely life can be.

Iggy has been given the Gift of Life by Susan Stacey

This wonderful girl is Iggy! It’s been almost two months since she arrived, and although she is doing incredibly well, sadly she has had very little to no interest so far.

As a Frenchie / Bulldog lover myself, I took to this girl instantly, and she has now moved into my section. She has settled in so well and walks beautifully on her harness.

Iggy’s biggest fear is being touched. When someone reaches for her, she crouches down as though she wishes the ground would swallow her up, and she trembles with fear. Every day, I sit beside her in her kennel and gently stroke the side of her face, reassuring her that she doesn’t need to be afraid anymore. She is slowly learning that not everyone is there to hurt her, but I can only imagine what this poor girl may have experienced in her life.

What makes her progress even more special is seeing her learn from the other dogs around her. When they come over for fuss, Iggy has started running towards my hands and giving them a little boop! She has even started taking treats, which is a huge step for this very special girl.

Iggy absolutely loves being out in the yard with her friends. She enjoys nothing more than rolling around in the sunshine, and I could happily sit and watch her all day when she’s feeling relaxed and happy.

But as wonderful as her time here has been, I know that what Iggy truly needs now is a home of her own. A quiet, patient and understanding home where she can continue to learn that the world isn’t such a scary place, at her own pace, surrounded by people who will never give up on her.

Iggy is a scared little lady who has come to us from a breeder. She is beginning to show an interest in people and will cautiously approach if you crouch down to her level, but she quickly loses confidence if movements are too fast or overwhelming. She simply needs time to learn that people can be kind. Iggy takes great comfort from her kennel friends and will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home that she can lean on as she builds her confidence, learns to trust, and discovers the joys of home life. As Iggy has never lived in a home before, her adopters will need to be patient while she learns all about house training and settles into a new routine. She can live with older, dog-savvy teens aged 13+ who are sensible and allow her time to settle in. She will need adopters who have experience with ex-breeders as she can be nervous and will need a home that understands her needs.

She is new to lead walking and will need continued, gentle encouragements in her new home as she continues to learn. Iggy is a wonderful girl who just needs time, patience and lots of TLC. With an understanding family and a confident canine companion by her side, we're sure she will continue to blossom and find her paws.

Iggy has been assessed by our vets who have noted that she has Grade 3 bilateral luxating patellas. These aren't causing her any issues at the moment and may improve with gentle exercise as she builds muscle. They will need to be monitored by her adopters and their vet and her adopters should be aware that any future treatment relating to her luxating patellas will not be covered by insurance.

name: Fallon
description:
I will need an adult-only home that understands me.

I would prefer to be the only dog in the home!

I will need a secure garden, with at least 6ft+ fencing to explore!

I am new to lead walking, and would like to continue this once I have settled in.

I have lived in a home before, but may need some reminders.

I have been spayed & am ready for my forever home!

05-11-26 Fallon is a super sweet and clever girl who originally came to us from a breeder but was sadly returned after struggling to cope with visitors coming and going in her previous home. She is a sensitive lady who can find changes to her environment and unexpected interactions difficult, but she has made wonderful progress with us and has formed some lovely bonds with her main carers. Once she knows and trusts you, her silly, playful personality really starts to shine, and she gives the very best snuggles!

Fallon can mix with other dogs but would prefer to have her own space in a home, so she is looking to be the only dog. She walks well on a lead, although she can occasionally walk in circles when feeling anxious or excited. She may also bark back if another dog reacts towards her. Fallon can be sensitive when resting and has previously startled and made contact when someone sat beside her on the sofa, so her adopters will need to understand her boundaries and give her quiet, undisturbed places to relax.

Fallon is looking for an adult-only home with at least 6ft secure fencing, where her adopters have previous ex-breeding experience and a good understanding of Collies and their sensitive nature. She will need a calm environment, predictable routines and cosy bed spaces where she can retreat when she needs some quiet time.

Fallon really is a lovely girl with so much personality, and it is wonderful to see how far she has come. She just needs someone who understands her needs, respects her space and is willing to give her the time to settle. In return, they will discover a clever, playful and incredibly affectionate companion who has so much love to give!

Fallon has been given the Gift of Life by Carolina Olsen

name: Nicole
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

Nicole has come to us from a breeder and is now searching for her forever home. She was very scared when she first arrived and had clearly had little handling or socialisation, making human contact very worrying for her.

Nicole briefly moved into a foster home to learn about home life but returned to us following one incident where she became tangled in her lead and harness, panicked and nipped her fosterer. This was a single incident during a frightening experience, but adopters must understand that she can panic if she feels trapped or overwhelmed.

Nicole has now been back at the rescue for just over a month and is making lovely progress. She still doesn't like being picked up or handled, but is much better than she was and is increasingly comfortable spending time around people she trusts. She enjoys sitting in the play yard with her trusted people and responds brilliantly to treats, which are helping to build her confidence. She is a curious, cheeky little character who loves food, toys and snoozing in her bed, and she is even trying hard to be kennel clean.

Nicole loves other dogs and takes comfort from their presence, so she will need a kind and confident resident dog to help her feel secure and act as a role model.

She needs a calm, quiet, adult-only home with adopters who have experience of nervous ex-breeding dogs. As she has never successfully experienced home life, she will need patience with house training and learning the basics of being a pet. Lead and harness training will also need to be introduced very carefully because of her previous experience.

Nicole still has a long way to go, but her curiosity and wonderful personality are beginning to shine through. With the right home, canine companion and plenty of time and understanding, we hope she will continue to blossom.

Our vets noted a slightly unusual heart rhythm, and a heart scan showed mild valve changes. She currently requires no treatment and is expected to live a normal, happy life, although routine heart checks and monitoring for future symptoms are recommended. She has been treated for a ear infection.

Nicole has been given the Gift of Life by Shirley Bourne

Nicole has been back at the rescue with me for just over a month now, and even though she is still a scared lady, I can definitely see she has made progress. She still doesn’t like to be picked up and handled, but she’s a lot better with it now than she was when she first arrived. She’s also more content just being in my presence now and will happily hang out with me in the play yard with confidence. I spend a lot of time sitting on the floor with her and dishing out treats every so often to stay in her good books. She does love her food, so this helps massively with building some trust with her!

Nicole does still have a long way to go until she’s anywhere near being a ‘normal’ dog, but she has a lot of curiosity in her and definitely some Shih Tzu attitude as well, so I’m hoping she will blossom in the right home. If you have lots of time and patience, and a space in your heart and home to welcome a special lady, please consider Nicole. I promise you won’t regret it!

Nicole is the type of dog that can instantly put a smile on your face, even when she’s not doing anything. She has such a comical and infectious energy, and I really just love spending time with her. She loves snoozing in bed in her kennel through the day and playing with toys too. She even tries her hardest to be kennel clean!! She’s very easy to look after day to day. So please… give her a chance.

Nicole has been in foster for a week and is a sweetie. She has a wonderfully inquisitive nature and loves investigating everything around her, which makes us chuckle! She is still very nervous about being handled and will bark when she's feeling unsure, but she is already making progress. She now takes treats from us and absolutely loves her food. She is also mostly clean overnight.

Nicole has come to us from a breeder and is now searching for her forever home. She is a lovely little girl who is understandably feeling very scared and overwhelmed to find herself here. It’s clear she hasn’t had much handling or socialisation before, so human hands are quite worrying for her at the moment, but we will continue gently helping her learn that hands can be kind.

Nicole will be looking for a calm and quiet adult only home where she can settle in at her own pace. She would really benefit from adopters who have experience with nervous ex-breeding dogs and who understand the patience, time and reassurance she will need as she learns to trust.

She loves other dogs and takes great comfort from their presence, so Nicole will need another kind and confident resident dog in her new home to take her under their wing and help her feel safe and secure.

As Nicole has never lived in a home before, she will need patient adopters who are ready to help her learn everything about home life from the very beginning. She will need to learn new skills like house training and will also need to learn all about walking on a lead and harness.

With time, kindness and plenty of TLC, Nicole will begin to grow in confidence and let her personality shine.

Our vets have noted that Nicole has a slightly unusual heart rhythm, so she underwent a heart scan at our vets which showed some mild valve changes. At this stage she does not require any treatment and is expected to live a normal, happy life, although we would recommend routine heart checks and monitoring for any future symptoms.

name: Rachel
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I have never been on walks, but may be too scared and will need some time.

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

I have had a pea size cyst removed from my right shoulder at the time of spay.

Rachel is a very scared girl who has come to us from a breeder. When she first arrived she was extremely overwhelmed by her new surroundings and clearly hadn’t had much socialisation or handling before. Since being with us, she has slowly started to show small signs of progress as she begins to realise she is safe. Although she still finds being handled very frightening, her kennel mum can now stroke her gently when she's in her bed at the back of the kennel.

She will need a calm and quiet adult-only homewith adopters experienced with traumatised ex-breeding dogs who can provide the reassurance and stability she needs to continue building her confidence and learning about trust and kindness. Her adopters will need to allow her to settle in at her own pace and let her set the speed of her progress as she can still become easily overwhelmed.

Rachel relies on other dogs for comfort and reassurance and will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home who can take her under their wing and help her settle into her new home. They will need to be happy to snuggle up with her and to let her rely on them for support. For some reason she is especially fond of Dachshunds, but she does love all dogs. When she forms a bond with another dog, she absolutely dotes on them and becomes the most loyal best friend to them. It’s so sweet to see.

Day to day, she is a super happy and laid back girl. She LOVES toys and spends a lot of her time chewing on a bone or playing with a plush teddy in one of her beds. She also really loves her food and this has been a great help in gaining her trust and forming a bond with her.

Rachel has never lived in a home before, so she will need very patient and understanding adopters while she settles in and learns all about home life and new skills like house training.She follows a daily routine beautifully, happily running out to the exercise yards and returning to her kennel when it is time to come back in. She is not currently 100% kennel clean, but she is likely to take to toilet training well in a home, as she toilets almost immediately when she goes out into the yard. Her adopters will need to give her plenty of opportunities to go outside while she learns the new routine. Rachel doesn't walk on a lead or harness just yet, but hopefully in the future this is something that we can introduce to her.

The big wide world still feels quite scary for Rachel, but she is beginning to show curiosity in safe environments, and gentle time in the garden will be a great way to help her slowly explore and build confidence. She is not yet cat tested, but we feel cats are unlikely to be an issue for her, although this would need to be assessed appropriately.

Although Rachel has been making progress and will now allow her kennel mum to gently stroke her when she's in a bed in the back of her kennel, she still doesn't enjoy this. She finds being picked up extremely frightening and will panic and does have the potential to bite purely out of fear, so it is imperative that her adopters fully understand her behaviour and are confident managing her needs. We really don’t think she’ll be this way forever, and she’ll get better and better as time goes on, but it would be a lot easier if she was in a home with someone who knew how to help her.

Recently, Rachel needed to have her thick coat clipped during the warm weather, which unfortunately had to be done under sedation as she is not yet ready to be groomed. Despite how frightening this experience must have been for her, she coped far better than we ever expected, allowing herself to be carried to the vets and held for her injection once she was safely in our arms. We couldn't have been prouder of how brave she was. As her coat grows back, we will continue gently introducing her to grooming so she can slowly learn that being brushed doesn't have to be scary.

Rachel has so much potential and, with time, patience and kindness, we truly believe she will continue to make progress and learn that she is safe and loved. She really is an easy dog to care for in every other aspect – she is wonderful with other dogs, thrives on routine and never puts a paw wrong. She just needs a truly understanding home where she can continue building on the trust she has started to develop and finally blossom into the dog she is meant to be.

Rachel came to us with a pea-sized cyst on her shoulder, which was removed at the time of her spay.

Rachel has been given the Gift of Life by Tracy Davidson

Rachel is doing so much better than we expected and is already showing us little glimpses of the lovely girl she could become. She quickly discovered the dog sofas and has found her favourite spot, where she is happiest relaxing alongside her support Dachshund.

Rachel really loves the Dachshunds in the home and will need to be rehomed with at least one calm, friendly and tolerant Dachshund who she can rely on. She is very attached to them and will look for her friend if they are out of sight. She will even approach her fosterer if her Dachshund is sitting on their knee!

Rachel is becoming more inquisitive and has started to approach for a little nose bump on a finger. She will sometimes allow a hand to be offered to her while she is on the sofa and will give a little finger bump in return. She is still not comfortable with being stroked and made it clear that having her face touched was too much for her, so this is something that will need to be respected and worked on slowly.

Rachel is very observant of the other dogs and watches their interactions with people closely. She is still a very scared girl, but she has already exceeded expectations and is beginning to blossom in her foster home. She is happy to share her space with people as long as they do not get too close, and she is even starting to follow basic instructions such as going inside and moving between rooms.

Rachel is settled downstairs in an open crate in the kitchen alongside two Dachshunds and is happy to settle without making any noise. She can be a little destructive with the mats when left for short periods, but overall she is making wonderful progress. We are so pleased to see her beginning to feel safer and more curious about the world around her.

Rachel (or Rachy as I call her) has had quite a few updates on her page now, so I thought I’d do something a little different with this one and basically summarise her and the type of home she needs!

Rachy is a super happy and laid back girl day to day. She LOVES toys and spends a lot of her time chewing on a bone or playing with a plush teddy in one of her beds. She also loves other dogs - especially Dachshunds!! We have no idea why, but she lights up when she’s around them. When she forms a bond with another dog, she absolutely dotes on them and becomes the most loyal best friend to them. It’s so sweet to see. She also loves her food (probably more than anything), and this has been a massive help in gaining her trust and forming a bond with her. She runs to the play yard from her kennel, and back in with no problems, and she also toilets as soon as she gets to the yard every time, so I have a feeling it won’t take long to house train her at all.

Rachy is very easy to look after at the rescue and follows routine beautifully. If you didn’t know anything about her, she looks like quite a normal and happy dog most of the time. But, and this is a big but, she still absolutely hates being touched, and hates being picked up or handled even more. I’ve taken things very slow with her as she isn’t the type of dog you can rush, so I’ve managed to get to the point with her where I can give her gentle strokes when she’s in one of her beds in the back of the kennel. She doesn’t enjoy it, but she does tolerate it now. Picking her up, on the other hand, is a different story. She’s still not used to it and she will still bite to protect herself, so I do have to use a thick blanket to avoid that. I really don’t think she’ll be this way forever, and I do think she’ll get better and better as time goes on, but it would be a lot easier if she was in a home with someone who knew how to help her.

Things such as walking on a lead, grooming, vet visits etc. won’t come easy, but I do believe she will get there and allow these things in the future. She really just needs someone who will love her for who she is, accept her worries and fears, and work with her on them. Most importantly, she needs someone who will never give up on her no matter what.

Rachel’s progress continues slowly and steadily and even though she still doesn’t like to be touched, she is so much more content and calm in general. She’s now more than happy to hang out with me and lay down near me, and just this week she actually went to sleep next to me with her tummy exposed!!! I know that may not sound like a lot, but it’s HUGE for a dog like Rachel with such severe trust issues.

The past couple of weeks at the rescue have been extremely warm and Rachel started to struggle a little bit with having such thick fur, so I decided to get it shaved off. Rachel is still not ready to be groomed, so I did have to take her into the vets to be sedated. This is the first time I’ve had to actually pick her up since I started going the crate and touch work with her, but it had to be done. She does still try her very best to get away and she does still try to bite, but it is less severe than what it was when she first came in. Getting her into my arms was the most difficult part, but after I had hold of her I was able to walk over to the vets carrying her, and hold her while she had her injection without a fuss. I was so, so proud of her. She’s now a bit bald, but so much more comfortable and cooler. When her fur starts to grow back I am going to start introducing her to a brush so she can get used to it, as her coat does grow quite fast and it’s very dense which means it gets matted easily. It’s not ideal for a dog like Rachel needing to be groomed regularly, but I’ll try my very best to ease her into it.

Looking after Rachel on a daily basis is very easy. She follows routine beautifully - running to the play yards and back into her kennel when it’s time to come in. She tries her best to be clean with her toileting and I think if she had access to a garden regularly, she would pick it up really quickly. She also shares everything with her kennel friends perfectly and she never puts a paw wrong with other dogs. Aside from hating being touched, she really isn’t a problem at all. I really am hoping that she’ll start to get used to it soon, and I think she will … but being in a home would help massively. So I hope she doesn’t have to wait too much longer for that to happen.

For the past month, Rachel has officially been my “project dog”. This means I’ve been spending a lot more time working directly with her, and I set a goal for both of us when I started. Because Rachel’s biggest fear is human hands, that became my main focus — helping her feel more comfortable with being touched and gently stroked.

In the first week, I wanted to get her used to my touch without her panicking. When Rachel thinks she’s about to be handled, she’ll run around the kennel, jumping from bed to bed to avoid me, and will bite to protect herself if I get too close. I felt that all the running and panic was only reinforcing her fear, making things harder for both of us. So, I introduced a crate to safely contain her in a smaller space, allowing me to begin gentle handling in a more controlled way.

My hope was that she would start to realise that a soft fuss on her head or body isn’t actually that scary — that the anticipation was worse than the reality. Each day for that first week, I set up a crate at the back of her kennel and spent a short session gently touching her, just once a day to ease her into it.

On the first day, it took a little while for her to go into the crate, but she eventually went in with her friend. She was actually very good and allowed me to gently stroke her face for a few minutes, before becoming a little unsettled and starting to nibble my hand. By the second day, she went into the crate much more quickly and again allowed strokes around her head and under her ears. As I carefully moved further down her body, she became uncomfortable and nibbled a bit harder to let me know she’d had enough.

By the third day, she went straight into the crate, and I focused more on her body. She allowed longer strokes before becoming unsettled. The fourth day was very similar, but on the fifth day there was a real breakthrough — she let me stroke her tummy and chest without any nibbles at all.

After every session, I made sure to sit at the front of her kennel for a few minutes and give her treats so we always ended on a positive note (and to make sure she was still my friend!). Rachel is known to hold a grudge, so maintaining that trust was really important, and thankfully this work hasn’t damaged our relationship at all.

In week two, my goal was to remove the crate and see if she would choose to stay settled in a bed while I handled her. I wasn’t sure how it would go, but she absolutely amazed me. On the first day, she settled into a bed at the back of the kennel while I sat on the floor and gently shuffled towards her — and she stayed still, allowing me to stroke her. I kept things consistent over the next few days without pushing her too far.

By the fifth day, I introduced something new: scissors around her head. She needs a fringe trim, so I wanted to begin desensitising her to the sensation and presence of them. She did incredibly well — so well, in fact, that I managed to snip a tiny bit, which I hadn’t even planned to do. Because she was coping so calmly, I took the opportunity, and it paid off.

In week three, I continued trimming her fringe gradually, little by little. After a few days, I was able to clear the hair from around her eyes.

That’s where we are now. There’s still a long way to go, and Rachel will need plenty more time, patience and love, but I’m so pleased with how far she’s come. We’ve definitely made real progress, and I’m excited to keep building on it with her.

Rachel has been at the rescue for just over a month now and in that time she’s gained a lot of inner confidence, and has blossomed into a very cheeky and happy girl who always seems to be up to mischief!! She absolutely loves toys and gets very excited when I put them in her kennel every morning, and she also loves playing with them in the yards. She’s also very partial to starting ‘parties’ AKA getting all the dogs to have a massive game of chase with her, which she finds very amusing. Her favourite thing in the world though … food!!! She is one of the foodiest dogs I’ve ever met and is always at the front of the queue for breakfast, dinner, and treats.Even though Rachel has made progress in many areas, one thing she still simply can’t handle is being touched by us humans in any way. Her fear of our hands is so strong and she will try to bite to protect herself. This doesn’t mean she’s a nasty dog in any way, it’s just complete panic and fear. It’s something I’m trying to de-sensitise her to and I’m working with her as much as I can, but I do think it’s going to take a long time and a lot of consistency. We don’t know what she’s been through in her life that’s made her the way she is, so all we can do now is prove to her that humans can be kind, and hope that one day she’s able to put her past behind her.Rachel will need a very experienced home with people who will be extremely patient with her, understand her, and work with her through her worries and fears. She’ll need at least 1 resident dog to learn from, and absolutely no children. Things that are normal to most dogs such as going for a walk, being brushed/groomed, or even just having a little fuss, are alien to Rachel, so it’s important her adopters take all of this into consideration and be okay with it.

It may be a long and slow road to get Rachel to where she needs to be, but I promise it will be so worth it. There is no better feeling than a dog like her showing you love and trust for the first time!

Rachel is a very scared girl who has come to us from a breeder. She is a very scared girl at the moment who is quite overwhelmed to find herself here and clearly hasn't had much socialisation before. She is looking for a home with adopters with experience of scared ex-breeding dogs who can provide the reassurance and stability she needs to help build her confidence as she learns about safety, trust, and our intentions.

She will need an adult-only home that can offer a calm and predictable environment where she can take things at her own pace. Rachel will also need at least one kind and confident resident dog to help her settle in and take her under their wing, as she can be easily overwhelmed at the moment.

Rachel has never lived in a home before, so she will need patient and understanding adopters while she learns about house training and how to walk on a lead. Right now, the big wide world may feel too overwhelming for her, so gentle sniffs in the garden would be a good place to start.

Rachel is only acting out of fear, and we have not yet been able to see the girl she will become once she feels safe. She deserves so much love, she just isn’t sure how to accept it yet and will need a truly understanding home to help her blossom.

Rachel has come to us with a pea sized cyst on her shoulder that has been removed at the time of her spay.

name: Maggie
description:
I'd like a quiet, adult-only home to help me relax and feel safe.

I can be an only dog or live with one dog my size or larger. I cannot live with cats!

I'd like a secure garden to play in that has 6ft fencing.

I walk well on a lead and would enjoy one or two walks a day!

I have lived in a home so I know the basics.

I have been spayed and have had 4 teeth extracted.

Maggie spent the first few years of her life at a breeders & originally came to us when she was 5 years old. She was adopted in January 2025 & spent 16 months in a home. She ended up back in our care & has since waited to find her forever. Maggie really is just the sweetest, most special girl. Whilst she is shy at first, she bonds incredibly closely with her people. She has a cheeky, playful side & loves to fling herself around with a tennis ball. She bounces & prances around the yard just keeping herself entertained. Maggie is our girl who helps the scared dogs be brave. Maggie shows them how it’s done & truly she has been the helping hand for so many dogs since she has been with us. She has seen kennel friends come & go, yet she still waits in kennels. Maggie is a happy dog even in kennels, especially when she is with any of her favourite people. She is so affectionate & truly a little shadow. You gain a best friend when you’re loved by Maggie. Our groomer has said multiple times that she is an absolute delight to groom. Maggie loves nothing more than to roll around in mud, sand, leaves, she gets mucky quickly. Her & our groomer are well acquainted now so she is well adjusted to grooming.

Sadly, Maggie was returned to us following an incident involving one of the smaller resident dogs in her previous home. While out in the garden one evening, Maggie became frightened by the other dog barking, and although we don't know exactly what happened, the interaction unfortunately ended in a fight. They struggled to make up or comfortably co-exist afterwards, so Maggie will need a carefully chosen home where everyone can feel safe and settled.

Maggie is looking for a calm and quiet, adult-only home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and can give her plenty of time, patience and understanding to settle at her own pace. She can be worried by men and initially barked at the male resident in her previous home, although with time, patience and gentle handling, she slowly began to come around. We are continuing to help her build positive relationships with men here, and she has bonded well with a male staff member who is part of her care team.

Maggie is very people-oriented and, once she knows and trusts you, she becomes an incredibly loving and devoted companion. She is particularly attached to her main carer and loves following her around, enjoying fuss and cuddles. When she first returned to us, she was very shy and unsure of new people, but she has since settled in wonderfully and has made lovely progress.

Although Maggie previously lived with another dog, her home will need careful consideration following her return. We would now consider her as an only dog in the right circumstances, with experienced adopters who have plenty of time to help her settle. Alternatively, she could live with a calm, confident resident dog of a similar size or larger. She has shared her kennel with several different dogs since returning and has been wonderful with them, happily sharing food and toys. She also enjoys play dates with a larger group of dogs in our big play yard. I cannot live with cats, so I will need a home without small furries.

Maggie is very food-motivated and loves her treats, which will be helpful when settling into her new home. She can already walk nicely on a lead and harness without pulling and will often check back with you for reassurance. Having previously lived in a home, she will be familiar with home life, although she may need some reminders of her house training.

On one occasion in her previous home, Maggie became tangled in her harness and panicked, biting the hand of the male owner who was trying to help free her. This was an isolated incident caused by fear, but it is important that her new family understands how she may react when frightened or overwhelmed. She will need calm, gentle handling and people who can recognise when she is worried and give her the reassurance and space she needs.

Maggie has also shown that when she feels stressed or overwhelmed, she may try to escape by climbing. For this reason, she will need a very secure garden with boundaries of at least 6ft to help keep her safe.

Maggie has had four teeth extracted, and this should be kept in mind as part of her veterinary history.

Maggie has so much love to give to the people she trusts. In the right calm and understanding home, with experienced, patient and dog-savvy adopters who allow her to settle at her own pace, we are confident she will continue to flourish and become a truly wonderful companion.

Maggie has yet again made some new canine friends here at the rescue, Jinx - Hound and Hayley - Poodle and yet again she has been amazing with them, showing them that us staff here at the rescue are nothing to be feared and helping them understand that a human touch can be loving and kind, she has been incredible with a lot of our scardies and the change you then see in those dogs, a lot of it thanks to Maggie, is amazing, she really is a special girl.I also had to bath her (again) this past week as due to her fur type and the weather she gets dirty rather easily, but, she is so good in the bath, she's very tolerant of the water and being shampooed. When it comes to brushing and drying, she is also easy, for the most part she either just stands or lays there which makes her quicker to dry.She really is a dream dog and she's still waiting for her forever home after almost 5 months. Winter is coming, that means cold days and nights, and although we do everything we can here at the rescue to ensure that they're all comfy and warm, it's nothing compared to the home comforts of being wrapped up in her own blanket, snuggled up with her own family knowing, who wouldn't want that for her?Please consider Maggie, she's one of our most overlooked angels and it genuinely makes me sad that no one seems to take an interest in her. I promise you she'll make an amazing companion and a true best friend just like she is for me while I'm her kennel mum.

Maggie aka Magaluf, Magarita, Mags or Miss Maggie is a special girl. She's the kind of dog that once she's comfortable with you, you instantly feel the love she has for you from her and it's such a lovely feeling, she is very affectionate and loves her people more than anything, well, maybe not more than her food or treats but we're her second favourite.

Maggie's confidence has grown so much these past months that she's even helped some of our more shyer residents come out of their shells, and by them seeing how she is with us makes them realise that they too can be like that with us and have fusses and cuddles etc.

She is an incredible girl and it truly baffles me as to why she keeps getting overlooked. She is beautiful both inside and out and has such a fun personality. She is good with other dogs but won't necessarily need to be rehomed with another dog as we believe that she is confident enough to be an only.

Maggie will become a best friend and a true companion, and I know I'm probably a lot biased being one of her kennel mums but she truly is so so special and anyone would be lucky to have her in their life.

Maggie has settled into rescue life beautifully, but having spent over a year in a home, we are really desperate to get her back into one ASAP!

Since her arrival, Maggie has been kenneled with our lovely Bocker Eddie whom she gets along with wonderfully. She does enjoy her time with him, and would happily live alongside one resident dog - male or female, her size or larger!!

During Maggie’s time here she has formed a wonderful bond with her kennel mums who she absolutely dotes on. She’s even bonded with a kennel dad who has said she’s an absolute sweetheart, and he’s had no trouble with her too, which is so good to hear.

Maggie's kennel mummies describe her as loyal, affectionate, and loving. She really looks to them for reassurance, and when they’re around nothing else matters. Seeing as she’s grown so much in confidence, we’re happy to say she can now also be homed as an only dog too in the circumstance her adopters have lots of time to spend with her!!

Maggie isn’t really too fussed on playing with toys, but what she does love is her food & treats so gaining her trust will be a breeze!

A dog like Maggie is absolutely wasted in kennels, she’s already lived a life at home & we are so desperate to get her back into one!!

Maggie is a sweet Cockapoo who originally came to us from a breeder. She was adopted for around 16 months, but has sadly returned to us from a home following an incident with one of the smaller resident dogs in the home. During the evening, while out in the garden, Maggie was frightened by the other dog barking. Although we don't know exactly what happened, the interaction unfortunately ended in a fight and they struggled to make up or co-exist after this.

Maggie is a very shy and sensitive girl who is wary of strangers, although she does allow handling. She is trying very hard to be brave and is beginning to show small signs of progress, even getting close to taking treats from our hands, though she is not quite confident enough just yet.

Maggie is not yet confident enough to be an only dog, so we feel she would settle best in a home with one calm and confident resident dog of a similar size or larger, who can help her feel safe and reassured as she adjusts.

As Maggie has previously lived in a home, she will be familiar with the sights and sounds of a home environment. However, she may still need some support with house training as she settles into a new routine. Maggie can already walk on a lead, so she would enjoy one or two walks around the local area with the resident dog when she is settled in.

Maggie is particularly worried by men and did initially bark at the male resident in her previous home. With time, patience, and gentle handling, she slowly began to come around. Unfortunately, there was also an incident where Maggie became tangled in her harness and, in a panic, bit the hand of the male owner who was trying to help free her. Because of this, Maggie will need a calm adult-only home with patient and understanding adopters who have experience or understanding of the challenges that can come with rehoming ex-breeding dogs.

Since Maggie has been with us, she has shown that when she feels stressed or overwhelmed, she may try to find a way to escape by climbing. Because of this, she will need a very secure garden with boundaries of at least 6ft to help keep her safe and prevent any potential escape attempts.

Once Maggie knows and trusts someone, she is a very sweet and happy girl. In the right calm and understanding home, with patient and dog-savvy owners who are willing to let her settle at her own pace, we are confident she will continue to make wonderful progress and slowly come out of her shell.

Maggie is currently being treated for an ear infection in the left ear.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Max
description:
I need an active, breed experienced home that loves playtime!

I’m active and would love a large, secure garden to let off steam.

I walk on the lead but I can pull when excited.

I am house trained but I need to learn some manners.

I have been neutered and am ready for my forever home!

Max is a superstar Lurcher who has been returned to us from his adoptive family. They made the heartbreaking decision to bring him back as he was becoming dominant over the other dog in the home.

He is a very excitable, happy boy - essentially an overgrown puppy in a big body. Max is full of fun and enthusiasm and will need an active home that can meet his exercise and stimulation needs. He already knows some basic commands such as “sit”, “paw”, “lay down”, and “wait”, and he is eager to interact with his people. He is very food oriented, which makes training enjoyable and rewarding, and he already shows lovely food manners, waiting patiently when asked.

Max absolutely loves other dogs and gets incredibly excited when he sees a potential new friend. However, he is still young, full of energy, and not always aware of his size and strength. This can sometimes lead to him becoming overexcited, a little mouthy, and unintentionally overwhelming other dogs. He has been working hard on his social skills and has been socialising while wearing a muzzle for safe and positive interactions. This is purely as a precaution, and his future adopters will need to continue this training and take a responsible approach when introducing him to other dogs.

As he was too much for a more timid dog in his previous home, we feel that Max would be best suited to being homed as an only dog, provided he has plenty of appropriate socialisation with dogs of a similar size and play style. He cannot live with cats or small furries.

As Max has previously lived in a home, he is familiar with household sights and sounds and is house trained. However, he is still working on his lead manners and can pull when he gets excited. Ongoing training, structure, and consistency will be important, along with plenty of mental stimulation to keep his busy mind engaged. He would thrive in a home that can offer activities such as training games or even dog sports.

Max could share his home with older, dog-savvy teenagers aged 16 and over, who understand that he can be a bit of a bull in a china shop. Any young people in the home will need to be confident and not worried by an enthusiastic dog who may jump up while he continues to work on his manners.

Max does struggle with separation anxiety and can become destructive if left alone for long periods, so he will need a home where someone is around most of the time and who is committed to helping him gradually build confidence with being left.

Max's new home will need a large, secure garden with 6ft boundaries, where he can let off some steam.

Max will make an amazing addition to a home with experience of similar breeds. He truly is a lovely boy, bouncy, affectionate, and full of life, with so much potential. He is a big-hearted lad who gives his whole heart, and with the right guidance, he will grow into an incredible companion.

Max has recently been castrated, and while he was feeling (understandably) sorry for himself for a few days after, he was brilliant going into the vets and during his recovery. Although he has had to wear a buster collar just to stop him licking at the area, he doesn't let that bother him and is such a good boy when you take it off to take him out for a walk and pop it back on when he's back in his kennel and he has been so easy to give his pain relief medication to as well, he really has been a model patient. He is such an easy dog to handle, given his size he is no issue at all.

During his recovery period, Max has only been on short walks so that he doesn't overdo it in the play yards, but slowly this past week he has been spending some time in our agility yard to have a run and you can definitely see that he is back to his full, playful self, running around, chasing a tennis ball and being inquisitive about anything and everything.

Max is a fantastic boy, and any time I spend with him is just so enjoyable and full of love and fun, he is such a special dog, I'm constantly scratching my head wondering why and how he's still here.

Where do I start with the wonderful ball of energy that is Max.

First and foremost, the question I ask myself and almost everyone that meets Max asks too, how on earth is he still waiting?! A young, handsome, intelligent dog who is BARRELS of fun. There’s something about Max that is just so loveable and he truly does capture people’s hearts. Many of the volunteers who walk him are always so happy to see him and enjoy their time together.

Recently we’ve been working on nailing a ‘touch’ command. When Max is focused he is such a rewarding dog to train. Sometimes his desire to please takes over and he waves his paw at me until I have to accept it (and of course reward because he's the goodest boy no matter what). He is also learning to be calmer when greeting people and has even had some gentle fuss from some children too. It remains true that Max cannot be homed with children under the age of 16, but it is so important for Max to have positive interactions with respectful children to prevent any reactivity / fear from developing. It also helps teach him to be calm when meeting new people, especially when they’re smaller than him!

Max brings such a unique type of energy to the rescue, he is such a joyful boy and truly comes alive when he is with his people. I threw Max a 1st birthday party and all of his favourite people came throughout the day to play with him and bring him yummy treats, fuss and cuddles. He had the best day and it was so touching to see how loved he is despite not being in a home.

We are doing our very best to raise Max into a well rounded, well socialised and well adjusted adult dog. However, he is at such a crucial stage in his development and has already spent 5 months in kennels. It’s no place for a young dog to grow up. Nearly half of his life spent in kennels patiently waiting for his second chance to come and take him home.

Despite his size Max really is just a baby and definitely a lap dog too. So if you have a spot on the sofa you can share, Max will happily join you and be the bestest friend anyone could wish for.

Myself and Max have formed a very close bond over the last few months we’ve been working together. We take daily walks, go to the big play yard and have plenty of cuddles and fusses.I’m not sure what it is about Max that keeps getting him overlooked, it could be his size or that he is like a big playful puppy or something else, whatever it is, anyone would be lucky to have this handsome chap in their lives, he will always put a smile on your face and he has such a good sense of humour, watching him having zoomies in his kennel yard while he’s jumping off the obstacles in there then stoping then going back round again is nothing short of entertaining, or when he’s fishing treats out of the paddling pool while simultaneously blowing bubbles with his nose.Max truly deserves the world, he is such a sweet and caring boy with a big personality and so much love to give, as well as his big size there is also a big heart and all he wants is to be able to fully give it to someone and finally find his forever home.

Max is a big, happy baby with bags of energy and so much love to give. He is an excitable, affectionate boy who adores attention and loves having people around him. He is always happy to greet you and be part of whatever is going on.

As Max is still young and growing, he is slowly learning his manners and how to greet people politely without jumping. . He will need adopters who can match his energy, continue his training, and give him the stimulation, guidance, and love he needs to thrive.

Max is a gentle, overlooked soul who is learning new things every day at the rescue, but he is missing the comforts of home. He cannot wait to find a family who understands him and can help him blossom into the wonderful companion he is meant to be.With the right home, patience, and plenty of love, Max will make a loyal and joyful best friend.

Since coming back into our care, Max has been working hard on learning how to socialise with other dogs. He absolutely adores them and gets incredibly excited when he sees a potential new friend! Because he’s still young, full of beans, and a bit unaware of his own size, he can sometimes be a little too enthusiastic. This can lead to him becoming overexcited, a bit mouthy, and unintentionally overwhelming other dogs.

To help him learn safe and positive interactions, Max has been socialising while wearing a muzzle. This is purely for his safety and that of other dogs, and his future adopters will need to continue this training and take a responsible approach when introducing him to new canine companions. Aside from that, Max is everything you’d want in a young pup he's bouncy, happy, affectionate, and full of life.

He’s very food oriented, which makes training a dream! He already knows commands like “sit” and has learned great food manners where be waits patiently until he’s told he can eat. Max thrives on mental stimulation and ongoing training, and with the right guidance, he has all the potential to grow into an incredible dog. Max does struggle with separation anxiety and can become destructive if left alone for long periods. He really craves human company so he’ll need a home where someone is around most of the time and is committed to helping him build confidence being alone gradually. He’s such a loving, handsome boy who gives his whole heart, and it would be wonderful to see him back in a home environment where he can truly thrive. As a young pup, he’s missed out on some important early experiences, so a patient, committed family will make all the difference in helping him become the best version of himself.

He is a very excitable, happy boy - essentially an overgrown puppy in a big body. Max is full of fun and enthusiasm and will need an active home that can meet his exercise and stimulation needs. He already knows some basic commands such as “sit”, “paw”, “lay down”, and “wait”, and he is eager to interact with his people.

Max loves other dogs but is often unaware of his size and strength, having grown into such a big lad very quickly. As he is still just a puppy, he is still learning about manners and can be mouthy and plays in a very typical Lurcher way. In his previous home, there was an incident when he was around 3 months old, where he was a little too rough and resulted in a small dog needing veterinary treatment. He has started muzzle training for off-lead play as a precaution, and he will need a home that understands Lurcher play styles and is confident managing this appropriately. We have been socialising him with dogs of all sizes on walks and he is doing very well.

As Max has previously lived in a home, he is familiar with household sights and sounds and is house trained. However, he is still working on his lead manners and can pull when he gets excited. Ongoing training and consistency will be important.

Max will make an amazing addition to a home with experience of similar breeds. He truly is a lovely boy. He is a big-hearted, affectionate lad who is still convinced he can curl up and fit on your lap.

name: Rhea
description:
I could live with dog-savvy teens who respect my space.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training and lead walking.

I have bilateral cataracts & I will be spayed before adoption!

08-11-26 Rhea has come to us from a breeder to find her forever home. She is a worried little girl who is a little overwhelmed to find herself here at the moment. She can be quite timid when she first meets you, but after a while she does start to come out of her shell and will accept a fuss with a little waggy tail. She is also starting to become quite nosey and inquisitive, which is lovely to see.

Rhea will be looking for a loving home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and will allow her to settle in at her own pace. She currently relies on her kennel friends for comfort and reassurance, so she will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home who she can look to as she begins to find her feet. Rhea does show some signs of resource guarding around food and can grumble at other dogs, so she will need to be fed separately from any other dogs in her new home. This is specifically around sharing food with other dogs, rather than with people. Her adopters will need to be confident in managing this and helping her feel comfortable at mealtimes.

Rhea has never lived in a home before, so her adopters will need to be patient and understanding as she learns about the routines of home life, including house training and walking on a lead. Having a confident canine companion to show her the ropes will be a big help as she builds her confidence and starts to discover the world outside the rescue.

Rhea could share her home with dog-savvy teenagers aged 16 and over, who can appreciate and understand that she will need a gentle, quiet introduction to the home and her own space to settle in.

Rhea is a sweet, timid girl who will need a little extra time, kindness and reassurance to help her find her paws. With the right home and a lovely doggy friend by her side, we hope she will gradually grow in confidence and learn to enjoy all the comforts of home life.

Rhea has arrived with bilateral cataracts, which does not seem to be bothering her at this time but will need to be monitored in her future home.

Rhea has been given the Gift of Life by Rosalind Steven

name: Benji
description:
I could live with older, dog-savvy teens who respect my space.

I can be an only dog or live with other dogs. I have never met cats.

I'd like a secure garden to have fun playtimes in.

I walk on a lead and would enjoy a nice walk once a day.

I have lived in a home so I know the basics.

03-11-26 Benji is a beautiful, playful boy who originally came into our care as an unclaimed dog in 2024. He was adopted but has sadly returned to us because of illness in the family, meaning his owners were no longer able to care for him.

Benji is feeling a little out of sorts being back in kennels but is coping well. He is a super-loving boy who absolutely adores attention, cuddles and bum scratches. He has been spending lots of time in the office with us while his exercise is restricted and is always happy to soak up some fuss. He has lots of character and a wonderfully silly personality, and we know he would love nothing more than to be back in a home where he can relax on the sofa and enjoy life with his favourite people!

Benji can be a little reactive towards other dogs when out on walks, but having spent time in a home, he has made some lovely improvements. He is currently kennelled with a friend and we feel he could potentially live with another suitable dog or as an only dog. His adopters will need to be understanding of his needs and willing to continue supporting him with his training around other dogs. When Benji was initially with us, he could snap at feet when leaving his kennel, but this behaviour has improved massively since his time in a home. He is generally much better around doorways, although he can still become uncomfortable if someone lingers in a doorway or enters without greeting him, so his adopters will need to be mindful of this.

Having lived in a home before, Benji is familiar with the sights and sounds of everyday life and will hopefully settle back into a home routine with a little time. He needs a calm home with adopters who understand his breed and can give him the consistency and reassurance he needs. He can live with teenagers aged 16 and over who understand his needs and will respect his space.

Benji was castrated and had nasal wedge surgery in 2024. He can still experience episodes of being sick, particularly following exercise, excitement or periods of stress. He is currently being trialled on a course of medication to see whether this helps manage his symptoms, but he may require further investigation and potentially additional surgery to address his breathing, such as BOAS surgery, in the future. His exercise and activity levels are currently being managed, so he will need adopters who are happy to accommodate his reduced exercise needs and understand that he may require further veterinary treatment and monitoring as needed.

Benji really is a lovely little man who is full of character and has so much love to give. He is a typical silly Frenchie who is desperate to get back to being the couch potato he deserves to be! With a calm home, understanding adopters and plenty of cuddles, we know he will be so happy to have a sofa to call his own again.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Rizzle
description:
I need a calm and quiet home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

I have been spayed & am ready for my forever home!

Rizzle is a quiet and timid girl who has come to us from a breeder. When she arrived she was quite overwhelmed and in need of plenty of TLC, but she has since started to come out of her shell.

Rizzle has recently moved to a wonderful foster home where she is settling in and starting to learn about home life for the first time ever. She is making gentle progress and is even starting to wag her tail when her fosterer speaks to her and has ventured onto the sofa twice so far, although she is understandably still quite nervous and isn't yet feeling brave enough to approach but is trying her hardest to be brave.

She will be looking for a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and who will allow her to settle in at her own pace. She will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home who she can look to and lean on as she begins to gain confidence and learns that the world isn’t such a scary place.

She has never lived in a home before moving to foster, so her adopters will need to be kind and patient as she learns all about home life, including house training, though she is starting to get to grips with this already. She doesn't yet walk on a lead and harness as she is quite worried about being handled, but hopefully this will be introduced to her in the near future.

She is a sweet little lady with so much potential and just needs someone willing to take a chance on her. With a loving home, a confident canine companion and plenty of patience, we’re sure Rizzle will slowly find her confidence and become a wonderful companion.

Rizzle has been given the Gift of Life by Carolina Olsen

Rizzle is a real sweetheart, but still very nervous, moving away from me most of the time. She has just started to wag her tail when I talk to her and has twice shared the sofa, but at a distance. If she moves into a corner, I can give her a brief stroke, otherwise she will only come for a quick sniff of my hand. She is not yet confident enough to take a treat from me. She eats well, preferring to eat alone, but not because of any guarding issues.

Rizzle has chewed toys and played with Petal, my other foster dog, but this is not a regular occurrence. She spends a lot of time alongside Petal. She is getting used to household sounds, dislikes the vacuum cleaner and goes in the garden but is OK with the washing machine, and tolerates the ironing board.

Rizzle will briefly bark if she hears a sound in the garden, eg another dog or voices. At night or if I go out, she sleeps quietly in the lounge with the other dogs. She doesn't enjoy handling at the moment, so I have not made any attempt to put a harness on her. Her toilet training is a work in progress, being clean when the back door is open.

Rizzle is a quiet and timid girl who has come to us from a breeder. She is beginning to show us just how inquisitive she can be and is trying her hardest to be brave. Rizzle isn’t quite ready to approach us just yet, but she does follow the lead of her doggy friends and takes lots of comfort from having them around. With plenty of TLC, patience and reassurance, we’re sure it shouldn’t take her too long to come around and start showing her lovely personality.

Rizzle will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home who she can look to and lean on as she begins to gain confidence and learns that the world isn’t such a scary place. She has never lived in a home before, so her adopters will need to be kind and patient as she learns all about home life, including house training. She will need time to take everything at her own pace and shouldn’t be rushed before she is ready.

Rizzle can live with older, dog-savvy children who are sensible and will understand that she needs time and space to settle in. She is a sweet little lady with so much potential and just needs someone willing to take a chance on her. With a loving home, a confident canine companion and plenty of patience, we’re sure Rizzle will slowly find her confidence and become a wonderful companion.

name: Hazel
description:
I would like a home filled with love and kindness!

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I will be spayed before going to my forever home!

07-11-26 Hazel is a sweet lady who has come to us from a breeder to find her forever home. She is quite timid at the moment, but will gently approach you and give your hands a little sniff and once you spend some time with her she starts to come out of her shell and has a waggy little tail and is happy to have some fuss and attention and even enjoys being picked up.

Hazel will need a kind and patient home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and who will allow her to settle in at her own pace. We would consider homing her with gentle, dog savvy children aged 9+.

Hazel relies on other dogs for comfort and reassurance and will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home who she can look to for comfort and reassurance as she continues to build her confidence and learns about the world around her. Hazel has never lived in a home before, so her adopters will need to be understanding as she learns about all the new experiences that come with home life, including house training and walking on a lead. She may need a little extra time and encouragement before feeling brave enough to venture out and explore, so allowing her to take things at her own pace will be really important.

Hazel is a lovely girl who just needs someone willing to give her the patience, kindness and love she needs to find her paws. We think she has so much potential and hope she will blossom with the right family!

Hazel has been given the Gift of Life by Marie Bradshaw

name: Lizzy
description:
I would like a home filled with love and kindness!

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training and lead walking.

I am overweight and will benefit from a healthy diet. I am spayed.

08-11-26 Lizzy is a sweet lady who has come to us from a breeder and is a typical aloof Corgi! She is quite happy spending most of her time curled up in her bed and would love a cosy bed of her own to snuggle into in her new home.

Lizzy isn't quite confident enough to approach people just yet, but we think that with time, patience and a gentle approach, she will slowly begin to come out of her shell. She would be well suited to a home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and in the right circumstances we would consider homing her with gentle, dog savvy children aged 9+. She will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home who she can look to for reassurance as she continues to build her confidence and learn about the world around her.

Lizzy has never lived in a home before, so her adopters will need to be understanding as she learns all about things like house training and walking on a lead. She may need a little extra time before feeling brave enough to venture out and explore, so a gentle introduction to new experiences will be important.

Lizzy is a lovely, sweet-natured lady who just needs someone to give her the time and encouragement to find her paws in this big new world. We think she has so much potential and will blossom with the right family!

Lizzy has arrived overweight and will benefit from a healthy diet.

Lizzy has been given the Gift of Life by Lyn Lang
