name: Sixpence
description:
I will need an adult only home, that will let me settle in at my own pace.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I can be a little nervous, and will need a secure garden to learn about the outdoors.

I have never been on walks, but may be too scared and will need some time.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have been spayed & am ready for my forever home!

Sixpence is a nervous girl who has come to us from a breeder. She isn’t brave enough to approach you just yet, but she is easy to handle once she is in your arms. We have now learnt that she is trying so hard to be brave and, although she is still quite nervous, we are seeing little bits of her cheeky Daxi personality coming through every day.

Sixpence seems to have had very little positive touch or affection before coming to us. She has recently moved in to foster and is happy to take treats from her foster parents but is not quite sure about being stroked yet. She will allow them to put her harness on as long as she is in a quiet corner and things are taken slowly. You can tell she isn't entirely comfortable, but she trusts us enough to allow it and is always very happy to enjoy a little cheese reward afterwards! With continued positive reinforcement, we are confident that this will improve as Sixpence learns that good things can come from new experiences.

Sixpencerelies heavily on other dogs and really enjoys being around her resident dog friends. She watches what they do and follows their lead for confidence, and she has even learnt from them how to use the dog steps to get onto the sofa and watch the world go by from the front window! She will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home that she can lean on as she continues to find her confidence and learn about home life.

Penny is also discovering all sorts of things that she enjoys. She loves sunbathing, having the freedom to explore a secure dog field, stuffed teddies and, of course, cheese! She has a crate set up with a fluffy bed where she can go when she wants some quiet time to herself, and she seems to really enjoy having this safe space available to her.

Sixpence will need a calm and quiet home with adopters who have breed experience and understand that she will need plenty of time, patience and encouragement as she settles in. Her ideal home would have one or more small, friendly dog companions who can help her feel secure. We feel that children would be too overwhelming for Penny, so she will need an adult-only home.

Penny has never lived in a home before, so her adopters will need to be kind and patient as she continues to learn about home life, including house training. She will also need to continue her harness and lead training at her own pace, as these are still very new experiences for her.

Sixpence is a very sweet little girl who is trying her very best to be brave. She has already made some lovely progress in the short time she has been with us, and we can't wait to see just how much more of her personality comes out as her confidence grows. She just needs someone willing to give her the time, space and love she needs to discover how wonderful her new life can be.

Sixpence has been given the Gift of Life by Sarah Maddox, on behalf of Jesus Christ

We have had Sixpence or 'Penny' as she is known here for a little over a week. it is clear that she has had very little positive touch or affection before and she is trying desperately to be brave!

Although she is still quite nervous were are noticing her trying or learning something new everyday and her cheeky little Daxi personality is starting to shine. She has discovered a love for sunbathing, the freedom of a secure dog field, stuffed teddies and cheese!

Penny is happy to take treats from us but isn't currently sure on being stroked. We can put a harness on her as long as we find a quiet corner and go slow. you can tell she isn't entirely comfortable but let's us do it and enjoys her cheese reward afterwards. We have every confidence that this will improve with more positive reinforcement and learning just how amazing walks are.

She really enjoys being around her resident dog friends and follows what they do for confidence. She's even learnt from them how to get up onto the sofas with the dog steps and watch the world go by out of the front window. We have a crate set up in our dining room with a fluffy bed in for when she wants some time to herself which she likes.

Penny's ideal home would be a quiet one with one or more small dog friends and owners that are willing to give this girl the time and space she needs to learn her new life at her own pace. Sadly we think she would find children too overwhelming. We can't wait to see her confidence grow in her new life.

Sixpence is a nervous girl who has come to us from a breeder. She isn’t brave enough to approach you just yet, but she is easy to handle once she is in your arms. She will need time, patience and plenty of trust-building before she feels confident enough to come out of her shell.

Sixpence relies heavily on other dogs and will follow their lead, so she will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home that she can lean on as she learns about home life and finds her paws. She will need a calm and quiet home, with adopters who have breed experience and can understand her needs.

Sixpence has never lived in a home before, so her adopters will need to be kind and patient as she learns about house training. She is working with her kennel mummy on harness training and would like to continue this in her new home. She can live with sensible, dog-savvy teens aged 13+ who will give her the time and space she needs. Sixpence is a very sweet girl who just needs someone willing to give her the chance to blossom.

name: Faith
description:
I will need an adult-only home that understands I need time to settle in.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I will need a large, extra-secure garden to keep me safe as I learn about the home.

I’m new to walking on a harness and doing well!

Please be patient with me, I haven’t lived in a home before.

I've started my vaccinations and will be spayed before adoption.

Faith is a beautiful girl who came to us from a breeder and was initially incredibly shut down and terrified of people. She would run away from any human interaction and wouldn't even eat when people were around. However, over the last two months, Faith has made some wonderful progress and is slowly learning that people can be kind. She now walks on a harness, although she can still be easily spooked, and is happiest walking with people she knows and trusts. She will now take treats from us in her kennel, and sometimes on walks when things are quiet, with hot dogs being a particular favourite! Recently, she even allowed a little gentle fuss in the big play yard, choosing to stay for affection rather than run away. This may seem like a small step, but for Faith, it is a huge achievement.

Faith absolutely adores other dogs and truly comes alive when joining her friends for playtime in our big yard. She approaches them with a full-body wiggle and has even discovered how much fun toys can be, although she cannot be left unsupervised with soft toys! She will need a kind and confident resident dog in her new home to help her continue building her confidence and show her the ropes of home life. As a Collie, she will also need plenty of enrichment and exercise to keep her busy once she has settled in.

Faith is still a very nervous girl who will need an adult-only home with Collie experience, where her progress will be celebrated and she can continue learning at her own pace. She has never lived in a home before, so she will need patient adopters who can help her with house training, lead walking and all the other new experiences that come with family life. She will also need an extra-secure garden of at least 6ft to keep her safe as she settles in.

Faith really is such a sweet girl who tries her very hardest to be brave. Although she is making lovely progress with us, kennels is no place for a puppy to spend these important months of her life. Her three Collie friends who arrived with her have all found their forever homes, and now it is Faith's turn to find someone who can see just how far she has come and how much potential she has. With time, patience and lots of love, we know this special girl has so much more to discover, and we desperately hope her forever family won't keep her waiting much longer.

Faith has been given the Gift of Life by Raychel Mount

name: Tippins
description:
I would like a calm and quiet home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I will need another dog my size or larger in my new home.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I walk on lead but I can be spooked. Let's take it slow!

I have spent some time in a home, but still have lots to learn.

Tippins is a lovely lady who has come into our care from a breeder. She can be apprehensive when meeting new people and may bark at strangers, but once she feels comfortable, her wonderful personality shines through. She has formed lovely bonds with staff at the rescue and, once attached to someone, she adores cuddles and wants to be as close to her favourite people as possible. She is a ridiculously affectionate girl who gives her whole heart to those she trusts.

Tippins was briefly adopted as an only but has sadly returned to our care as she really struggled without another dog by her side. Although she didn't appear to rely on other dogs for comfort in kennels, she became very shut down in the home and struggled to come out of her shell. We therefore feel she will need a calm and confident resident dog, her size or larger, to act as a role model and help her settle. She isn't particularly cuddly with other dogs, but she shares her kennel well and we believe having another dog around will help her feel more secure while she adjusts to her new surroundings.

Tippins walks beautifully on her harness alongside her handler, although busy places and traffic can still make her nervous. Her new family should continue her confidence-building with quiet walks and plenty of reassurance.

Although she has spent some time in a home, Tippins had never experienced home life before her adoption and so her adopters will need to be kind and understanding as she learns all about home life and house training. She will need a quiet home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and understand that settling into a home may take her some time. Once she feels secure, she will try her very best to be brave and become a devoted companion.

Tippins can live with teenagers aged 16 and over who are sensible and able to respect her need for a gentle introduction. Her adopters should also be prepared to welcome her onto the furniture, as we suspect this affectionate girl will thoroughly enjoy being close to her people once she feels safe.

Tippins has returned to us with an ear infection and is currently receiving treatment. Our vets are monitoring her ears and will continue to provide any treatment she needs. She will need her ears to be monitored and cared for in her new home as appropriate.

Tippins is a very special little lady who has made fantastic progress with us. With the right canine role model, an experienced and peaceful home, and the time she needs to settle, we hope she will finally discover just how wonderful life can be.

Tippins has been with me for about a month now, and I have really, REALLY fallen for her. Even though she presents as a nervous girl and will bark at strangers, it doesn’t take her long to let her guard down at all. When she does, she is your best friend, your shadow, your snuggle buddy... and you are her whole world. She absolutely adores the people she loves and really gives her whole heart to us. She is ridiculously affectionate, and I fear she’s so wasted being in kennels.

Tippins walks beautifully on a harness right by my side and looks up at me to check in constantly. She can still be nervous in busy places and around traffic, but that is something that she’ll get used to in time. I would recommend her adopters do some practice in the garden first before they venture out, and definitely establish a bond with her first.

Even though Tippins has never been in a home before, I’m pretty certain she’s going to want to join everyone on the furniture for snuggles, so this must be welcomed with open arms. Every day with me, she jumps up onto the bench next to me in the play yard, and she loves it when I sit in her bed in her kennel with her. So she’s a cuddler for sure!!

Please don’t keep this very special girl waiting for too much longer. She deserves to be loved and in a home so much.

Tippins is a lovely lady who has come into our care from a breeder. She is a little apprehensive when she first meets new people, but she is already showing signs that her confidence is growing. Once she knows you, she enjoys a fuss and is happy to be handled. Tippins has a big personality and is a fun girl to spend time with.At the moment, Tippins is feeling a little less brave and is finding comfort in the company of her kennel friends. We feel it would be best for her to be rehomed with at least one other confident resident dog for support and companionship. She has always lived with bigger dogs and seems happiest around them. Tippins can be a little bossy with less confident dogs, so she wouldn't be suitable to live with smaller or younger dogs. We will continue to assess her confidence while she is with us to see if she could adapt to being an only dog. She will need adopters with ex-breeding experience that can understand her needs.As Tippins has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training and the other basics of home life. Her new family will need to be patient while she settles in and learns what home life is all about. She can live with older, dog-savvy teens, aged 16+ that can allow her time to settle into a calm environment.Tippins already walks on a lead, but doesn't seem to be overly confident on this so she will need continued support as she learns, and once she has settled into her new home, she would enjoy one or two walks around the local area with her resident dog so that she can continue lead training.Tippins is a lovely girl with lots of character. She's already showing us what a sweet dog she is, and we hope that, with time and patience, she'll continue to grow in confidence and enjoy everything home life has to offer.Tippins is now receiving regular cleanings from the vets for waxy ears and this will need to be monitored in her new home.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Nora
description:
I need a calm and quiet home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I’m new to walking on a harness and doing well!

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

Nora is a gentle girl who has come to us from a breeder and is now in foster, where she has been able to experience life in a home for the first time. She has been in foster for over a month now, and this has given us a much better understanding of her mobility, as well as allowing her confidence to grow and her lovely personality to shine through.

Nora is still very mistrustful of people, but she is beginning to show us that she really does want to make friends. She is now much more willing to approach her fosterer and has recently started coming over to take treats from her. She will even jump up onto the sofa to watch Netflix, as long as there is another dog already on the sofa with her! These may seem like small things, but for Nora they are huge steps forward and show just how much she is beginning to relax. She will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her home that will allow her to lean on them as she continues to settle.

She absolutely loves the comforts of home life and takes great reassurance from having other dogs around her. She has also been on a few short walks outside the home, allowing her to slowly experience the world beyond her garden. She is still a very sensitive girl and everything will need to be introduced gradually, but she is making lovely progress.

Nora's mobility has also improved in a home setting. Her ataxia appears to be closely linked to her stress levels and is much more noticeable when she is worried or overwhelmed. When she is relaxed, her movements are almost normal, which is incredibly encouraging. She is not currently on any medication, and her fosterer is helping her to build muscle strength through daily massage and gentle exercise.

Nora will need a quiet and understanding home with adopters who have experience with nervous dogs and, ideally, ex-breeders. She will need at least one calm, friendly resident dog to give her confidence and show her the way. Her new family will need to be incredibly patient and allow her to settle and build trust at her own pace, without expecting too much too soon.

Nora has had lots of hardships in her life and is still learning that she can feel safe around people. However, the progress she has made since moving into foster has been wonderful to see. Beneath her worries is a very sweet girl who is slowly discovering how lovely life can be, and we are hoping that the right home will give her the security, patience and love she needs to continue blossoming.

Nora has been given the Gift of Life by Judie Fisher

Nora has been in foster for over a month now which allowed us to have a good assessment of her mobility, and also helped increase her confidence and introduce her to living in a home. This gentle girl has a very sweet personality and loves the comforts of home life and the company of other dogs. She is still very mistrustful of humans, but I can see that she is now more willing to try and be friends. She has recently started coming up to take a treat from me, and will even jump up on the sofa to watch Netflix with me (as long as there is another dog on the sofa too). She has also been on a few short walks outside to see the world beyond my home and garden!

Nora's ataxia has improved in a home setting too, largely because it is connected to her mental state and seems to be worse when she is stressed. When Nora is relaxed, her movements are almost normal, which is lovely to see and gives me hope that once she feels safe and comfortable mentally, she will have a great quality of life. We just need to help her get there. Nora is not on any medication at the moment, but I massage her daily and we are working on building her muscle strength.

Nora's ideal home will be a quiet setting with one or more calm and friendly dogs. Her people will need to be kind and very patient, with experience of scared dogs and preferably beagles too. This gorgeous girl has had lots of hardships in her life, it is time for her to finally have a place where she feels safe and loved.

I have been working with Nora a few days a week since she first arrived with us and was on medication and crate rest for her legs. Around two weeks ago, Nora moved to a different section, so I haven't seen her in a little while. I popped over today to check in and chat to one of her new kennel dads to see how she's doing.

Since arriving on her new section, Nora has made huge leaps! She is now harness-trained and wears her harness comfortably during the day. She has grown more confident with handling and with walking on her harness to and from the yard, though she is not yet feeling up to walks outside the centre. She also now sits curiously at the front of her kennel, watching people and dogs come and go on her section, rather than hiding in the back.

Nora still has a long way to go in learning to trust humans and receive our love, but she's made huge steps already. It's a great reminder that all of us working here have different skills, and sometimes a dog who is struggling just needs a change of scene to take the next steps in their journey towards their forever home.

Nora is so gentle and if you ignore the deep defensive howl (she is a beagle after all!) eventually she quietens down and she shows her soft side.Nora is still trying to get used to enjoying human company. She is not there yet but is slowly beginning to show signs of trusting people and does settle near you with a little patience.

It appears to me that it's not that Nora dislikes people, it's more a matter of how she is unsure of who we are and how we do things.

Once she  settles and it does take a little time, although still afraid, is much more willing to be approached by people.

In this calmer state, I was able to smooth her coat all over and gently stroke her without her worrying too much which is a positive step for her.

Nora will need this gentle approach for some time but the reward will be endless love and loyalty which is priceless.

I believe all Nora needs right now is the stability and security that a loving home can offer.Nora does much prefer the company of dogs  at the moment so it is a must that there is a resident dog already in the home for her to be with.

Nora has kennelled with small dogs but we do feel she would be better placed with a dog of a similar size or larger.

Our next step whilst Nora is with us will be to train her to walk on a harness so she can start to discover and enjoy the outside world.

Nora has come to us from a breeder and is now looking for a very special forever home. She is a scared girl who is understandably feeling overwhelmed to find herself here and is desperately in need of kindness, patience and TLC as she begins to settle and learn that the world can be a safe place.

When Nora first arrived with us, she was showing some neurological symptoms and ataxia, and her back legs would occasionally slide from underneath her, causing her to stumble. Following investigations with our vets, it was found that her proprioception was delayed in all four limbs. She was trialed on a course of medication alongside crate rest and has made wonderful progress. Her proprioception is now normal, she is able to get around and play happily, and she enjoys life much more comfortably. She does still have a slight amount of ataxia and can occasionally limp still. Our vet feels that she may have suffered an acute injury at some point in the past which has largely resolved itself, though she will likely never present like a normal dog.

Nora will be looking for adopters who will love and cherish her just as she is. Due to her mobility history, she will need a home without slippery flooring, or one where plenty of rugs and runners are in place to help her move around confidently and safely.

She would be best suited to a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience of nervous ex-breeding dogs and understand her worries. Nora will need time to settle at her own pace and will thrive with patient adopters who are happy to let her progress in her own time. She takes great comfort from the company of other dogs and will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home to show her the way and help her build confidence.

Nora has never experienced life in a home before so her new family will need to be understanding as she learns all about home life and new skills like house training. She doesn't yet walk on a lead and harness and initially she will need to practise wearing her harness and exploring safely within the home and garden before she is ready to venture further afield.

Although Nora is still very worried and unsure of the world around her, beneath her fears is a sweet and deserving little girl who simply needs someone to believe in her. Watching a scared dog slowly learn to trust is one of the most rewarding experiences, and with love, patience and understanding, Nora will blossom. The day she greets you with a wagging tail and a sparkle in her eyes will make every moment of that journey worthwhile.

name: Royal
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I would like to live with a female dog. No cats please!

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I can walk on a lead and harness and love to explore quiet areas.

I am learning about house training in my foster home, and am doing so good!

Royal is a very special Chow Chow who has come to us from a breeder in search of his forever home. When he first arrived, he was extremely frightened of the world around him and was very wary of being touched or handled. Thanks to gentle care and patience, Royal has made incredible progress and is continuing to blossom in foster, where he is experiencing home life for the very first time.

Royal has exceeded all expectations with how well he has settled into foster. He has been an absolute superstar, sleeping soundly through the night, travelling well in the car, walking beautifully on lead and has even been completely clean in the house. Every day brings a new milestone, and it has been a joy to watch his confidence grow as he discovers all the comforts and pleasures of family life.

Although Royal is still nervous of people initially, he so desperately wants to trust and tries his hardest to be brave. He has begun asking his foster carers for gentle neck and bum scratches, happily takes treats from their hands, enjoys rummaging through the toy box, has found his little voice and now greets them with his wonderful wagging tail. He is such a sweet, gentle soul who simply needs time to work things out at his own pace.

Royal absolutely relies on the resident female dogs in foster for confidence and reassurance. He watches their every move, learning how to be part of a family, and loves playing alongside them. He will need to share his forever home with at least one kind, confident female dog who enjoys a good play and can continue to show him the way. He cannot live with cats.

As this is Royal's first experience of living in a home, he thrives on routine and will need patient, understanding adopters who will allow him to settle without pressure. He has made remarkable progress already, but he is still very nervous of the unknown and benefits from people who understand that he needs time to process new experiences. A calm, rural or quiet home would suit him best, as he is currently worried by traffic. He is looking for an adult-only home with breed experience and experience with very nervous rescue dogs would be highly beneficial.

Royal has recently had a bath and full groom at the rescue and was an absolute gentleman throughout. As a Chow Chow, his beautiful coat will require regular daily grooming. He is very tolerant of being brushed when it is introduced slowly, little and often, and this has become an important part of his routine.

Royal is an incredibly special boy who has embraced this new chapter in his life with quiet bravery. With patience, kindness and the continued support of confident canine companions, he will become a wonderfully loyal and loving companion. Watching him continue to discover the world and grow in confidence will be an incredibly rewarding journey, and he is sure to make his forever family smile every single day.

Royal is currently being treated for an ear infection.

Wow! This darling boy has just exceeded all expectations with how well he’s settled into his very first home, in his first week. Not a single accident (unheard of for a boy), sleeps soundly over night out of a crate, happy to be left alone with the company of the resident dogs, walks well on a lead, travels well. A literal angel boy.

Royal is the sweetest soul, he doesn’t trust humans easily but he really wants to and tries so hard to be brave.

He relies heavily on our resident girl gang for confidence & reassurance, watching & copying them intently to learn what being a member of a family is all about.

After an initial overwhelming few days for him, every day now brings a new ‘first’ & burst of joy on our part! Asking for a neck / bum scratch, taking a treat from our hand, rummaging in the toy box, playing with the girls, finding his little voice & wagging his amazing tail when we talk to him. He is just loving this next step in life and is so ready to be someone’s special boy.

Royal currently needs an adult only home as has not yet been tested with children. He needs confident kind resident female dogs who like a good play. A rural / quiet location would be preferable as he’s currently quite scared of traffic.

He is still very nervous of the unknown, thrives on routine and needs to be guided and given time to work things out without any pressure so experience with very scared dogs would be helpful.

As a Chow, his beautiful coat will need grooming daily. He is very tolerant of this if done slowly, little & often.

Please get in touch if you feel you might be the right match for this special big guy, he will make you smile every day.

Royal is not a dog I’ve had the chance to work with until recently. I’ve heard a lot about him, as he’s one of our longer stayers. I had heard many great things from other members of staff, including the incredible progress he’s made since joining us!When I did get the chance to work with him, my first impression was “oh my days, you are beautiful!” On first sight, he is one of the most beautiful dogs I’ve ever seen and certainly the most stunning chow I’ve ever seen! How can you look at this handsome boy and not fall in love?!When I actually began working with him, I realised how shy and timid he actually was. Initially, he wouldn’t come to the front of the kennel to see me, he’d hide away in the back. It was evident to me that this boy did not trust me. As I continued to work with him, I was very aware of my actions, to ensure I wasn’t causing any anxiety. I began with treats (who doesn’t love a cheeky bribe?). It slowly worked. Initially, he wanted nothing to do with me. I didn’t want to invade his safe spaces (safe spaces are so important for a more scared or anxious dog. Could you imagine a big scary stranger coming into your home and not leaving? I wouldn’t feel too easy if that occurred to me). So, I’d place the treat and leave the kennel. He’d come out, have a little nosey and take the treat. With time, he began slowly coming out of the back as I entered his kennel. He then began taking treats from my hands and now, whenever I walk onto the section, he comes straight to the gate and waits for me. Honestly, such an incredible feeling making a bond like this with such an incredible boy! There is honestly no feeling like it. They say a dog is a humans best friend but, what no one tells you it works both ways. To build that bond, teach him that I’m not scary, I’m here to help him feel safe, comfortable, happy and to get such a response… it’s honestly the best feeling in the world. Royal needs a home, he needs people to show him this on a day to day basis. We do what we can but, we can’t teach him the safety and comfort of a home, of a family that’s there for him 24/7.Once I got to know this guy a little more, I was taken away. We go out on walks. I feel like this was another bonding experience for us. He loves a walk but, loud noises and interactions with loud people/dogs do freak him out, thus we try to go for quieter walks. He also loves frolicking in the yard. From my experience, he seems to just love being outside!When I worked with him, he didn’t have a friend in his kennel, however, since working with him I have seen him enjoying in the yard with other dogs and is now kennelled with a boxer. He seems very happy. As previously mentioned on his profile, he is to be homed with females around his size or alone. I have not worked with him enough to comment further on his compatibility and amiability with other dogs so, please read the rest of his profile and updates to get a fuller understanding of this incredible boy!At this point, I’ve worked with him enough for him to trust me. He’s happy to see me, he’s fine for me to touch him and fuss him. The Royal I see is a happy dude. He is a scared dog, I’m very aware of that but, the Royal I know now is far different to the Royal I first met. You just have to gain his trust and he’ll let you see him. When you first meet him, he will be shy. He’ll hide and he will not trust you. DO NOT let this deter you. He is one of the sweetest dogs I’ve ever met. From when I first met him to now, I feel like he’s a completely different dog. I was respectful of his boundaries, slow and calm, I did what I could to make him feel comfortable and safe, he then began to trust me and show me his true self (he hides it beneath all that fur). Honestly, I love him. I will take time out of my day to go see him, give him a little treat and some love, just because he is honestly that special. I cannot believe he’s been here over a year. He is one of our most special dogs. I don’t see how anyone can get to know this dog and not love him.Don’t overlook this fluffy dude. Yes, he’s shy and nervous but, the longer you spend with him, care for him and gain his trust, the more you’ll fall in love with him. I can say with confidence; if you put the effort in with Royal, you will fall in love with him.

I absolutely love this boy with my whole heart.

I've been working hard on helping him get used to being brushed because, as a Chow, it's something his future adopters will need to keep up with regularly to keep his coat healthy and prevent mats from developing, especially behind his ears.

Royal is now an absolute angel when it comes to grooming. I brush him every day, and with it being shedding season, no matter how long I brush for, there always seems to be more fur coming out! These days, he simply finds a comfy spot, settles down, and lets me get on with it. If he's had enough, or if I come across a mat that's uncomfortable for him, he communicates so well to let me know he's done for the day.

I also recently decided it was time to give him a bath. I wasn't sure how he'd cope, as it involved picking him up and putting him in the bath, but he was an absolute angel from start to finish. He allowed me to pick him up without any fuss and stood beautifully while I bathed and shampooed him.

I'm so incredibly proud of him. Afterwards, I introduced him to the grooming blower to help remove some of his loose coat. He wasn't a huge fan of it, but he tolerated it for a short while, and I'll continue using it regularly so he can build his confidence with it.

I honestly think all this grooming time has strengthened our bond even more, because lately he seems to be seeking out so much more affection and attention from me. He's such a special boy, and it has been wonderful watching his confidence grow.

Royal has now been with us for over a year, and we’re still waiting for the right person to see just how special he is. He’s had two meet and greets during this time, but sadly neither worked out as he was too nervous meeting new families.

Royal is a sensitive boy who simply needs time, patience, and understanding. He can be unsure at first, but once he begins to trust you, his cheeky, affectionate personality really shines through and it’s such a joy to see.

With a consistent routine, Royal truly thrives. He now enjoys running freely around our large yard without a harness or lead, and when it’s time to go back, he comes straight over. He’s also been out on two longer walks away from the rescue with one of our regular volunteers and has done amazingly well.

All Royal is looking for is someone willing to give him the time and patience he deserves. In return, he’ll become a loyal and loving companion.

I’ve come on leaps and bounds over the past month. I’m still a little shy and can get nervous when I meet new people, but I’m working on it!

I feel most comfortable when I spend quality time with people. It doesn’t take long for me to start feeling at ease (though I still sometimes like my own space). The more time you spend with me, the more comfortable I become—and treats help too! I’ll return your love in equal measure, as long as I’m given the right time, support, and respect.

I love going out for walks, though I can get nervous around loud noises or sudden movements. They might make me jump or feel uneasy, but a bit of love and reassurance always helps!

I feel more comfortable every day. I benefit not only from interaction with my humans, but also from the company of my kennel friends that I live with.

Another month has gone by, and my cheeky boy Royal is still waiting in kennels. I honestly don’t know why this handsome lad isn’t getting much interest. Not only is he completely unique-looking, but he also has the funniest, quirkiest personality. If you want a dog who’ll make you laugh every single day here he is!

Royal is 99% kennel clean and always keeps his bedding tidy… well, until I make his bed perfectly for him. Then he likes to “show me how it’s supposed to be done” by pulling it all across the floor. He walks beautifully on the lead now; he can still get a little spooked from time to time, but he’s made massive progress since the day he arrived.

He loves his toys he just doesn’t love sharing them! He’s also a bit selective with kennel mates, so his ideal home would include a calm, placid large female dog who won’t make too much fuss over him.

Royal truly is an amazing boy, inside and out, and I hope he doesn’t have to wait much longer for the forever home he deserves.

Royal never fails to make us smile with his crazy, funny, and quirky personality. He’s got such a cheeky side to him just waiting for the right people to help it shine.

On the lead, Royal is already walking beautifully, though he can still get a little nervous at times. His new family will need to be patient and willing to help him build confidence. Loud noises or sudden movements can overwhelm him, so he’ll do best with calm, quiet walks to start.

This week Royal had his very first trip down to the big yard! He loved it, though he found his confidence by sticking close to his doggy friend. With more practice, we’re sure he’ll begin to explore on his own.

Royal absolutely adores other dogs. Once he’s settled in, he loves to play, so he’ll need a kind and confident resident dog to show him the ropes, give him reassurance, and of course, enjoy plenty of playtime together.

He’s such a handsome boy with so much love to give we can’t believe he hasn’t found his forever home yet!

This past month has been a huge step forward for our boy Royal! Once a little unsure of the world, Royal is now walking beautifully on lead, it’s such a massive step for him considering how nervous he once was!

Royal currently shares his kennel with both a male and a female dog and he’s proving to be a respectful and easy companion. He enjoys their company, often watching what they do and following their lead. Royal will definitely need another resident dog around his size in his home, so he can continue to have the doggy companionship to help him continue to grow in confidence.

Despite his progress, Royal is still a sensitive soul, and it takes a little time for him to warm up to you. Royals forever family will need to give him time and patience to come out of his shell, so for this reason I believe Royal would be best suited to a home with no children.

Please don’t leave Royal waiting much longer for his forever home, he really deserves a cosy sofa to curl up on!

I’m so proud of Royal, this boy has come on tremendously since arriving at Many Tears. From arriving a terrified dog and very unsure of us humans, he has now slowly but surely begun to trust us and realise we are not so bad, especially when we arrive with cheesy treats.

Royal loves food, toys and being outside in our yards. He has just began harness training, ready to begin lead walking. At the moment he is not so keen on lead walking but he has taken a few tentative steps and with the help of some squeezy cheese and possibly a confident doggie friend to follow I think it won’t be long before he can begin to enjoy exploring the world.

Royals adopters will need to understand he is still very wary and unsure of his environment and he is going to need plenty of time, love and patience to trust his humans, but in the right home and given time I think this boy is going to be a big, playful and lovable boy. Royal will need a home where there is already a resident dog.

Royal is a very scared boy who has come to us from a breeder. He is especially scared when it comes to being touched by us humans but when you get him in the back of the kennel he will allow you to gently stroke him but he is uncomfortable with this. At the moment Royal could possibly make the wrong decision if handled incorrectly but this is purely through fear and he is already starting to make improvements. He will actually get excited to see his kennel mum in the mornings and will wag his tail but he’s not sure how to interact with her yet.

Royal has never lived in a home so this is going to be completely overwhelming at first and he will definitely need at least one other dog in the home to help his confidence. This will help him with house training and lead walking but these are things that are going to take him time to learn as the garden may be as scary as the home at first.

Royal will need a very calm and quiet, adult only home and adopters who have lots of experience with scared dogs. We think he’ll come out of his shell a lot more over time but Royal needs a lot of TLC, time and patience.

These wonderful souls may be older, have medical needs, or come with a few unique quirks—but they have endless love to give. Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Gabriel
description:
I need an adult-only experienced home that understands me.

I would need to be the only animal in the home.

I may be shy now, but once I have settled I would love a nice garden I can play in!

I love going for walks, and would love an active home!

I know some tricks & walk well on the lead but will need help with housetraining.

I have been neutered and am ready to find my forever home.

Gabriel originally came to us from a breeder, and for him the world felt like a very frightening place. He was worried of people, and new environments and unfamiliar experiences left him feeling overwhelmed. Even something as simple as having a lead put on was a huge challenge. He needed time, patience and gentle encouragement to begin to feel safe.

Gabriel was adopted for a short period, but unfortunately it was not the right fit for him. He was returned after displaying unwanted behaviours in the home and making the wrong choices when he felt uncomfortable in a situation, which did result in Gabriel biting. He will need a quiet, adult-only home without resident or visiting children. Gabriel can struggle with visitors coming to the house, so he will need a home without too many visitors and where he can be placed in a separate room when people do come over. His adopters will also need to be willing to meet him multiple times before adoption so that he has the opportunity to develop a bond and build trust with them.

Gabriel is a very sensitive boy who feels anxious about a lot of things. During his time here we are trying to help him feel more comfortable by giving him the tools to know how to be more relaxed in these scary situations. To Gabriel, new people are very scary and he feels that he needs to tell them to go away by barking and lunging, when put in poor situations this has led to him having a bite history. He is a very sweet dog but he has very little he trusts in this world and unfortunately humans are top of that list at the moment. With people who have earned his trust he is exceptionally sweet and loving, he loves to give you cuddles and he really thinks he should be a lap dog. When introductions are done slowly and in a manner that he can cope with he will allow that person into his circle reasonably quickly and then he gets very excited to see them.

As he has had very little in this world he does become exceptionally attached to his trusted humans and doesn't like to share them with other dogs or other people, so he is looking for a home with a maximum of two people and will need to be the only dog in the home. Adopters with experience of guarding behaviours are essential to help him succeed in his next home and make sure it really will be his forever home.

Gabriel walks nicely on his harness and gets very excited to see dogs when out and about but is wary of strangers walking past, for this reason he is muzzled when out as it keeps him safe in the event of someone getting too close or trying to touch him.

He has shown signs of resource guarding his food here and any high value long lasting treats. He has Kongs as he is happy for the empty Kong to be removed from his kennel once he feels he's finished with it, but these are things that will have to be managed in his new home. It would be a good idea to limit his access to the kitchen in the home to avoid the possibility of him getting things that he may be inclined to guard, especially until he settles and the bond has been built with him to ensure that he trusts that you won't take things away from him without him getting something higher value in its place.

Gabriel socialises well with other dogs here and does enjoy chasing dogs around our big play yard here, so having the opportunity to continue making friends with playful dogs in his new home is necessary to keep him happy and help him to continue to grow in confidence. Someone will be incredibly lucky to have Gabriel as their companion, they will just have to understand that he does require the time and effort to make sure he progresses and starts to see the world is less scary than he thinks it is.

Gabriel will need more than one meet and greet with his prospective adopters to allow him time to build a bond and feel comfortable with them before being adopted.

Gabriel is still waiting for his forever home, I don't know what it's going to take for people to notice this handsome man.

Gabriel recently had a play date with Margate who some of you may have heard of, they went to spend a few hours at a nearby lake with two of our members of staff, and he had a blast. He was on a long line and was free to explore wherever he wanted.

He was so well behaved during the walk, with Margate, the two staff members and when they stopped for ice cream after. He just loves being out adventuring, he wants to sniff everything and explore the world around him, needless to say he was knackered when he returned, had his dinner and went to bed, the sign of a good day.

Gabriel loved his time and the lake, so much so that I'm planning on taking him for another adventure soon that he will hopefully love just as much.

Today I got to spend more time with Gabriel than I usually would so I took advantage of that and we went for a much longer walk.... As usual he was brilliant, he listens, if we need to move out of the way for a car he'll listen to me and move off the road to the side, if he's walking slightly ahead and I call him he stops and turns back.

We also sat around the other side of the rescue where it's usually busier as I want to get him used to being in busier areas and being around people he doesn't know, as he can be a bit reactive.... He did so well, it was fairly busy so he was a little unsure at first but the longer we stayed the better he was, he was good with others around him too, he has come such a long way, but this is something I'm going to keep on working on with him for the foreseeable as we don't know what life he'll have outside of here and he may need to used to busier areas.

We also played with a puzzle feeder today, which he decided would be fun to pick up with his mouth and drop it on the floor to get the treats out faster, he really is a funny boy, but he's super smart too and is quick to pick up tricks especially when there's treats involved.

He really is every Bocker lovers dream and he always gets so overlooked.

He is muzzle trained, and would need to wear his muzzle when meeting new people, dogs or at the vets, but he's also just a big softy who gives the loveliest cwtches and kisses, to be a part of his gang is such an amazing feeling and he shows his affection for you so clearly when he loves you.

This week we’ve had a heatwave which has meant alot of our rescue dogs have needed their ears checked incase they’ve had any mucky build up - Gabriel was one of the unlucky few that have needed some TLC in this area!!We’ve recently had a new meds person who has been visiting Gabriel to do his ear cleans & he has been an absolute angel. He’s even been given the nickname Angel GabrielIt’s just a testament to Gabriel that yes he can be unsure of new people, but once he knows you he truly is such a wonderful boy. He just needs someone to take that chance on him, show him the love he’s desperate to have & he’ll return it tenfold.Gabriel has been waiting such a long time now, and seeing a boy so full of love & hope is heartbreaking when we can’t reassure him that his time will come soon!!!

Today, I worked with Gabriel again for the first time in months. I was a little worried he’d have forgotten, however, it’s safe to say the bond previously made still remains.Gabriel is such an excited little boy. He lives for treats. He’s such a clever and obedient boy when the treats come out. Usually, he’s full of energy and excitement. Once the treats are out, he’s still and sits like the perfect little boy we know he can be.As he can be very busy, I’ve always thought it essential to take him out on walks, the longer the better. As mentioned in a previous update, he loves walks! Once you pull the lead out, you get a similar reaction to the treats.The longer the walk the better. Walks are so good for this gorgeous boy. They keep him stimulated and help shave off the pounds he gains from everyone giving him treats!On the whole, I was so happy to see my boy again. So happy, so loyal, keen to go on walks and he listened so well. I’m so proud of the progress he’s made since I last saw him!Gabriel still can be a challenge and, he does not like everyone. Once you’ve made that bond with him though, it stays. Don’t overlook this boy. He’s such a beautiful, intelligent and fun dog!

This boy has my heart, once you form that special bond with him I do believe it's for life. He is very loving and enjoys a cuddle and a fuss from people he feels comfortable around, as his adopter you'll hopefully get that bond through spending time with him and letting him go at his own pace.Gabriel, as most bockers do, lives for his food and treats, whenever I run him in from being in the yard I always leave a small treat in his bed or somewhere in the back for him to find, and he absolutely loves this he gets so excited knowing he'll get a treat and runs straight to the back of his kennel to find it.He loves his walks and his time in the big yard. He's the curious, adventurous type who just wants to investigate everything, a 10 minute stroll up the road can take us an extra 20-25 minutes to stroll back because he likes to explore, but I don't mind, seeing him happy makes me happy I'd never want to stop him from exploring the world.Gabriel would need an experienced, adult only home (view profile for explanation), he would need someone who is active and can provide him with mental and physical stimulation daily. He is a very smart boy and can pick things up quite quickly which is why, with the help from some treats I think he would pick up toilet training rather quickly.Please don't overlook this handsome guy just because he's not your small and fluffy type dog, Gabriel is a special boy with a lot of love to give, and for that right person/people he would become a true companion and best friend.

Gabriel, a stunning Bocker with a huge personality and an even bigger heart. This handsome boy is full of life and enthusiasm, always ready to embrace whatever the day brings. Gabriel thrives on affection and absolutely loves a good fuss and cuddle — he’s a real people-dog who enjoys being close to those he trusts.

Gabriel is a clever lad with so much potential. He’s already showing us just how intelligent he is as he responds to basic commands! With the right guidance and training , we know he’ll flourish and continue to grow in confidence, not that he lacks any confidence! He also walks beautifully on the lead, making him a joy to take out on adventures.

Sadly, Gabriel has been returned to us, and we are now searching for the right forever home where he can truly settle and feel secure. Gabriel would be best suited as an only dog, in a calm and quiet home environment. We are looking for a home with minimal visitors and no children, as busy households can feel overwhelming for him.

Gabriel can display guarding behaviours, so he will need experienced owners who understand this and can manage the home environment appropriately to support him. With the right knowledge, structure, and patience, Gabriel will thrive and continue to build trust.

Gabriel has so much love to give to the right person. With understanding, consistency, and kindness, he will make an incredibly loyal and devoted time

Gabriel is a stunning Bocker who is full of life, love, and character! This gorgeous boy is bursting with energy and adores nothing more than a good fuss and a cwtch.He’s incredibly smart, and we just know it wouldn’t take long for him to be trained to a very high standard – he’s already showing us how bright he is every day. Gabriel also walks beautifully on the lead, making him a joy to take out and about.Now all he needs is a forever family who can give him the love, attention, and adventures he deserves. With his brains, energy, and big heart, Gabriel is sure to make someone the most wonderful companion.

Gabriel has come to us from a breeder and has made incredible progress since arriving with us! When he first came, he was nervous around new people and worried about having a lead put on, which made walks and new kennel staff introductions a real challenge. Now, he gets excited for walk time and happily allows us to put on both his lead and harness with no issues.This handsome boy is a true foodie and loves learning new tricks. He already knows “sit” and “paw,” so with trust and patience, teaching him more tricks should be a fun and rewarding experience. Gabriel needs a confident, experienced, owner who will provide clear boundaries and structure, as he can be cheeky if he thinks he’s in charge as well as an adult-only home where he can continue to learn. Gabriel has the confidence to be an only dog in a home with can allow him the dedication and time he needs and will need a home with no cats or small furries.Once Gabriel knows and trusts you, he is affectionate, loyal, and loves nothing more than sharing his goofy charm. Underneath his shy moments, he is a beautiful boy with a heart full of love. He is looking for someone who will continue his training, set clear rules, and enjoy all the affection, loyalty, and joy he has to give.

These wonderful souls may be older, have medical needs, or come with a few unique quirks—but they have endless love to give. Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

name: Dutch
description:
I could live with dog-savvy teens aged 16+ who respect my space.

I need to be the only dog in my new home. No cats please!

I walk well on a lead and muzzle trained. I would enjoy an active lifestyle!

Please be patient with me, I haven’t lived in a home before.

I am already vaccinated and neutered and ready for my new home!

Dutch is an incredible boy who has come into our care from a pound in Ireland in search of a fresh start. Unfortunately, we don't know much about his history, but what we do know is that he is one of the most loving and affectionate dogs you could ever hope to meet, with a heart as big as his personality. Dutch simply wants to be close to his people, whether that's following you around, leaning into you for fuss, or curling up beside you for cuddles. Being with the people he loves is all he really wants.

Dutch would love to find a home with adopters who are around for most of the day and can include him in everyday life. He thrives on human companionship and will make a wonderfully devoted shadow to his new family. He will need adopters who have experience with similar breeds and understand typical breed traits, including prey drive and the need for appropriate mental and physical enrichment.

Dutch would be best suited to life as an only dog. Although he can socialise well with other dogs of a similar size, he can become overexcited and mouthy, which may lead to frustration. Because of this, he is muzzle trained and wears a muzzle during social interactions to help him continue building positive experiences. He cannot live with cats or small furries.

As Dutch has never lived in a home before, he will need support with house training and learning the general routines of family life. He is such a clever boy and always tries his very best to do the right thing, so we are confident he will enjoy learning with patient, positive guidance.

Dutch already walks well on a lead, although he can occasionally be reactive when passing other kennels. This is understandable in a busy rescue environment and may be something his adopters will need to continue working on. He is an energetic, happy-go-lucky boy who is more than ready to start exploring the world with his new family. An active home where he can enjoy plenty of walks, enrichment, training and quality time with his people would suit him perfectly.

Dutch could share his home with older, dog-savvy teenagers who can appreciate that he will need a gentle introduction to his new surroundings and his own space to settle in.

Dutch is bright, affectionate and full of love. He has so much to offer and is simply looking for someone to love as much as he loves them. For the right family, he will be an incredibly loyal, fun-loving and devoted companion.

Dutch has a passport and travel document.

Dutch has been given the Gift of Life by Louise Southward

I’m truly so sad that Dutch is still waiting for his forever home. It’s such a shame that certain breeds can be so easily overlooked.

Dutch is the most sweet, loving, loyal and clever boy. He absolutely loves everyone, has bags of confidence and is always bursting with excitement to say hello to everyone he meets out on a walk.

We've recently started walking Dutch with different friends each day to help him learn to manage some of his reactivity, and honestly, after just one walk, the very next day he was absolutely brilliant!

Dutch isn't reactive because he wants to be difficult, he's simply so excited and eager to say hello that he's still learning how to manage those feelings.

He's such a smart boy and has picked things up so quickly. He just needs someone who will keep that clever brain busy, give him some guidance and help him continue to learn.

Please don't overlook Dutch. There is so much to love about this boy, and we would love nothing more than to see him finally find his forever home.

I still can’t quite understand how this incredibly smart and loving boy hasn’t found his forever home yet.If you’re looking for a dog to train, learn new tricks and go on lots of adventures with, then Dutch really is your boy.He’s the best of both worlds a crazy, energetic boy who also absolutely loves his people and loves nothing more than a good snuggle.

Dutch, or as I like to call him, Dutchy, is honestly one of the most loving and affectionate boys you could ever hope to meet.

He's the kind of dog who just wants to be close to you. Whether it's following you around, leaning into you for fuss, or curling up for cuddles, being with his people is all he really wants. Watching him have to go back into his kennel after spending time together is heartbreaking because kennel life is just no place for a boy like him.

What makes it even sadder is that he hasn't received a single application. If I'm honest, my biggest worry is that he'll become one of our long-stay dogs, and my heart breaks at the thought of that because he simply doesn't deserve it.

He's such a clever boy and always tries so hard to do the right thing. He recently went on his first long walk with one of our wonderful regular volunteers and was an absolute angel. He took everything in his stride and made everyone so proud.

He's also been having play dates with our lovely girl, Swanny, to help him burn off some of that doggy energy while learning good doggy manners.

At the end of the day, Dutchy is just a baby. He's got the biggest heart, so much love to give, and he deserves a home where he'll be someone's whole world instead of waiting behind kennel doors. I know his family is out there somewhere; I just hope they find him before he spends another day wondering why no one has chosen him.

Dutch is an incredible boy who has come into our care from a pound in Ireland in search of a fresh start. Unfortunately, we don't know much about his history, but what we do know is that he is one of the most loving and affectionate dogs you could ever hope to meet.

He would love to find a loving home with adopters who are around most of the time and would have plenty of time to spend with him. He would need adopters who have experience with similar breeds and experience with his typical breed traits like prey drive etc.

Dutch would be best suited to being homed as an only dog as although he does socialise well with other dogs of his size, he can become over excited and mouthy which can lead to frustration. For this reason he is being trained to wear a muzzle when socialising. He cannot be homed with cats or small furries.

As Dutch has never lived in a home before, he will need to learn all about house training and the other basics of home life. With patience and guidance, we think he will adapt well and enjoy all the comforts a home has to offer.

Dutch can already walk well on a lead, though he can be a little reactive when passing other kennels, this is understandable in a busy rescue environment, but may be something his adopters will need to work with him on. He is an energetic and incredibly lovely bo who ie is happy-go-lucky in nature and is more than ready to start adventuring with his new adopters. He would love an active home where he can enjoy plenty of walks, enrichment, and quality time with his people.

Dutch could share his home with older, dog-savvy teenagers who can appreciate and understand that he will need a gentle and quiet introduction to the home, along with his own space to settle in.

He is a bright, affectionate, and fun-loving boy who is sure to make a wonderful and loyal companion for a lucky family.

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. Every sponsorship helps us rescue and save more dogs in desperate need. If you would like to become part of a rescue story, please consider donating to our Gift of Life fund.

name: Tulip
description:
I will need an adult-only home that understands me.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I'd like a secure garden to potter around in.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

I am learning about house training in my foster home, but will need more training.

I am spayed and ready to find my forever home.

Tulip is a sweet little lady who has come to us from a breeder and is currently finding the world a little overwhelming. She is a scared and worried girl who is still very unsure of people and does not like to be handled at the moment. She relies heavily on her canine friends for reassurance and can still be confused and worried by unfamiliar sights and random noises. She will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her home that will take her under their wing.

Tulip is now in a foster home where she is beginning to learn all about living in a home, including house training and the new noises and routines that come with being in a home. She is making progress, but she is going to need plenty of time and patience to settle and feel safe enough to show her true personality. Her adopters will need to understand that this may take some time, and she cannot be rushed.

Tulip will need an adult-only home with experience of ex-breeding dogs and at least one kind and confident resident dog who she can lean on for reassurance. She will need a home without young visiting children or a lot of coming and going as she would prefer a quiet place to settle. She will need a quiet home where her new family can take things slowly and allow her to build her confidence at her own pace. We are looking for adopters who either have previous experience with ex-breeding dogs or have the time, patience and understanding to help this little dog settle into home life. Ideally, adopters would be home most of the day, such as those who are retired or do not work.

Tulip is a lovely little lady who has a lot to learn about the world, and we hope that with the right home, patient adopters and a friendly dog by her side, she will gradually learn that she is safe and loved.

Tulip has been given the Gift of Life by Karen Cooper

Tulip is still an extremely nervous little girl who is finding the world quite overwhelming at the moment. She is very worried and does not like to be handled too quickly, so her adopters will need to understand her body language and give her plenty of space. If she feels cornered or frightened, she may react defensively, so she will need people who are experienced and willing to take things very slowly.Tulip will need a very quiet, settled home with minimal disruption and no children or young children visiting, as this would be far too overwhelming for her. She does look constantly worried at the moment, but we have started to see little glimpses of her personality, including a few lovely moments of play, which is very encouraging.Tulip has a long way to go, but we are hopeful that with time, patience and the right home, she will gradually learn to feel safe and show us the happy little girl underneath all those worries.

Tulip is a fun little lady who has come to us from a breeder and has such an amazing personality! She is a very inquisitive girl who is always interested in what is going on around her and we know she will absolutely blossom once she is settled into a loving home. Tulip can be a little touch-sensitive and is still learning to trust people, but she is trying so hard to be brave and is making lovely progress.Tulip will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home who she can lean on for reassurance as she learns about home life. Having a friendly dog by her side will help her feel more secure while she gets used to all the new sights, sounds and experiences that come with living in a home.Tulip has never lived in a home before, so her adopters will need to be kind and patient as she learns things such as house training and walking on a lead. She can live with older, dog-savvy teens aged 16+ who are sensible and understanding and will give her the time and space she needs to settle in.Tulip is a lovely little lady with a wonderful personality who is trying so hard to be brave. We are sure that with the right home, a kind resident dog and people who are willing to give her the time she needs, she will continue to grow in confidence and absolutely love home life.

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. Every sponsorship helps us rescue and save more dogs in desperate need. If you would like to become part of a rescue story, please consider donating to our Gift of Life fund.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Rhiannon
description:
I need a calm and quiet home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I will be spayed before finding my forever home.

name: Bilbo
description:
I would like an adult only home with adopters who have plenty of time for me.

I would be happy to be homed as an only dog! I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden with 6ft+ fences.

I would love one or two slow walks a day!

I have lived in a home before so know the basics, but I may need a few reminders!

I have been neutered and am ready for my forever home.

07-11-26 Bilbo is a gorgeous boy who has found his way into our care after spending nine years in a home before sadly being returned to his breeder. He is an absolutely lovely boy who is very much a family dog and is ready to find somewhere to enjoy his golden years.

Bilbo will be looking for a loving home with adopters who have experience with dogs of a similar breed. At the moment, we feel he would be best suited to an adult-only home where he can have the time, patience and understanding he needs to settle into his new home. Bilbo does show signs of separation anxiety and can become quite unsettled when people leave his kennel and will bark at them to try and stop them leaving. He will need adopters who are happy to work with him on this, helping him to feel more comfortable and gradually building up the time he can be left alone. With patience, consistency and lots of reassurance, we hope he will soon learn that he is safe and doesn't need to worry when his people leave him.

Although Bilbo is an older boy, you wouldn't know his age when you meet him! Bilbo is outgoing, friendly and just wants to be everyone's best friend. He walks well on a lead, although he can be a little strong at times. Bilbo is confident enough that he could be homed as an only dog as long as his adopters were around most of the time and had plenty of time to spend with him. At the moment he is kenneled alone, but we will start introducing him to other dogs and in the right circumstances he may be able to be homed with another kind resident dog.

Having previously lived in a home, Bilbo may already know some of the basics, although he might need a few gentle reminders as he adjusts to his new surroundings. He has some stiffness in his legs, which is to be expected with age, and he will be started on YuMOVE to help support his joints.

Bilbo has already given nine years of his life to a home, and he deserves nothing more than to spend his golden years surrounded by love, comfort and all the fuss he could ever want. We really hope someone will see what a special boy he is and offer him the forever home he so deserves.

name: Yasmin
description:
I can live with older, dog savvy teenagers, aged 16+ who respect my space.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I'd like a secure garden to potter around in.

I haven't tried walks yet, a secure garden will be fine for now.

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training and lead walking.

I have an umbilical hernia that will be addressed at the time of my spay.

22-10-26 Yasmin is a quiet little girl who has come into our care from a breeder in search of a new start. She seems a little overwhelmed by her new surroundings, but she has been accepting of handling and is not overly scared. Yasmin is a shy girl who will need time, patience and gentle encouragement to help her feel safe and begin to build her confidence. However, the longer she has been with us, she has built some confidence and will approach to take some treat paste from you.

Yasmin would do well with a kind and gentle resident dog in her new home to help guide her and give her the reassurance she needs as she settles in and finds her paws. Having a friendly canine companion by her side should help her feel more secure as she adjusts to life in a home. Her adopters will need to have experience with ex-breeders to better understand her needs. She can live with older, dog-savvy teens aged 16 and over who are sensible.

Yasmin has arrived with a large abdominal hernia, which our vets will address at the time of her spay.

With a calm, loving home and a little patience, we hope Yasmin will gradually grow in confidence and discover the comforts of being a cherished family member.
