name: Crumble
description:
I need an adult-only, experienced home where I can feel safe and loved.

I want to be the only dog in the house. No cats please!

I’m still shy, so I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I love my walks so one or two a day would be great!

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

Crumble is a lovely lady who came into our care from a breeder, searching for a fresh start. When she first arrived, she was very worried and unsure of the world around her, but with time and patience she has begun to settle beautifully. Crumble is now much less fearful of us humans and has really started to come out of her shell, choosing to engage more with staff members and showing curiosity about her surroundings. She seems to be gaining confidence each day, which is wonderful to see.

While she can still be sensitive and appreciates having her space respected, it’s clear that Crumble simply needed time to feel safe. With gentle reassurance and plenty of TLC, her true personality is beginning to shine through. She is a gentle soul who responds best to calm, kind interactions and slow introductions.

She would be happiest and thrive best as the only dog in the home, where she can enjoy all the attention, settle more easily into a routine, and build a strong bond with her new family.

As she has never lived in a home environment before, she will need patient support with house training and learning everyday routines. She will need a home without cats as she is overly interested.

We are looking for an experienced, adult-only home where Crumble can continue to build her confidence at her own pace. A quiet household with understanding adopters who are happy to let her take things slowly will allow her to truly flourish. With the right people, time, and lots of love, Crumble will make a wonderfully rewarding companion.

On arrival, our vets noted that Crumble had a Grade 2 luxating patella. During her time with us she has shown very intermittent lameness, mostly only seen when she’s getting up from laying down for a long time. She was sent for x-rays which showed potential damage to her left cruciate ligament, as well as hip dysplasia in her right hip. She is currently managing very well with rest and pain relief, and we will work on building correct muscle tone to support her as well as slow introductions to controlled exercise and physio.

I was very eager to say hello to my little croissant, haven’t worked with Crumble for a little over a month, but she was a bit reluctant to approach me. Once I allowed her a little time to recognise me and give me a standard sniff, the very friendly, bouncy little lady almost tackled me with love. Bum scratches galore!

I showed her the harness, and she was beaming, giving little excited nibbles of my hands to show just how excited she was to spend time with me, an old friend, out of the kennels.

She is currently on kennel rest and has been instructed to have one small walk a day to keep her legs strong, and it is quite a challenge to keep this girly still.

I hope Crumble finds a home before Christmas because seeing such a happy girly who can live alone still living in kennels, as much as we do our best to ensure Crumble is well taken care of, is sad. She deserves the love of a home, a comfy bed and unlimited scratches and walks!

Crumble is one of those ladies that you may need to work harder to earn their trust initially but once she loves you she truly is besotted and becomes very excited to see you every time you appear. She is very playful with her best friend Criss Cross but is very dog selective otherwise, she has recently been approved to start going for short walks daily after being on kennel rest and she is very happy to be able to go for a walk with Criss Cross and have all the sniffs again.

Crumble can be unsure about noises and her instinct is to go to her safe space in the back of her kennel and wait for the scary thing to go away but she does take comfort when her trusted people go in and sit with her to let her know that she is okay.She may be looking for a particular set up with very special people who understand her and love all of her quirks, but when she finds it she will make them smile and laugh every single day, this girl has so much love and personality to share with you once you've made her feel safe around you.

Crumble is the most incredible girl who loves her humans once she has bonded with you. She has such a huge personality and makes all of her kennel mums and dads laugh every single day.

She absolutely loves playing with her best friend Criss Cross and she loves splashing in water when it's warm weather.

She's one of those exceptional girls who will make someone incredibly lucky and give them so much love and fun once they've put in the time to earn her trust and build that bond with her.

There’s not a bad word you could say about this girly pop. She is goofy, affectionate, playful, friendly and gaining confidence by the day! She has been trying her best to be kennel clean, no encouragement needed.

She is a staff favourite and that girls little teefys are part of her personality! Nibbling at you to show you just how much she loves to play with you, entertains her pal Criss cross and her kennel mums in the yard.

She belongs in a home where her people can show her the best doggy life imaginable while also understanding that Crumble has also not known much of the world and requires a bit of patience and care when handling her.

Taking every opportunity to play and zoom around with her best friend, Criss Cross.Her confidence is growing and enjoying her walks and greeting new people at her own free will as long as she is guaranteed some fuss or treats.

She enjoys sprawling out on the floor with her chew toy just enjoying the vibes.When she finds her home she will be very eager in sharing her affectionate nature with her family

Crumble is becoming a very happy chow now and has recently discovered that there's no limit on zoomies. She does get along with her chow friend, Criss Cross, but isn't keen on other dogs, so is looking for a home as an only. She is wary of people initially, but once you've gained her trust she becomes your absolute best mate. She loves her walks and gets very excited when she sees you bringing her harness towards her. She's a big foodie too and loves treats.

Crumble is coming on so beautifully and it truly makes my heart melt. Today we had some cuddle and play time in her kennel, and it was such a special moment. For a girl who once wasn’t very happy with touch, she’s now rolling over for belly rubs, snuggling in her bed, and even playing “paw paw” with me.

She’s also learning about wearing a harness and is improving every day. If you have a Crumble shaped hole in your life, she really is something special.

Crumble is a worried lady who came into our care from a breeder, searching for a fresh start. When she first arrived, she was very worried and unsure of the world around her, but with time and patience she has begun to settle beautifully. Crumble is now much less fearful of us humans and has really started to come out of her shell, choosing to engage more with staff members and showing curiosity about her surroundings.

Crumble will need a confident and friendly resident dog who can help guide her and show her the ropes. As she has never lived in a home environment before, she will need patient support with house training, lead walking, and learning everyday routines. But will need to take things slow to start with some garden sniffs adventures on the lead may be too scary to start.

Crumble has a previous bite wound inside her ear, which is currently being treated.

These wonderful souls may be older, have medical needs, or come with a few unique quirks—but they have endless love to give. Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

Despite her fears, she will let you gently stroke her and with love and TLC we think she will start to come out of her shell.

Venus will be looking for a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and will allow her to settle in at her own pace. We would consider homing her with dog savvy teenagers.

Venus is a timid girl who will need a special home willing to give her the time and patience she deserves. With a kind family and a confident doggy friend by her side, we hope she can slowly find her paws and discover how lovely life in a home can be.

name: Bee
description:
I could live with dog-savvy teens who respect my space.

I would like to be homed with another canine friend. I've not met cats so I'm unsure!

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I haven't tried walks just yet and will find this a bit overwhelming at the moment.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I am spayed and ready to find my forever home.

Bee is a gentle, shy little lady who has come into our care from a breeder. She is still a timid girl who can find the world around her a little overwhelming, but she has been making some lovely progress since arriving with us and is really trying hard to be brave.

Bee can be handled and picked up as long as you take things slowly and carefully. She is beginning to show us that she wants to build a bond with people, and she has started getting very excited to see her favourite people in the mornings, running over to say hello and even giving little kisses on their fingers! She is still a little unsure about accepting fusses, but we think she is getting closer to letting her guard down and learning that human attention can be a lovely thing.

Bee has always lived with the company of other dogs and gets on wonderfully with her kennel friends. She relies on their company for comfort and reassurance, so she will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home who she can learn from, follow and look to as she settles into home life. We think having a friendly dog or two around will really help her find her confidence and make the transition into a home much easier.

Bee has never lived in a home before, so there is still lots for her to learn. She has recently had her first little introduction to wearing a harness and did brilliantly! Although she only managed a few steps, she was happy to have a sniff around, take some treats and explore without becoming overwhelmed. We will continue building on this little by little, and her adopters will need to be patient as she learns about lead walking, house training and all the other things that come with home life.

Bee will be looking for a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience with worried ex-breeding dogs and understand that she will need time to settle and gain confidence at her own pace. We think she will really benefit from being away from the busy kennel environment and having the chance to learn about life in a quieter setting. She can live with sensible teenagers who understand that she will need to be given space and allowed to settle without pressure.

Bee is such a little sweetheart, and it is lovely to see her starting to show us the happy little girl hiding underneath all those worries. She is trying so hard to be brave, and we think she has so much potential to blossom in the right home. With an experienced ex-breeding dog home, kind canine companions to guide her and plenty of love and reassurance, we are sure Bee will make a wonderful addition to the family. Please don't keep this lovely girl waiting any longer for her chance at home life!

Bee has been at the rescue for just about a month now and I love her more and more every day. She’s still a timid little girl, but I can tell she’s trying so hard to be brave. She gets really excited to see me in the mornings and will run up to me and give me kisses on my fingers, and it’s so sweet to see. I think she really wants to start having fusses from me, but she’s still holding back just that little bit. I really don’t think it will take too long for her to drop her guard though!! And I do also think she’ll come on a lot faster in a quiet home environment as opposed to busy kennels!

Today I took her out on a harness for the first time. She didn’t take many steps, but she did some sniffs, took treats off me, and didn’t have any panics. To me, this is a brilliant first attempt!!! I only did a very short session as I didn’t want to overwhelm her, so I’ll keep doing that little by little and I do think she’ll start to walk relatively soon. I’m not saying she’s going to be a pro walking up mountains any time soon, but baby steps!Bee is SUCH a little sweetheart and she’s really no bother to look after at the rescue at all. I think she’ll slot into home life pretty quickly with a sibling or 2 to help her. So please don’t keep her waiting much longer.

Bee is a gentle, shy little lady who has come into our care from a breeder alongside her sister, Gemma. She has been making great progress since coming to us, although she is still a very timid girl who is feeling overwhelmed by many aspects of the world around her.

Bee can be handled and picked up as long as you take things slowly and carefully. She still finds human interaction worrying, so her adopters will need to give her plenty of time and patience to build trust and understand that people can be kind and positive.

Bee has always lived with the company of other dogs and gets on wonderfully with her kennel friends. She relies on their company for comfort, so she will need a kind, confident resident dog in her new home who she can learn from, follow and look to for reassurance as she settles into home life.

Bee has never lived in a home before, so there is lots for her to learn. She will need patient adopters who understand that lead training, toilet training and all the other basics of home life will be completely new to her. She does not yet have these skills and will need them introduced gradually, with plenty of encouragement and positive reinforcement.

Bee will be looking for a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience with worried ex-breeding dogs and understand that she will need time to settle and gain confidence at her own pace. She can live with teenagers who are sensible and understand that she will need to be given space and allowed to settle without pressure.

Bee is a really lovely girl who is trying hard to find her confidence. She deserves a home who will absolutely adore her and give her all the time, patience and reassurance she needs. With an experienced ex-breeding dog home, a kind resident dog to guide her and plenty of love, we are sure Bee will continue to blossom into a very sweet addition to the family.

name: Archie
description:
I'd like a quiet, adult-only home to help me relax and feel safe.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I walk well on a lead and would enjoy one or two walks a day!

I have lived in a home so I know the basics.

I have been neutered and have had 21 teeth removed.

Archie is such a sweet little man who came into our care from a breeder. He was adopted but has sadly been returned after his adopters felt they were not the right match for him. Archie formed a very strong bond with his female owner, but found it much harder to build a relationship with her husband, who was frequently away from home and therefore had very little opportunity to gain Archie's trust. When Archie becomes closely bonded to his favourite person, he can become protective of them. In his previous home, he nipped when he was sitting with his owner and her husband approached, so his new adopters will need to understand this behaviour and be prepared to continue building his confidence in a positive and patient way.

He is a cuddly and affectionate little dog once he feels comfortable, although he isn't quite brave enough to take treats from our hands just yet. Although Archie gets on well with other dogs, he can become protective of his favourite person around them, so we think he would be happiest as the only dog in the home, where he can relax and build a close bond with his new family.

As Archie has lived in a home before, he will already be familiar with the sights and sounds of home life. However, he may need a little reminding of his house training in a new environment. He walks well on a lead and enjoys his walks with volunteers.

Archie is looking for a quiet, adult-only home with adopters who have experience of the breed and of rescue dogs. He will need people who are happy to give him the time and space he needs to settle and understand that he is safe.

Archie is doing really well since returning to us and his confidence is growing all the time. He is such a loving little dog, and in the right home, we hope he will continue to thrive and become a devoted companion.

We absolutely love this little guy at the rescue, Archie may be small but his personality is mighty. He is funny, lovable and impossible not to love. Archie is still a tiny bit shy with new people but it’s taking him less and less time to open up to new people and dogs. Archie loves to play with tennis balls, smother you with kisses and generally amuse us with his cheeky personality. Archie would like a child-free home as he is still a little anxious at times.

Archie is an absolute pleasure to work with! It’s been some time now, and our bond continues to grow stronger every day.He absolutely loves smothering you with kisses and will do anything to get himself onto your lap! Archie has been kennelled with a few dogs and socialised with plenty more, but he has become particularly taken with a Cocker called Trixie. They share some similar traits, including not wanting to share their humans, although neither has displayed any jealousy towardsthe other so far. They absolutely love running laps around the yard together before heading straight into your lap for some fuss. Archie will even stand on Trixie’s back just to make sure he gets in on the action and doesn’t miss out on any attention!As mentioned, Archie is yet to display any jealous traits towards either dogs or humans, but that doesn’t mean he won’t potentially show this once settled into a home. It’s something any potential adopter should be mindful of and prepared to manage appropriately.

What I can promise, though, is that Archie will become your best friend. He has so much love to give and, once he trusts you, he will love you unconditionally.This gorgeous boy deserves someone who will give him the love, patience and understanding he needs — and in return, you’ll have a loyal companion who will want nothing more than to be by your side.

Archie is the funniest and cheekiest of little Dachshunds. Archie needs a little time to warm to you (but not all that long), and once he does, he is the most lovely of boys. I have been caring for him for a few weeks now, and I am totally smitten.

Archie walks beautifully on lead and loves nothing more than when we venture out for a stroll along the lanes around the rescue. Archie is very fond of his toys and will happily run around the yard with a ball in his mouth. He will also spend much time organising his cuddly toys, making sure they are in just the right place.

Archie has been kennelled with other small female dogs. He seems to do best with robust smaller females, as he can be a little frisky with the more timid dogs. Archie could go as an only dog in the right home, one where there are humans who will have lots of time for him.

Archie is very enthusiastic with his kisses once he knows you and will desperately clamber over you for fusses. Archie is an all-round lovely little dog, best suited to a quiet adult home where there is plenty of love, time, and patience for him to truly settle in.

Archie is such a sweet little man who came into our care from a breeder. He was adopted but has sadly been returned after his adopters felt they were not the right match for him. Archie formed a very strong bond with his female owner, but found it much harder to build a relationship with her husband, who was frequently away from home and therefore had very little opportunity to gain Archie's trust. When Archie becomes closely bonded to his favourite person, he can become protective of them. In his previous home, he nipped when he was sitting with his owner and her husband approached, so his new adopters will need to understand this behaviour and be prepared to continue building his confidence in a positive, patient way.

He is a cuddly, affectionate little dog once he feels comfortable, although he isn't quite brave enough to take treats from our hands just yet. Although Archie gets on well with other dogs, he can become protective of his favourite person around them, so we think he would be happiest as the only dog in the home, where he can relax and build a close bond with his new family.

Archie is a gorgeous little boy who came to us from a breeder and was understandably unsure of the world around him. It was truly heartbreaking to see how frightened he was as he would shy away from human contact and retreat when approached. Archie needs gentle handling, patience, and calm, slow movements to help him feel safe. Already, we are seeing progress. He enjoys a gentle fuss and has grown some confidence wagging his tail enthusiastically.

He gains reassurance from other dogs and will need a kind, confident resident dog in his new home to help guide him, boost his confidence, and show him that people and home life can be safe and rewarding.

Archie has never lived in a home before, so his adopters will need to be patient and understanding as he learns the basics, including house training and walking on a lead. He could share his home with older, dog-savvy teenagers aged 16 and over, who can appreciate and understand that he will need a gentle, quiet introduction to the home and his own space to settle in.

Since arriving with us, Archie has undergone extensive and much-needed dental treatment and has had 21 teeth removed. He is now recovering well and feeling much more comfortable.

name: Rosita
description:
I would like a home filled with love and kindness!

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I am spayed and have had 8 teeth extracted.

08-11-26 Rosita is a sweet girl who has come to us from a breeder to find her forever home. When she initially arrived she was a very worried girl, but she has since started to come out of her shell and is a happy little girl. She will now slowly approach you to say hello and is happy to have a gentle fuss, but is still a little worried about us.

Rosita would be best suited to a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and will help her to settle in at her own pace. In the right circumstances we would consider homing her with dog savvy, gentle children aged 9+.

Rosita is happiest when she is with her kennel friends and relies on them for comfort, so she will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home who she can look to as she begins to build her confidence and learns about the world around her.

Rosita has never lived in a home before, so her adopters will need to be very kind and patient as she gets used to all the new experiences that come with home life, including house training and walking on a lead. She may need a little extra time before feeling brave enough to explore, so allowing her to settle at her own pace will be really important. Rosita is a lovely girl who just needs someone willing to give her the time, love and encouragement she needs to find her paws.

We hope that with the right family beside her, she will slowly discover just how lovely life can be!

Our vets have noted that Rosita arrived to us with severe periodontal disease, she has had a dental and had 8 teeth extracted, but her adopters will need to continue to monitor her teeth.

Rosita has been given the Gift of Life by Diane Stephen

name: Lollipop
description:
I could live with dog-savvy teenagers aged 16 +, who respect my space.

I need a doggy friend in my new home and would prefer a male dog. I don't mind cats!

I'm new to lead walking and need some practice!

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training and lead walking.

I have a grade 2 luxating patella and have had 7 teeth extracted. Read below for more

Lollipop is a lovely Bichon Frise who has come into our care from a breeder in search of a new start. She is an inquisitive and funny little girl who is already showing glimpses of her playful personality. Lollipop will happily come over to lick our fingers before darting away again, as if she's still deciding whether people are quite as interesting as her kennel friends.

Lollipop is still a nervous little girl, but she has been making lovely progress and is gradually becoming more curious about the people around her. The more time you spend with her, the more interested she becomes in you, and it is lovely to see her slowly coming out of her shell.

Lollipop loves the company of other dogs and relies heavily on them for comfort and reassurance. She is happy to follow their lead and takes great confidence from having another dog around. For this reason, she will need to have a resident dog in her new home. She will be looking for a home with a male resident dog as she can sometimes be a little sassy with female dogs.

Lollipop has also been making lovely progress with her harness training. She is easy to put her harness on and recently went out for her very first walk. Considering how nervous she can be, she did incredibly well! She will need plenty more gentle practice to help her become confident and comfortable with walking, and her adopters will need to continue this at her own pace.

As Lollipop has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training and the other basics of home life. Her adopters will need to be patient and understanding as she adjusts to a whole new world and gains confidence in her surroundings.

Lollipop could share her home with older, dog-savvy teenagers aged 16 and over who can appreciate and understand that she will need a gentle, quiet introduction to the home and her own space to settle in.

She has arrived with a Grade 2 luxating patella, but her mobility appears unaffected and this may improve as she builds muscle tone. Lollipop has also arrived with severe periodontal disease and has had seven teeth extracted.

Lollipop is an active and spritely little girl with a bright future ahead of her. With the support of a kind canine friend and a patient family, we hope her confidence will continue to grow and her charming personality will shine through even more.

Lollipop has been given the Gift of Life by Jodie Stanley

Lollipop is a lovely lady, she’s doing ever so well here and making great progress in confidence. She loves going out for a stroll or bouncing around with her friends in our yards. Lollipop also loves to sunbath as seen in her photos.

name: Pippa
description:
I'd like a quiet, adult-only home to help me relax and feel safe.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I will need an extra secure garden to keep me safe.

I haven't tried walks yet, a secure garden will be fine for now.

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training and lead walking.

I am spayed and ready to find my forever home.

30-09-26 Pippa is a very scared and nervous lady who has come into our care from a breeder. She is very worried about being handled and becomes stressed if we attempt to pick her up. She will try to jump from our arms and, because of this, we would consider her a flight risk and she will need fencing of at least 6ft in her new garden to keep her safe. She will need very careful handling and adopters who understand just how frightened she is at the moment.

Pippa gets on wonderfully with her kennel friends and relies on their company for comfort, so she will need a kind and confident resident dog in her new home to help guide her and give her the reassurance she needs as she settles in and finds her paws.

As Pippa has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training, lead training and the other basics of home life. Her new family will need to be very patient and give her time to adjust to all the new sights, sounds and experiences that come with living in a home.

Pippa will need a quiet, confident, adult-only home where she can relax and settle into her new surroundings without too much hustle and bustle. Her adopters will need to have ex-breeding experience and understand her nervous nature and allow her to progress at her own pace.

Pippa is a very worried girl right now, but with the security of a kind canine companion and a calm, patient family, we hope she will slowly begin to feel safe and gain the confidence she needs to enjoy her new life.

Pippa has been given the Gift of Life by Margaret Hunter
