She does love having a playfriend and she seems to be happiest when amongst other collies and collie crosses. She doesn't like sharing her food but is happy to share toys, beds and treats.

Lassie absolutely loves going out for her walks and gets very excited when she knows it’s time to head out. She really enjoys having a good sniff along the way and is always very interested in watching what’s going on in the fields as she passes by. Once she gets to know you, she is incredibly loving and affectionate, although she can take a little bit of time to warm up to new people. Lassie would still need a home with a resident dog, and she would truly thrive in a collie-experienced home where her needs and personality can be well understood.

Lassie is such a beautiful girl and once she knows you, she is the most affectionate, loyal and loving companion. She now walks well on a lead and absolutely loves her walks.

She will need a home with at least one other kind and confident resident dog who is a similar size to her and who loves to have a good play sometimes.

She doesn't like to share her food bowl, so he will need to be fed separately and this is something that her adopters will need to manage. In the right home she'll be someone's absolute best friend.

Lassie is a worried little lady who has come to us from a breeder. She has not had much experience with people, so everything feels very new and overwhelming to her. She can be quite skittish when approached, so she will need a calm, experienced home where she can be given the time and patience she needs to learn to trust.

At the moment, Lassie is scared of being touched, but she has already started to build a bond with her kennel mum and now allows gentle strokes from her. This shows that with consistency and kindness, shecanlearn to trust, and once she feels safe, she will begin to show her sweet side.

Lassie does walk on a lead, though she finds new experiences worrying, so she will need gentle introductions to the big wide world. She will also need to learn about house training and all the basics of living in a home, as these are things she has never known before.

Because Lassie is such a sensitive soul, she will need an adult-only home with no visiting children, and adopters who are happy to take things slowly at her pace. She will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home who can help her feel secure and show her the ropes. She gets on brilliantly with all dogs here and socialises well with a variety of breeds and sizes. She cannot be homed with cats or small furries.

With time, patience, and lots of love, Lassie will blossom. Once she has settled and gained confidence, she will become a cracking addition to her new family and will enjoy all the adventures life has to offer.

These wonderful souls may be older, have medical needs, or come with a few unique quirks—but they have endless love to give. Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Helga
description:
I can live with older children, aged 13+, who understand I need time to settle in.

I would like to be the only animal in my new home.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I walk well on a lead and would enjoy one or two walks a day!

I have lived in a home before so know the basics.

I have been spayed & am ready for my forever home! Read below for more!

25-09-26 Helga is a wonderful lady who originally came to us a while ago and was adopted into a loving home, where she spent several happy years. Sadly, she has now returned to our care as it wasn't the right long-term match for her needs, and she is looking for a new home that understands her and can give her the life she deserves.

Helga generally mixes well with other dogs, but she can be quite selective about who she likes and can be unpredictable around certain dogs. For this reason, she will need to be the only dog in her new home, and her adopters will need previous experience with reactive dogs and an understanding of how to manage her around other dogs when out and about. She cannot live with cats or small furries and will also need to be kept on lead around birds and livestock.

When it comes to people, Helga is a complete big baby! She doesn't quite understand her size (47kg!) and loves nothing more than getting as close to you as possible, and will use your legs as her very own leaning post while she soaks up all the fuss. She has quickly become a favourite with everyone she meets and is such a lovely girl to have around. Despite her size, she has a lovely, calm temperament with people and is incredibly affectionate once she knows you.

She is an outgoing lady that would love to go on plenty of quiet adventures where she can enjoy the outdoors in peace. However, she can also be a lazy lady, and would love a home where she can enjoy being a couch potato.

Helga can live with sensible, dog-savvy older teenagers aged 13+ who understand her needs and will treat her with kindness and respect. Due to her size and strength, she can be quite strong on the lead, so any children in the home should not be responsible for walking her, as she could potentially overpower them if she reacts or becomes excited while out.

Having already lived in a home for several years, Helga understands the basics of home life and is house trained. However, her adopters should be prepared to give her a little patience and some gentle reminders while she settles back into a new routine. Moving home can be a big change, and we want Helga to have the time she needs to feel comfortable and secure again.

Helga is an amazing lady who has so much love to give. She does have some specific needs, but for the right person who understands her and is experienced with reactive dogs, she could be a wonderful companion. She just needs someone willing to look past her quirks, understand what makes her tick and give her the chance to find the right forever home.

Helga has arrived overweight and is now on a diet to help her back to a healthy weight. Her back legs seem to be affected by this and she is now on joint supplements to help her joints as she continues to lose the weight.

Helga's previous adopters had her DNA tested and this came back as 46% Giant Schnauzer, 44% Caucasian Shepherd Dog, 3% Saint Bernard, 2% Black Russian Terrier & 2% German Shepherd Dog.

name: Hatty
description:
I need an experienced adult-only home where I can feel safe and loved.

I need a resident dog to help me feel safe. I've never met cats so I'm unsure!

I'm a bit of a Houdini and will need a secure garden to keep me safe.

I am too scared to go out for walks right now and will need careful introduction.

I'm still learning house training, lead walking, and other basics of home life.

I’m fully vaccinated and spayed, ready for my forever home!

30-09-26 Hatty originally came to us from a breeder, and was adopted for a period of time, and was sadly returned to our care due to her adopter becoming unwell. She managed a recent vet visit incredibly well considering how worried she can be, allowing the vet to examine her and administer her vaccinations while she was safely cuddled in her blanket. We know that the right home for Hatty is out there, and that with someone who truly understands her, she can form an incredibly special bond.Hatty is a very worried little lady who has come such a long way since arriving with us. She finds human interaction incredibly stressful and can still be very timid and defensive when she feels she is going to be handled. However, she has made some lovely progress in her foster home and is showing us that, with the right person and plenty of patience, she can learn to feel safe.

Hatty will still need a blanket to help her feel comfortable when she needs to be picked up, and she can become frightened enough to toilet herself when she is worried about being handled. Once she is safely settled, she will allow gentle strokes around her face, head and back, although she is not comfortable with her feet being touched. Her foster home has found that she is happiest when she is given plenty of space and allowed to approach things at her own pace.

Hatty absolutely loves other dogs and is particularly happy around other Dachshunds. She gets very excited to see her dog friends and enjoys being around them, so she will need a confident resident dog in her new home who can help her feel safe and show her the ropes. She enjoys having a cosy space of her own to retreat to, but also loves being able to relax on the sofa alongside the other dogs.

Hatty is very treat motivated and will happily come over for treats, which is a lovely way for her adopters to build a positive relationship with her. She is content plodding around, observing what is going on and enjoying the company of her canine friends. She can be destructive if left alone, so her adopters will need to be prepared for this and ensure she has plenty of safe things to occupy her.

Hatty will need a very special home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and understand just how frightening the world can feel for her. She will need a quiet, adult-only home with someone who is around most of the time and who can give her the time and space she needs without placing expectations on her. She will need gentle handling and continued support with things such as toilet training and lead training, although walks may not be something she becomes comfortable with.

Hatty is not going to be an easy dog to rehome, but she is a very special and frightened girl who deserves someone willing to see past her worries. With a confident canine companion, a quiet home and an adopter who can give her the time and patience she needs, we believe Hatty can continue to flourish and discover just how lovely life can be.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Jules
description:
I can live with older children, aged 16+, who understand I need time to settle in.

I will need a kind resident dog in my new home. I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I haven't tried walks just yet and will find this a bit overwhelming at the moment.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have had 32 teeth removed and will need a soft food diet.

21-09-26 Jules has come to us from a breeder to start her new adventure. She is a very nervous girl who is feeling overwhelmed by all the changes in her world. She is unsure of people and worried about being handled, so will initially run away and hide. She is a sweet girl underneath her worries, and we hope that with kindness, reassurance and time, she will slowly learn that people can be trusted.

Jules will be looking for a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience with scared ex-breeding dogs and understand that she will need to settle in completely at her own pace. We would consider a home with gentle, dog-savvy teenagers aged 16+ who can give her the space and patience she needs.

Jules will need a kind and confident resident dog in her new home to take her under their wing and help her feel safe as she adjusts to home life. Having a canine friend to learn from will be important for Jules as she begins to build her confidence and discover that the world isn't such a scary place.

Jules has never lived in a home before, so she will need kind and patient adopters as she learns all about home life and new skills like house training. She will also need to learn about walking on a lead and harness, starting with gentle practice around the garden and gradually building her confidence.

Jules is a sweet girl who has so much potential, and in the right home, we hope she will truly thrive. With patience, understanding and the support of a confident canine companion, she can begin to feel safe and discover just how wonderful life can be.

Our vets have noted that Jules has ectropion affecting her lower eyelids, which has been assessed but required no treatment. She has had 32 teeth removed at the time of her spay and will need a soft food diet moving forwards.

Jules has been given the Gift of Life by Susan Stacey

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. Every sponsorship helps us rescue and save more dogs in desperate need. If you would like to become part of a rescue story, please consider donating to our Gift of Life fund.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Pop
description:
I can live with older, dog-savvy kids aged 13+ who love cuddles, and are active!

I will need to be the only pet in my new home, so all of the attention is on me!

I would like a secure garden where I can have plenty of play time!

I am very active and will need a home that will take me on plenty of adventures!

I may have previously lived in a home, so I may already know the basics.

I have been spayed and am ready to find my forever home!

Pop is a fantastic little lady who has come to us from a breeder, although we have been told she has lived in a home previously. She knows her name and responds to “Pop”, so her new family will need to keep this name.

Pop is full of love, character and energy. She can be a little timid when first meeting new people, but it doesn't take her long to warm up. Once she knows you, she absolutely loves cuddles, enjoys giving kisses and thrives on human company. She has a very affectionate nature and loves being involved in whatever her people are doing.

As an active Jack Russell Terrier x Collie, Pop is looking for a home that can provide plenty of physical exercise and mental enrichment to keep her clever little brain busy. She is a quick learner who has mastered “sit” and is currently learning “touch”. She picks things up quickly, which is helping with her ongoing muzzle training.

Pop walks beautifully on her harness and would happily walk for miles, so she will need an active home that enjoys getting out and about and helping her learn new things. She is doing well with her training and is now walking alongside calm dogs, which is lovely progress. However, she is not yet comfortable wearing a muzzle for long periods, and we are continuing to build her confidence with this gradually. The aim is to help her become comfortable wearing one when needed, so she can be kept safe around other dogs in busier areas in the future. At the rescue, under supervision with her surroundings managed, she is enjoying muzzle free play time with Lassie so it is possible she will not always need a muzzle for mixing with her canine friends.

Pop will need to be the only dog in her new home. Although she is making progress with carefully managed walks alongside calm dogs, she can still become reactive when she feels overwhelmed. Her adopters will need to be experienced, understanding and committed to continuing her positive, reward-based training to help her feel more comfortable around dogs when out and about.

As Pop has previously lived in a home, we think she is likely to know many of the basics, although she may need a few reminders as she settles into a new routine. She could live with sensible, dog-savvy children aged 13 years and over but will need a home without cats.

Pop is a wonderful little dog with so much love to give. With patient, experienced adopters who can provide the active lifestyle, ongoing training and consistency she needs, she will make a fantastic, loyal and loving companion.

Pop has been making really good progress and has even made a friend here that she mixes with unmuzzled, she seems to enjoy a little bit of a play but then needs to have a little pause during some play dates when her friend gets a little bit too playful and overwhelms her. After a couple of minute of calm she will happily play again but it's important that her new people don't rush her with her socialisation, and instead, just take it at a pace that Pop is happy and comfortable with. She is very good at communicating when she's feeling a bit overwhelmed so you just have to listen to her and take her out of the stressful situation.

We are still muzzle training her to help her with her doggy social skills, this is very much a work-in-progress as we want her to be 100% happy with one step before moving on to the next, but I am very proud of her for reaching the stage of putting her nose in on queue and holding it there for a few seconds before getting more tasty paste.

In general she is such a happy ball of energy who just wants someone who will take her on adventures and truly be her best friend.

Pop can be homed with dog-savvy teens but they must be understanding of her getting a little mouthy when over-excited and although this is something that she is improving on, we don't want her new adopters to be worried by this behaviour if it were to happen in the home. We ignore it and reward her for being calm, which is all it usually takes for her to stop and then we continue with something fun, she also will usually grab a toy when excited in her kennel, so we are in the process of teaching her to do this on command to help her know where to place all that excited energy safely.

I can see her making a family incredibly happy, she really does have so much to offer the right home.

Pops is such a beautiful, smart girl who is super friendly with people. She has just mastered "sit" and is currently learning "touch". She picks things up pretty quickly, which is also helping her with her muzzle training.

Pops isn't sociable with other dogs currently, but this is something we're working on by taking her on walks with calm dogs at a distance. Once she is happily muzzle trained, we will work up to safe mixes with dogs who are a good match.

She does need to be an only dog in the home, and her people will need to keep up the training we've put in place to help her feel more comfortable around other dogs when out and about in public.

She walks absolutely beautifully on her harness and would happily walk for miles and miles, so she will need an active home who enjoys helping their dog feel happier and learn new things.

Pop is a fantastic little lady who has come to us from a breeder, although we have been told she has lived in a home previously. She knows her name and responds to "Pop", so her new family will need to keep this name.

Pop is a wonderful little girl who is full of love, character and energy. She can be a little timid when first meeting new people, but it doesn't take her long to warm up. Once she knows you, she absolutely loves cuddles, enjoys giving kisses and thrives on human company. She has a very affectionate, sweet nature and loves being involved in whatever her people are doing.

As an active Jack Russell Terrier x Collie, Pop is looking for a home that can provide plenty of physical exercise as well as mental enrichment to keep her clever little brain busy. She is doing well with her lead walking and enjoys getting out and about, but she will need owners who are committed to continuing her training and helping her build confidence.

Pop will need to be the only dog in her new home. Whilst she can walk past some dogs, she is worried by them and can become reactive on lead, making the wrong choices when she feels overwhelmed. Her adopters will need to be experienced, understanding and willing to continue working on her doggy social skills using positive, reward-based training. We have already started muzzle training with Pop to help build her confidence, with the hope that, in time, she may be able to enjoy controlled walks alongside calm canine companions.

As Pop has previously lived in a home, we think she is likely to know many of the basics, although she may need a few reminders as she settles into a new routine.

She could live with sensible, dog-savvy children aged 13 years and over but will need a home without cats.

Pop is a truly wonderful little dog with so much love to give. With patient, experienced adopters who can provide the active lifestyle and ongoing training she needs, she will make a fantastic, loyal and loving companion.

name: Gigi
description:
I will need an adult-only home that understands me.

I need a resident dog Cocker Spaniel size or larger to be my friend.

I would like a secure garden with 6ft+ fences.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have been spayed & am ready for my forever home!

Gigi is a very worried lady who has come to us from a breeder. When she first arrived, she was terrified of people and would try to escape any area she was in if she thought someone might approach her. Thankfully, she has made lovely progress and is now much more relaxed around the carers she knows. She has settled into her routine and will even come over for little sniffs when her kennel friends approach for attention. She is also much easier to handle now and, when worried, will retreat to her safe corner rather than trying to flee.

Despite her progress, Gigi remains a flight risk and her safety must always be a priority. Her adopters will need to be very safety-conscious and have a very secure garden with fencing at least 6ft high. Moving to a new environment may cause her confidence to regress, so precautions will be essential to keep her safe. We hope to begin harness training with her, but this will need to be introduced slowly and carefully. Double-leading will be absolutely essential for a long time to come.

Gigi absolutely loves other dogs and is delighted to meet them, wanting to be friends with everyone! She will need a kind, confident resident dog who genuinely enjoys canine company and can take her under their wing, helping her feel secure and guiding her through the different aspects of home life. She will need this dog to be Cocker Spaniel sized or larger and cannot be homed with smaller dogs.

As Gigi has never lived in a home before, she will need patient adopters who can help her learn about house training, lead walking and all the new experiences that come with being a much-loved pet. She needs an adult-only home with experience of ex-breeding dogs, where her fears are understood and she is given the time, space and reassurance she needs to settle at her own pace.

Gigi has come a long way already, and with the right home, a loving canine companion and plenty of time and patience, we believe she has the potential to continue blossoming. Her new family must be prepared to put in as much time and effort as she needs, taking everything slowly and steadily so she can learn that life can be a wonderful place to be.

Gigi has been given the Gift of Life by Rachel Morris

When Gigi was first moved in to her current section she was terrified, she would try to jump out of any area she was in if she felt a human may be getting near to her, now she has settled into the routine and knows the carers of the section well, she is far more relaxed with them, even coming up for little sniffs when her kennel friends do. She is much easier to handle now too and will freeze in her safe corner in her kennel rather than trying to flee.

Despite the progress she has made her new adopters will be very safety conscious with a very secure garden to ensure that if she were to regress when brought in to a new environment she would always still be safe. We feel that with the progress she has made we can now start to harness train her, this will be a slow process always keeping her safety at the forefront of our minds and double leading her will be absolutely essential for a long time to come.

Gigi loves other dogs, any dog she meets makes her very happy and she truly wants to be a friend to them all, so she will need a resident dog who actively loves having a companion and will really take her under their wing and help to guide her through all aspects of home life.

In the right home she will thrive but her new humans will need to be prepared to put in as much time, effort and patience as she needs and to take it slow and steady so she truly learns to see that life is actually pretty good after all.

Gigi is a very worried lady who has come to us from a breeder and is understandably very nervous and uncomfortable around people. She can be considered a flight risk as she will do her best to get away when she feels worried, so she will need very slow and gentle introductions to the world around her.

Gigi is going to need lots of TLC, patience and understanding from her new family as she learns that she is safe and begins to build her confidence. She will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home who she can look to and lean on for reassurance as she settles in.

Gigi has never lived in a home before, so her adopters will need to be patient and understanding as she learns about house training and walking on a lead. These things may take some time, and she will need a family who is happy to let her progress at her own pace. She will need a very secure garden with fences 6ft+.

Gigi will need an adult-only home with ex-breeding experience, where her needs can be understood and she can receive the patience and reassurance she deserves. With time, love and the support of a confident canine companion, we hope Gigi will slowly learn to trust and become the happy, active girl we know she can be.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Criss Cross
description:
I need an adult-only experienced home that understands me.

I'd prefer to be the only dog in the home and no cats please!

I’m still shy, so I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I can now walk on a lead and harness and enjoy my walks.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I am neutered and ready to find my forever home!

Meet Criss Cross, a big-hearted, sensitive lad who has come to us from a breeder and is slowly learning to find his confidence in the world. When Criss Cross arrived as a worried soul, needing extra patience, understanding, and gentle care. He had very little formal handling in his past, and early on could be grumbly or anxious when unsure. He required slow, careful introductions to people, places, and experiences while he started to understand his new surroundings.

While Criss Cross can still be a little shy when meeting new people, once he feels comfortable his affectionate side really shines through. He actively seeks out fuss and cuddles and has become quite the cuddle bug, often trying to return kisses to the people he trusts. He is learning his manners well and responds nicely to calm, consistent guidance.

Criss Cross is growing in confidence with his harness training and now enjoys daily walks beyond the rescue. He has even started greeting some people on his walks for a hello and perhaps a treat or a fuss. He can still feel a little unsure if people are behind him, but gentle encouragement and reassurance help him relax and continue exploring the world around him.

He has also started learning about kennel cleanliness, with staff helping him practice good toilet habits to make the transition into a home life easier for him in the future. When enjoying some quiet time on his own, Criss Cross loves exploring his toy collection, especially anything involving treats or food puzzles.

Criss Cross would prefer to be the only dog in the home so he can fully relax and enjoy all the attention for himself.

He will need a calm, adult-only home with experienced adopters who can continue helping him build confidence at his own pace. He also appreciates having a quiet space at mealtimes where he feels safe and secure. Criss Cross will need a home without cats as he is overly interested in them.

Criss Cross is a truly gorgeous, sweet-natured gentle giant with so much love to give. With patience, understanding, endless bum scratches and plenty of tasty treats, he has every chance to flourish into the loyal and devoted companion he is meant to be.

Criss Crosswill need more than one meet and greet with his prospective adopters to allow him time to build a bond and feel comfortable with them before being adopted.

Criss Cross is the most sensitive soul who is easily affected by life and it breaks my heart, he's looking for a very special human who would take him under their wing and give him all that he needs to thrive and cope with how scary the world can be. Whilst his best friend Crumble has been on kennel rest Criss Cross has really been struggling to be brave enough to go for road walks, he's only felt comfortable walking around the quiet field that's behind his section as he can cope with it there and he feels safe. Since Crumble has been given the go ahead to start going for little walks daily again he has been enjoying his road walks in her company. This just highlights how sensitive he is and how much he struggles in certain situations. He did go for a couple of walks with a collie but he didn't get much comfort from her company so didn't really enjoy them.I know he needs a very specific person who will love him exactly for who he is and who has the right set up to help him have a truly wonderful life as he deserves. I just hope they're out there somewhere looking for a big bundle of love who just needs some understanding to be able to help his cheeky and funny personality shine through.

Criss Cross has been doing very well socialising with other dogs, he walks politely next to calm dogs and even had a muzzled play date the other day. His best friend Crumble is currently on kennel rest, so he only gets to see her very briefly whilst on lead, but he always runs to the front of her kennel to say hello before going back to his own kennel.

He is such a sweet boy who adores his people once he trusts you. He just needs positive introductions to feel comfortable with new people. Very proud of the progress he's been making and we'll continue to work on his doggy social skills.

Criss Cross is such a sweetheart! He is loyal to his friend Crumble, his kennel mums and dads. He’s still greeting everyone on walks with a bit of caution but once he’s recognised you, you’re considered family.

He’s going on occasional independent walks to gain his confidence but he is always looking for Crumble to keep him company. He’s very cautious of new things however day by day his confidence is growing and with his trust in his kennel mums he always runs back to check they’re okay, showing you just how brave he is and continues to be, so when the right home finds him….they will have to earn his trust and give him the patience and love he truly deserves.

This distinguished gent is progressing so well, every day!

He has started to get in the practice of being kennel clean, one of his kennel mums likes to come in a little early to help him practice this so when he finds his forever home it might be a little less stressful learning toilet training skills properly.

Criss Cross is even getting more adventurous greeting people on his daily walks now just to  say hello and maybe scoring a treat or fuss, and even recognising some of the staff when they visit him.

He is protective of Crumble and always looks to see her catching up on their daily walks, and enjoys playing with her or being near watching over her. But when he has his solo kennel time, he has been exploring his personal toy collection, anything with a treat in it and he’s happy. This cuddle bug deserves a home with endless bum scratches and scrumptious treats

This handsome guy is progressing every day! And showing his kennel mums just how much of a sweetheart he is. He is an affectionate goofball once he’s comfortable with you. He enjoys playing with his chow friend Crumble and he loves getting love from her and his kennel mums. He loves to jump up to have his harness put on, refusing to stand still because he gets so excited to go out and explore with Crumble.

Criss Cross will now even allow some of his part time kennel mums and dads to give him attention too. He is still very cautious of new people but is slowly meeting new people and remembering them!

With some time his new family will find out just how special Criss Cross is!

Criss Cross has made incredible progress over the last few days. He used to hide and grumble when people approached his kennel, but this has changed massively!

Now, Criss Cross comes up to the kennel door and wags his tail, getting very excited to see people. Spending time with this handsome boy brings me so much joy; I often find myself straying from my section just to sneak in five minutes of cuddles.

Criss Cross is still looking for a quiet, gentle home and someone who will take things slow while he gets to know them.

Criss-Cross has grown into an incredibly sociable and interactive boy, although he can still be a little shy when first meeting new people. Once he feels comfortable, he actively seeks out attention and loves a cuddle, often trying to give kisses in return. Criss-Cross is a big lad and is still learning his manners; when he’s excited he can occasionally use his size to try and barge past, but he responds well to clear, firm verbal guidance.

He will need a quiet area to enjoy his meals, as this helps him feel more secure. Criss-Cross is doing very well with his harness training and has already ventured out of the rescue for walks, managing a good distance down the road. He can still feel a little unsure if people are walking behind him, and one of his endearing little quirks is that he finds reassurance if you turn and face him while walking backwards. Criss-Cross is a truly gorgeous, sweet and gentle giant who will thrive in an active, patient and understanding home.

Criss Cross is a very worried soul who has come to us from a breeder, and is needing extra patience, understanding, and tender care. He appears to have had very little formal handling in his past and can be grumbly or anxious when he feels uncomfortable. He requires slow, careful introductions and time to begin to understand the world around him.

Criss Cross would thrive in an adult-only home with experienced owners who can provide the reassurance and consistency he needs to start building trust. He is still learning the basics of house training and walking on a lead, so his adopters will need to be patient and gentle as he gradually discovers confidence. He will need an understanding and kind resident dog in the home he can look to as he continues to learn and trust.

This sweet, sensitive boy is not yet ready for the full bustle of the world, but with time, quiet encouragement, and safe garden sniffing adventures, he will slowly open up and reveal the loyal companion he can be. Criss Cross will need a calm, loving home where his cautious nature is respected and nurtured and where he can finally feel safe and truly belong.

These wonderful souls may be older, have medical needs, or come with a few unique quirks—but they have endless love to give. Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

name: Lolek
description:
Lolek is a 3.5-month-old male Cross-Breed available for adoption. He was born approximately 3.5 months ago and can travel to his new home once he reaches 4 months, depending on the development of his teeth.

Currently located in Tecuci, Romania, Lolek is part of a small breed and is eagerly waiting for a loving family to adopt him. His breed is an unknown mix, adding to his unique charm.

Lolek has been thoroughly prepared for adoption; he is vaccinated, blood tested, treated for fleas and worms, and microchipped. With rescue back up and support available in the UK, potential adopters can feel secure in their decision to bring Lolek into their home.

A home check and adoption process will apply to ensure a suitable environment for him.

Lolek and his brother, Bolek, were found abandoned on a freezing winter day, which highlights the resilience of these little pups.

A kind lady rescued them from the streets and sought help for their care, leading to their current situation where they are receiving the love and attention they deserve. Lolek is a playful sweetheart who thrives on human interaction and loves to be pampered.

He is sociable with the other dogs in the yard, indicating his friendly disposition, and is comfortable around cats as well. This sociability makes him an ideal candidate for a home with other pets.

It is estimated that Lolek will remain small when he fully grows up, making him a perfect fit for families looking for a compact companion.

name: Gia
description:
Introducing Gia! Once upon a time, on a mountain in Croatia, a beautiful dog with a poorly leg wandered aimlessly after she was hit by a car.

Despite her physical pain, no one seemed to notice her. Gia, with her gentle eyes and a spirit that refused to be broken, longed for help, and the Zarkovica team were notified and came to her aid.

Despite her hardships, Gia harboured no ill will towards humans. Although shy, she shows no aggression towards people.

Her leg couldn’t be saved due to the trauma she suffered during those painful times, but she has since undergone surgery to remove it and has fully recovered physically.

Gia will be happiest with another dog or dogs, as she prefers their company and gains confidence when in their presence, having lived in a huge pack for most of her life. She walks wonderfully with the team and enjoys her daily outings.

Gia is fully vaccinated, blood tested, flea and worm treated, microchipped, and spayed. She will travel on approved transport with her very own passport directly to her new home.

The application and checks apply through RBU – Meadow of Hope Dog Rescue.

name: Golda
description:
Golda is a 10-year-old female Cross-Breed with a heart as pure as gold. She has spent much of her life navigating the streets, demonstrating remarkable resilience and strength. Despite her difficult past, she remains a gentle and shy soul, always radiating a quiet charm that makes her truly special.

Golda prefers a peaceful environment over a busy, bustling one. She is the kind of dog who would rather curl up by your side than run around in a crowded park. Her calm and patient nature makes her a wonderful companion for those who appreciate a serene and soothing presence at home.

Although she has seen many challenges in life, Golda remains full of love to give. She has a sweet and endearing personality that will bring warmth to any home. She is well-behaved and content with a simple life, making her a perfect match for someone looking for a low-energy, loving companion.

Golda gets along well with other dogs and can live harmoniously with cats. However, she would be best suited to an adult-only home, where she can enjoy a quiet and relaxed environment.

Having already been vaccinated, blood-tested, flea and worm treated, microchipped, and spayed, Golda is ready to find her forever home.

If you’re looking for a loyal and affectionate companion to share peaceful moments with, Golda is the perfect choice. She is waiting for a special person to give her the love and security she truly deserves.

Adopt Golda and let her spend her golden years surrounded by warmth, care, and unconditional love.

name: Viva
description:
Viva is an 8-year-old female cross breed dog currently looking for a foster home. She is a loving and loyal companion who radiates warmth and positivity.

Despite being a senior, she still has plenty of love to give and embodies the gentle, calm nature that makes older dogs such wonderful companions.

Viva is friendly with both dogs and cats, making her a great addition to a multi-pet household. She is fully vaccinated, blood tested, flea and worm treated, microchipped, and spayed.

Her travel costs from Croatia to the UK are covered by the voluntary organisation, and she is available through Meadow of Hope Dog Rescue.

If you are looking for a devoted friend and a sweet, affectionate dog to brighten your home, fostering Viva could be a truly rewarding experience.

name: Blossom
description:
Blossom is a 5-year-old female Cross-Breed who will turn 6 in December. She is a medium-sized dog currently located in Romania, waiting for her forever home through Meadow of Hope Dog Rescue UK.

Fully vaccinated, blood tested, flea and worm treated, microchipped, and spayed, Blossom is well-prepared for her next chapter in a loving home.

With a heart full of love and an eagerness to please, Blossom’s friendly demeanour makes her a joy to be around. She has a naturally gentle and calm personality, making her an excellent companion for peaceful and cosy moments at home.

Whether it’s a movie night on the sofa or a quiet evening with a book, she’ll happily be by your side, soaking up all the affection she can get.

Loyalty is one of Blossom’s greatest strengths. She is the kind of dog who will stand by her family through thick and thin, offering unwavering companionship.

Her affectionate nature means she thrives on human interaction and loves to cuddle. Anyone looking for a devoted and loving pet will find the perfect match in Blossom.

Blossom is dog-friendly and has already been lead-trained, making her an easy companion for walks and outdoor adventures. She can also be cat-tested upon request for potential adopters with feline family members.

Given her gentle and social nature, she would make a wonderful addition to the right home, bringing warmth, joy, and unconditional love.

name: Rio
description:
Meet Rio: Rio is a 3 1/2 year old male Siberian Husky currently located in Croatia and available for adoption.

Sadly, he never had a real home. Life in a derelict box, without going out, we can’t call home, nor is it the life that any creature deserves. We cannot change the past, but we can guarantee a wonderful future.

Rio is a cheerful dog, full of life and desire for adventure. He is not trained to live in a home, and we are looking for a home with a fenced garden so that he can slowly get used to entering inside. He rejoices at all people and jumps a meter high when people approach his box. He adores cats and has shared boxing with them.

Rio is vaccinated, chipped, and neutered. In other words, he is ready to start his new life with someone who will love and care for him.

If you are looking for a friend forever, Rio is here, ready to give you all his love!

name: Ljubica
description:
Ljubica is a 13 year old female Cross-Breed is a medium-sized dog weighing 21 kilograms and standing 46 cm tall. Currently located in Croatia, Ljubica has spent her entire life in a shelter and is now ready to find her forever home.

Ljubica wants a patient home where the residents won’t expect her to shower them with affection and kisses straight away. It’s clear that she has had little human affection during her incredibly difficult life.

In a retirement home, she wants the freedom to live her life at her own pace.

Ljubica has never behaved aggressively towards those who care for her. She is simply a fearful soul, and it breaks our hearts that such a lovely dog is frightened of anything in this world.

She would thrive in a household with another calm and friendly dog. Ljubica is still learning to walk on the lead and will need time and understanding to settle.

She is vaccinated, microchipped, spayed, and has her passport ready. Ljubica is looking for someone who will love and care for her in her golden years.

If you are looking for a loyal and loving friend, Ljubica is here, ready to start her new life with you.

name: Milo
description:
Milo is a 3 year old male Cross-Breed, small to medium in size, standing 33cm tall and weighing 11kg.

He was abandoned in a park in Tecuci, Romania, and was going to eat at a rescuer’s door.

After being taken in by a kind lady and her daughter, Milo struggled to fit in with their two dogs, leading them to seek help.

Today, Milo is completely integrated with the other 30 dogs in the rescue yard. He is a gorgeous, cuddly dog who loves human contact and enjoys being petted and stroked.

He is sociable with other dogs and does not show any aggression towards the rescue’s cats. Milo is castrated, vaccinated, microchipped, and dewormed, with an EU passport and a full adoption contract.

He can live, after gradual introduction, with other dogs, cats, and children. Adopting a dog is a very big decision, so please make sure you are ready for the challenge and commitment.

Are you prepared to take care of them, pay their vet bills, feed them, walk them, and consider them a family member for the rest of their life?

name: Spirit
description:
Hello there! My name’s Spirit, a 3 year old male Cross-Breed from Romania, full of life and energy.

I was rescued from a field where I was attached to a chain 24 hours a day. My fur was matted, my skin was sore, and I was crawling with fleas—it was so uncomfortable for me.

Succeeding Paragraphs (Copied and Punctuated):

Despite those awful days, weeks and years of my life, I remain forgiving and happy.

I’m super friendly with people, other dogs, and children over 10.

I love to play, run around and roll in the long grass now that I am free from those horrible chains.I currently reside in private foster in Romania under the care of NGO Andreea.

I am super excited for what the future holds for me and what adventures can be made now that I have a new lease of life.

name: Viva
description:
Viva is an 8-year-old female Cross-Breed. She is a senior lady with a heart full of love, looking for a warm and caring home to spend her golden years.

Despite a past that may not have been the kindest, she remains full of spirit and affection, ready to give and receive love.

Throughout her life, Viva has been nurturing and caring, and now it’s her turn to receive the love and attention she deserves.

She gets along wonderfully with other dogs and even cats, making her a perfect fit for a multi-pet household. Her gentle and friendly nature means she will easily become a cherished companion.

At 50 cm tall and weighing 22 kg, Viva is a medium-sized dog with a sturdy build. She may be a senior, but she still has plenty of companionship and devotion to offer.

Her loving nature and calm temperament make her an ideal dog for someone looking for a loyal and affectionate friend.

Viva is fully vaccinated, blood tested, flea and worm treated, microchipped, and spayed. She is currently in Croatia but can travel to the UK through Meadow of Hope Dog Rescue once she finds a home.

Adopting Viva means giving a second chance to a dog who truly deserves it—one who will fill your home with love and loyalty.

name: Vigo
description:
Vigo is a 12.5-year-old male Chow-Croatian cross looking for a loving home to spend his golden years.

Despite his age, he still has a zest for life and enjoys walks, water, and curling up on the sofa after a day of adventure.

He is a well-mannered and affectionate boy, great with people, dogs, and cats, making him a fantastic addition to any family home.

Vigo is well-trained, walks perfectly on a lead, and is eager to please, ensuring he will settle into a new home with ease.

Fully vaccinated, blood tested, neutered, flea and worm treated, and microchipped, Vigo is ready to travel to the UK in March via Meadow of Hope Dog Rescue.

If you’re looking for a loyal, loving companion, Vigo could be the perfect match.

name: Lora
description:
Lora is a 6 month old female Cross-Breed. Lora has been through a lot in her life. As a four-month-old puppy, she ended up in a shelter because her previous owners couldn’t understand her playfulness, curiosity, and puppy testing of boundaries.

She didn’t immediately know the rules of house order, and nibbling on the couch was just one of her awkward actions.

Despite all this, Lora quickly won the hearts of many, and after several successful photoshoots, she found a home that gave her love and patience, teaching her the rules and giving her a safe place to live.

However, the circumstances changed and Lora ended up in the shelter again. Now, after all she has been through, she is looking for her forever home for the third time.

Lora is 6 months old, vaccinated and chipped, soon to be neutered and still believes that she will find the right family that will love her for who she is – playful, a little mischievous, but with a full heart.

If you’re ready to give Lora all she needs and love her for the rest of her life, please consider her.

Lora is waiting for her forever home! Rbu – meadowofhopedogrecue Application and checks apply.

name: Lina
description:
Lina is a beautiful female dog who, unfortunately, was abandoned on the street in Croatia.

Although she may appear older at first glance, Lina is estimated by the vet to be only 5 years old.

She is extremely friendly and gets along well with other dogs.

She is always ready to play, but above all, she craves human touch.

Lina walks perfectly on the leash and thoroughly enjoys exploring away from her kennel. Lina isn’t accustomed to living with cats or small children – older teenage children – no small furries.

If you’re looking for a loyal companion who will shower you with love, Lina is the perfect choice.

She is healthy with no known allergies or intolerances.

name: Lonely
description:
Lonely is a 6 year old male Cross-Breed. Lonely is a dog who came from the Žarkovica shelter in Croatia, where he was fearful and mistrustful of people.

After a lot of effort, love, and care, he has transformed into a loyal and devoted companion with the team.

He now enjoys walks, gets along well with other dogs, and feels more at ease with people, but this needs continued care.

He is healthy and has learned basic commands. We are looking for a home with someone or a family who has experience with dogs, patience, and is ready to give him the safety and love he deserves.

He is 50 cm in height and 21 kg in weight, vaccinated, flea and worm treated, neutered, and blood tested.

Once a lonely dog, now transforming into a lovely boy.

name: Osman
description:
Osman is a 2-year-old male Kangal Mix currently in foster care in Croatia. He is a large and impressive dog, weighing 54kg, with a cream-coloured coat. Despite his difficult past, Osman is friendly, loyal, and social with both people and other dogs.

He was introduced to dogs in a local town and displayed no signs of aggression, making him a great companion for a multi-dog household.

Osman was rescued from terrible conditions, where he lived on a chain alongside 67 other dogs. He was severely underweight and had lost a significant amount of muscle mass due to his confinement.

Since being in the care of his rescuers, he has been steadily regaining his strength. Though he still has some muscle to build, he is making remarkable progress every day.

He recently had an outing to the city and impressed everyone he met. He was calm, friendly, and enjoyed attention from strangers. Osman also handled the car ride well, though he was a little nervous when large trucks passed by. His confidence is improving, and with time, he will continue to grow into a well-adjusted companion.

Osman is an active dog who will thrive in a home that can provide him with both physical and mental stimulation. He does need some support with lead training, as he currently pulls a bit, but with positive reinforcement, he will learn to walk nicely on a lead.

His ideal home would be with an experienced large-breed owner who understands guardian breeds.

A home in the countryside, away from heavy traffic, would suit him best. He needs an owner who is physically fit and able to handle a dog of his size.

Osman would also benefit from a spacious home and garden where he can enjoy his surroundings. He is neutered, vaccinated, microchipped, and has a passport, ready to travel to his forever home.

name: Iskra
description:
Iskra is a 2 year old female Kangal. She is calm, gentle with children, graceful, loving, and never demanding.

She was a puppy – on a chain. No walks, no play, no freedom. In July of last year, we were finally able to rescue her. From her very first day at the shelter, she showed us how beautiful her soul is.

She loves people and other dogs – and everyone loves her. She was perfect – but to many, she was simply “too big.” So she remained at the shelter for months. Iskra is calm, gentle with children, graceful, loving, and never demanding.

She has so much love for people, no matter what has been done to her. Just look how relaxed she is surrounded by unfamiliar children… Two months ago, she got the chance to move into a foster home.

And from that day on, her real life began. Iskra immediately fell in love with the sofa – and with her new housemates, whether human or animal. She lives with five other dogs, including a dominant male and female, and gets along with all of them.

She also lives peacefully with four cats. She likes every dog – big, small, old, or young. She isn’t food-aggressive. She’s clumsy and simply funny.

Iskra is perfect in the city – she walks calmly on the leash, is relaxed and balanced. She doesn’t mind when people approach her – and honestly, everyone wants to pet Iskra. And she gets along with every dog she meets.

Even though she’s still young, she doesn’t need much exercise. She enjoys calm walks and travels perfectly in the car. As you can see, Iskra loves playing with other dogs. She’s very playful, but always respectful and careful. In all her time in foster care, she hasn’t shown a single problem.

She even helped care for an extremely annoying puppy – patiently and lovingly. Iskra has waited a long time to be seen. Now we hope there’s someone out there who truly sees her.

name: Freya
description:
Freya is a 2-3-year-old female cross-breed currently residing with the team at Azil Dubrovnik in Croatia.

On Valentine’s Day, she was discovered abandoned with her puppy, Amor, in the middle of nowhere. It was a harrowing experience as Freya, understandably protective of her little one, ran in panic, taking hours to be caught.

Eventually, with enough courage, she allowed rescuers to approach and save her baby.

Her past life remains a mystery, but she’s been promised the best from now on, with hopes of finding her forever home soon.

Initially shy, Freya has a remarkably gentle and affectionate character. Despite whatever hardships she may have faced, she adores people unconditionally.

Cuddling is one of her favorite activities, and she appreciates every gentle touch she receives.

The search is on for the perfect family to give Freya the love and security she deserves, ensuring that her sad story transforms into a happy ending.

name: Dingo
description:
Meet Dingo, an adorable and cheerful dog with a heart full of love to give.

Dingo is a 2 year old medium male Cross-Breed.

Despite facing challenges during his time on the streets, Dingo has remained resilient and is now grateful to be safe and cared for. He is described as very friendly, quickly forming bonds with both humans and his furry companions.

While he may be a bit cautious at first, Dingo’s warm and sociable nature shines through once he gets to know someone. His love for running and jumping adds to his playful personality, making him an ideal companion for active individuals or families.

Dingo pledges to be the best dog in the world for whoever adopts him, promising unwavering loyalty and affection.

Dingo is a medium-sized male dog of mixed breed, born in 2022. Residing in Bosnia, he has shown positive behaviours such as being accustomed to wearing a collar, walking on a lead, and responding to his name.

Additionally, Dingo has received essential care, including vaccinations, blood tests (with good results), flea and worm treatments, neutering, and microchipping.

Dingo’s journey to find his forever home is facilitated by Rbu – Meadow Of Hope Dog Rescue UK, where potential adopters can apply and undergo necessary checks to ensure a suitable match. If you’re looking for a loyal and loving companion, Dingo might just be the perfect match for you.

Application and checks apply through Rbu – Meadow Of Hope Dog Rescue UK.

name: Ruby
description:
Ruby is a charming 3-month-old female, a petite mixed breed currently sheltered in Romania. Ruby, with her tiny frame, has already received DHPPi/RL and KC vaccinations, undergone blood testing, and is microchipped.

Despite her young age, she has been diligent about flea and worm treatments. Found alongside her sister Grace, Ruby’s journey brought her under the compassionate care of rescuer Andreea Berar.

Ruby’s behavioural history in the shelter has been promising, displaying no notable issues. However, the transition from a shelter to a home environment necessitates a unique assessment.

She is not acclimated to the comforts of home living and will need the support, time, and patience of an understanding adopter. Special attention is required for toilet and lead training, making beginner training classes a valuable investment once she has settled.

Exercise, a crucial aspect of a dog’s well-being, is approached with care for Ruby. The recommendation is to allow her a few days to explore her new home and garden before introducing harnesses and leads gradually.

The emphasis is on a gradual progression, starting with leisurely strolls along the street before undertaking a full walk. Ruby’s successful integration into her new surroundings depends on her becoming familiar with the people, sounds, scents, and sensations.

Ruby’s compatibility with other animals is outlined. She hasn’t cohabited with cats in the shelter, and while she currently lives harmoniously with other dogs, a gradual introduction to new canine companions is advised.

The food test has revealed no allergies or intolerances, and her coat, once in a compromised condition, has significantly improved with ongoing treatment. A good coat supplement and regular flea treatment are recommended for her continued well-being.

Prospective adopters are encouraged to provide Ruby with a calm home environment that offers structure and time for her to decompress from the move.

In the pursuit of providing Ruby with the loving home she deserves, Meadow of Hope Dog Rescue UK oversees the adoption process.

name: Grace
description:
Grace is a 3-month-old female dog, a small cross breed, currently residing in a private shelter in Romania. She has received her vaccinations, including DHPPi/RL and KC vaccines, and has undergone blood testing.

Grace is also microchipped and receives regular flea and worm treatments. Currently unspayed due to her age, she awaits a caring and understanding home that can support her in her development.

Grace, along with her sister Ruby, was found roaming at the side of the road and is currently under the care of rescuer Andreea Berar. While in rescue, Grace has not displayed any behavioural issues.

However, it is acknowledged that the transition from shelter to a home environment may bring about different assessments and challenges. Grace will need time, patience, and support to adjust to her new surroundings.

Specific areas requiring attention include toilet training and lead training, suggesting that she would benefit from beginner training classes with her new owner to strengthen their bond.

To facilitate a smooth transition, Grace should be given a few days to explore her new house and garden before introducing the harness and leads gradually.

It is emphasised that exercise should not be the main focus during this initial period, allowing her to acclimatise to her new environment, including people, sounds, scents, and sensations.

In terms of compatibility, Grace has lived with other dogs in the shelter, showing a positive disposition towards them. However, her interaction with cats has not been tested in the shelter environment.

Grace’s health has improved significantly since her rescue, with treatment addressing her initial coat condition. Ongoing care includes a coat supplement and regular flea treatment.

The ideal home for Grace would be calm, providing structure and time for her to decompress from the move. A secure garden with at least a 5ft boundary is recommended to ensure her safety.

For potential adopters, it’s important to note that an application and checks are mandatory. If selected, a 90-minute adoption chat and a home check will be part of the process to ensure the best match for Grace’s well-being.

name: Frank
description:
Meet Frank – A Big, Affectionate Boy Looking for His Perfect Match

Size: Large Neutering: Frank has not yet been castrated. Castration will be a requirement of his adoption contract.

Frank, 2 year old male Cross-Breed, is incredibly affectionate and thrives on human connection. He loves being close to his people, enjoying cuddles, attention and physical touch. He is happiest when he feels included and part of family life.

He is a real cuddle bug who loves belly rubs and being as close to you as physically possible when relaxing. Don’t be surprised if this big boy tries to squeeze himself right beside you – personal space isn’t really Frank’s strong point!

He is intelligent, inquisitive and has a playful streak. He can be a bit of a cheeky boy, particularly when he gets bored or finds himself without company!

He has a lovely nature and has been wonderful with children.

He is also accustomed to living alongside a family cat. Around other dogs Frank really is a very docile, gentle boy and doesn’t look for confrontation or trouble.

If anything, he can be a little sensitive when other dogs aren’t receptive to him. He is quite happy to have a little sniff and say hello before carrying on with his walk.

Walks: Frank absolutely loves getting out and about, particularly beach walks and exploring the countryside.

Dog parks: He loves the freedom of running off the lead in suitable dog parks where he can stretch his legs and enjoy himself.

Teddy bears: Frank has a real soft spot for teddy bears! He will cherish his favourite teddy until it is literally falling apart.

Chewing: He loves a good knuckle bone to get his teeth into. He has a funny habit of hiding his prized knuckles in the garden before bringing them indoors when he fancies working on them again.

Food: Frank is very food motivated – the way to his heart is definitely through his stomach!

Cuddles and belly rubs: Frank is incredibly affectionate and loves nothing more than belly rubs, fuss and physical affection.

When it’s time to relax, he wants to be as close to his favourite human as possible. He is a big cuddly shadow who loves being right beside you.

Frank has one particular challenge: he really doesn’t enjoy being left alone. This is when his mischievous side tends to come out!

When left without company, Frank’s main mischief revolves around food and kitchen cupboards. He has a talent for accessing kitchen cupboards, emptying their contents and taking items outside into the garden.

His particular targets are food cupboards and kitchen appliances such as the air fryer and toaster, which are stored inside cupboards but which he can still manage to access.

It is important to explain that Frank is not generally destructive around the home. He does not target personal belongings such as shoes, clothing or furniture.

His behaviour is very specifically focused on kitchen cupboards, food and anything he thinks might contain something interesting or edible!

This behaviour tends to happen when he is left alone and becomes unsettled. He would benefit from a home where someone is around for most of the day, alongside suitable management of food storage and kitchen appliances.

Frank is generally good travelling in the car and is happy to accompany you on adventures. However, after a journey he can sometimes experience a slightly upset stomach, so this is something worth being mindful of.

Frank is extremely food obsessed and very enthusiastic when it comes to mealtimes! He has never shown food aggression or guarding behaviour towards people.

However, given the opportunity, he will happily try his luck at helping himself to another pet’s dinner! Feeding separately or supervising mealtimes would be sensible to prevent him from helping himself to food that isn’t his.

Frank would thrive in a loving home with someone who:

Has plenty of time to spend with him and can offer companionship throughout the day.

Enjoys getting outdoors for walks, beach adventures and countryside exploring.

Understands the needs of a large, affectionate and intelligent dog.

Can provide consistency, patience and reassurance.

Is happy to have a big cuddly shadow following them around! Most importantly, Frank needs a home where he isn’t expected to spend long periods alone. Having company is a huge part of his happiness.

Frank is so much more than the challenges he experiences. He is a loving, affectionate, funny and characterful boy who has brought so much joy to our family.

He loves wholeheartedly, enjoys the simple things in life and just wants to be around his people. Making the decision to find him another home has been heartbreaking.

Our family circumstances have changed considerably, and my working commitments now mean I am working 12-hour shifts at the hospital.

Previously, I worked from home and was able to be with Frank throughout the day or take him with me when I couldn’t be at home. Sadly, that is no longer possible, and he is struggling with the change.

This decision has not been made because we don’t love him or because he is a bad dog. Quite the opposite. We recognise that his needs are no longer being met in the way they deserve to be, and we want to put his happiness and wellbeing first.

We want to find a home where he can enjoy his walks, cherish his teddy bears, work his way through his knuckle bones and, most importantly, have someone there to give him all the love and attention he deserves.

Frank isn’t looking for a perfect home, just the right one – somewhere he can be loved, understood and never feel lonely. He has so much love to give, and we desperately want his next chapter to be a happy one.

Could You Offer Frank His Forever Home? Frank is being rehomed through Saving and Rehoming Strays SCIO, registered charity SC051584.

If you feel you could offer Frank the companionship, understanding and loving home he needs, please visit: www.savingandrehomingstrays.org.

Please provide as much information as possible in your application so we can help establish whether your home is the right match for Frank. A home check and adoption donation apply.

Meet-and-greet and collection arrangements will be discussed with successful applicants. Please note that Frank has not yet been castrated, and this will be a requirement of his adoption contract.

Frank is waiting for someone to give him the time, love and company he deserves. Could that someone be you?

name: Ricky
description:
Ricky, a 1.5-year-old male with a small stature cross-breed, seeks a loving family from Romania.

His journey began with abandonment, leaving his parentage a mystery, but his resilient spirit shines bright as he searches for a home to call his own.

Despite the challenges he’s faced, Ricky’s gentle nature and affinity for companionship make him an ideal furry friend for the right family.

In his interactions with other dogs, Ricky exudes kindness and tranquility, fostering harmonious relationships with his fellow canines.

Human contact brings Ricky joy, and he readily welcomes new faces without a trace of shyness. His leash manners are commendable, as he walks with ease and enthusiasm through the shelter fields, relishing the opportunity to explore his surroundings.

While in the shelter, Ricky has had positive interactions with children, showcasing his adaptable and amiable nature in various social settings.

Though Ricky has made strides in his journey, he still requires guidance and training in certain aspects of dog ownership, such as car rides and recall.

Therefore, an ideal home for Ricky would be one that offers patience, understanding, and support as he continues to adjust to his new life.

A secure garden would provide Ricky with space for play and ongoing training, while older children would complement his temperament and energy level.

Ricky comes with a clean bill of health, having been vaccinated, blood tested, flea and worm treated, microchipped, and neutered.

With his past behind him and a bright future ahead, Ricky eagerly awaits the opportunity to bring joy and companionship to a compassionate family.

name: Eric
description:
Eric is an 8–9-year-old male Cross-Breed. This distinguished gentleman is currently living in Romania under UK rescue backup, patiently waiting for the perfect retirement home.

After years of uncertainty, he deserves a peaceful and loving home where he can finally rest his paws.

A shelter is no place for a senior dog like Eric. In his later years, what he truly needs is a warm bed, a soft blanket, and a quiet corner next to the fire.

It would be his greatest wish to find a home before the cold winter sets in. Eric dreams of spending his golden years surrounded by comfort, care, and companionship.

Health-wise, Eric is in good shape with no known medical concerns, allergies, or food intolerances. He’s a calm and gentle soul who would thrive in a relaxed environment where his humans can devote time and love to him.

A retired person or couple looking for a low-energy, affectionate companion would be ideal.

Eric would love a garden to wander around at his own pace, enjoying fresh air and short bursts of activity. He’s not suited to living with cats or small children but could share his home with a calm female dog.

Short walks, time in the garden, and plenty of naps would suit him perfectly.

His rescuers emphasise that adopting a dog like Eric requires patience, understanding, and long-term commitment. Rescue dogs may carry emotional baggage, and some can display challenging behaviours.

However, with kindness and consistency, Eric is sure to reward his adopters with unconditional love and loyalty.

name: Billy
description:
Billy is a smallish crossbreed aged around three years old. Billy fostered Norwich Norfolk.

Billy was found outside the gates of the Crivatu private shelter in Romania around a year or so ago and pretty much invited himself inside. He has lived happily there until recently joining us in the UK to look for his forever home.

Billy is a cute little “man about town” kind of guy with a lot of character. Secretly he’s quite sensitive and insecure with new people and new situations but he “styles it out” with an air of nonchalance initially.

A couple of days later when he realises he’s in safe hands he is your best and most loyal friend. Billy loves a fuss and a cuddle, he’s enjoying his walks and loving being a domestic house dog.

He is more wary of men than women and can be nervous of visitors to the house.

Billy would like an adult home environment.

He was previously adopted with a shy dog but once established, he would try to bully her and she was not brave enough to stand up to him, so he would need to be the only dog in the home or could live with a dog that would not stand for that behaviour.

He’s currently living happily with many other dogs coming and going with no issues.

name: Bandit
description:
Our extra special boy Bandit is approximately two years old and a delightful and incredibly attractive cross breed towards the bottom end of medium.

Bandit weighs just fourteen kilos and measures fifteen inches from shoulder to paw. Having been found abandoned on the streets Bandit has been our Cyprus shelter for two weeks.

Our shelter manager describes Bandit as having perfect manners and enjoys making eye contact; he would make the most marvellous family companion.

Being a low maintenance boy, Bandit is included to blend with the crowd and socialises beautifully.

His personality shines bright with kindness, gentility and calmness. Bandit is stunningly attractive with array of tan in his glorious coat and his eyes shine.

Such a good looking and handsome boy. A readymade adoption candidate for an extremely lucky family.

Bandit walks nicely on his lead and enjoys his time in the car. He seems to mix perfectly well with other dogs, cats and children.

name: Lucy
description:
Lucy is a 6-year-old female Cross-Breed. She’s a big-hearted, lovable soul who has already been through quite a journey. Rescued from Breasta Public Shelter in April 2023, Lucy was one of the lucky ones pulled to safety just in time.

Now she’s living in a secure shelter in Romania, waiting for her forever home through Meadow of Hope Dog Rescue UK.

Lucy is friendly with people, dogs, and even cats. Despite not currently living with them, she shows good social skills and an easygoing nature that makes her a joy to be around.

She enjoys human contact, happily accepting strokes and affection from those she trusts.

At the shelter, Lucy has made friends with the smaller dogs and gets along well with them. Although she’s larger in size, she’s gentle and well-balanced, showing patience and calmness around others.

Lucy is still learning lead training and needs a bit of extra support with her house training, but her sweet temperament and willingness to learn make her a wonderful candidate for a loving family.

This beautiful girl has a calm, relaxed nature that’s hard not to fall for. Once settled into her forever home, Lucy is sure to repay all the love and kindness shown to her with loyalty, affection, and lifelong friendship.

Whoever adopts Lucy will truly be gaining a best friend for life.

name: Maudy
description:
Maudy is a 1 year old female Cross-Breed.

This happy little girl is ready to find a family of her own, and we think she is going to bring so much joy to the lucky people who welcome her home.

Maudy is a cheerful, friendly girl who loves people and gets on well with other dogs. She has a lovely nature and is a real delight to be around.

Now all she needs is someone to give her the chance to discover just how wonderful life in a loving home can be.

Maudy was found with a broken leg, but thankfully this has been successfully repaired and she has no ongoing issues from her injury.

She has been through a lot, but she hasn’t lost her happy spirit, and now it is time for her next chapter.

Maudy hasn’t yet experienced life in a home, so her new family will need to be patient and help her learn all the little things that many dogs take for granted.

She will need support with basic house training and getting used to household routines.

She has started walking on a lead, but she will need continued training and encouragement to build her confidence and skills. A secure garden will be essential.

Maudy needs time to settle into her new home, get to know her family and become comfortable in her surroundings before gradually venturing out on walks. She is cat-friendly.

There is no need to rush her; the important thing is to help her feel safe and secure as she learns about her new world.

Maudy could potentially live with sensible children, preferably older ones who understand how to behave kindly and respectfully around a dog.

She could also live with another friendly, compatible dog.

A happy, friendly girl who enjoys people and other dogs.

Spayed, vaccinated and has her pet passport. Her previously broken leg has been repaired, with no ongoing issues.

A secure garden and a family willing to help her settle.

Patience with house training, lead skills and all the new experiences of home life.

Maudy is a delightful little girl with so much love and happiness to share. She doesn’t need a perfect home or a family who knows everything already; she needs people who will give her time, kindness and the opportunity to learn at her own pace.

Could you be the family who helps Maudy begin her wonderful new life?

name: Bradley
description:
Meet the extremely handsome 4 year old male Cross-Breed Bradley.

This wonderful boy is ready for lots of fun with his new family.

Bradley is definitely the best furry friend you’ve been looking for.

A bouncy, cheeky, happy lad 4 Years old large size bundle of love.

He is more than ready to finally travel to his forever home.

Bradley loves water balls and running around the shelter playground. A fabulous boy who will keep you on your toes with endless hours of fun.

Bradley loves people very much and will let you throw his ball for hours. A active home is definitely needed for Bradley who have time and energy.

He walks wonderful on lead and is looking forward to lots of adventures in his new home ? No small children in his home due to his very bouncy nature.

Bradley is fully vaccinated, microchipped, flea and worm treated, neutered, brucellosis and leishmania tested, and vet checked.

Bradley currently resides in Bosnia under the care of Azil Danica 48hr quarantine in the U.K. for Bosnian dogs.

Rbu in the U.K. – Meadow Of Hope Dog Rescue UK Application and checks apply.

Let’s help make Bradley’s dreams come true.

name: Cosmo
description:
Cosmo is a 3-year-old male Cross-Breed. He comes across as upbeat and full of charm, carrying himself with a touch more confidence than his sister Nova.

He already shows the kind of gentle personality that makes people warm up to him fast.

Cosmo is currently staying in a private shelter in Romania, waiting for his chance to make the trip to the UK.

He shares a tight bond with Nova, and the two of them move through life like a little ready-made family.

Anyone thinking about adopting a pair would find these siblings a seriously wholesome match.

Cosmo has a small scar on his nose, but it doesn’t dim his sweetness in the slightest. He’s vaccinated, blood tested, and spayed, making him all set for a smooth transition into a forever home.

Pennypaws Rescue will be there with full rescue backup and support, along with a required video home check to make sure everything’s a good fit.

name: Tally
description:
Beautiful Tally is a 5 year old female American Bulldog, who experienced untold traumas before arriving in the care of the One Wish Dog Foundation. Tally is currently in foster in Oxfordshire.

Before being found by the dog warden, Tally had been moved from pillar to post, being relentlessly bred from before being left to starve in a filthy drug den.

Riddled with mange and dangerously skinny, Tally’s eyes were almost completely closed up from swelling and she had lost most of her fur from infections. Her back legs were also stiff and sore from emaciation, and being kept in a cage with no freedom and exercise.

If you’re following Tally’s journey on our social media pages, you’ll know that this special girl is now recovering from her traumas in a lovely, cosy home and she has made an incredible transformation thanks to expert medical advice and treatment.

You’ll notice from her photos how much better she is looking and feeling now.

Tally is now vaccinated and once she is fully back to health, she will also be spayed. No more pups for this poor darling, we dread to think how many litters she was forced to have.

What is most amazing about Tally is how, despite everything she has been put through by humans, she refuses to lose faith in us.

She looks to us for safety and comfort, and she is so, so gentle and trusting. She’s quite simply incredible and we’re totally committed to finding her happy ever after.?
