Penny is very much a people dog, and she is never happier than when she has her human friends right by her side. She absolutely loves enjoying a fuss, a good cuddle, and all the attention that comes with it.

She is also highly motivated by food and treats, which she takes with beautiful, very gentle manners.

When it comes to outings, Penny loves going for a walk. She can pull a little bit at the very beginning with the pure joy of going out, but she soon settles down nicely and walks well by your side.

Penny could potentially live with a male, neutered canine companion depending on successful introductions, and she could also share her home with older children. She is simply looking for an understanding home where she can finally feel safe and secure.

If this beautiful girl has caught your eye, we would love to hear from you.

name: Nusha
description:
Nusha – The Softest Little Bear With a Tender Heart

Nusha is a Ukraine war dog in need of a safe haven. Available under a foster-to-adopt. Expected arrival: 19 December.

Meet Nusha – a 7-month-old lower-medium girl, the gentlest and calmest of her siblings. With her soft “teddy bear” coat, her sweet eyes, and her quiet, delicate nature, she brings peace and warmth everywhere she goes.

Sensitive, affectionate, and beautifully mild-mannered, Nusha is ready to bloom in a safe, loving home.

HighlightsSIZE: Currently Lower-medium 45 cm/15 kg, still growing (below the knee; will gain little more height/weight)SPAYED: YesCHARACTER: Soft-hearted • Calm • Affectionate • GentleDOGS: Friendly, playful, needs canine companyCATS: Not testedCHILDREN: Good with older, gentle kids 8+

Rescue StoryNusha and her siblings, Lord and Lisa, were found abandoned as tiny puppies on derelict summer-house land — left with no food, no shelter, no human help. Volunteers rescued them and brought them into foster care, where they blossomed into wonderfully social, trusting young dogs.

More About NushaNusha is the calmest of the trio. She can quietly entertain herself, doesn’t bother anyone, and seeks affection with a soft, almost shy tenderness. Her coat is plush and velvety, and she absolutely melts when stroked — she freezes in bliss when touched gently.

She forms deep emotional bonds and struggles being an only dog — she needs a friendly resident dog for companionship and reassurance.

Her foster describes her beautifully:“She’s like a small teddy bear. Quiet, sweet, soft… she just wants love. She is happiest when another friendly dog is near.”

Ideal FamilyA peaceful, loving home would be perfect for Nusha. She loves walks and play, but thrives in calm environments, ideally with a friendly resident dog who can be her emotional support and playmate. She would suit adults or families with older, gentle children.

Nusha is pure tenderness — a gentle soul who wants nothing more than love, safety, and a doggy friend by her side.

Health InformationNusha is fully healthy. Spayed. Has all core vaccines done and is microchipped. All dogs are C.Brucella tested before the trip (owners will receive a licensed laboratory test certificate).

RBU, post-adoption support, and 4 weeks free PetPlan insurance provided upon adoption.

name: Luna
description:
Luna is 3 years old female Cross-Breed originally from Romania but now in Cleobury Mortimer Worcestershire.

10 to 12 kg an extremely loving and gentle girl who loves cuddles.

She is happy, puppy like and playful. House trained. Light and responsive on lead but does need some training on passing other dogs on lead not to get stressed.

Loves toys and is not destructive. Can be snappy with the bigger dogs in the house who invade her space but outside with them on walks etc she is fine.

But she is a good dog and we are looking for a home where she gets lots of attention and someone who is there for her most of the day and who can offer her a fun and intetesting life.

Good with all people. Please consider this lovely girl. Adoption fee, home check , rescue back up.

name: Kaido
description:
Kaido, a 9 month old male Shepherd Cross, was found abandoned with his siblings outside a rescue shelter in Romania.

He is playful bouncy happy and affectionate. He listens when called. A very loving friendly boy who would make a wonderful companion.

At the moment he is living in a property with a communal garden but he can be a bit wary being outside.

On walks he can be nervous of traffic and sudden noises. So Kaido needs further lead training. But Kaido is fine free running in gardens.

He is looking for a home with his own good sized enclosed garden where he can run free and enjoy going freely in and out of the garden.

Whoever adopts needs to have plenty of time for him someone who can be there most of the day as we want him to have lots of company.

Please consider this wonderful boy. Adoption fee, home check requested. rescue back up. Kaido is in Sutton, Greater London.

name: Rapunzel
description:
Rapunzel – A Shy Young Beauty Waiting for Her Fairytale Beginning

Rapunzel is a Ukraine war dog in need of a safe haven. Available under a foster-to-adopt. Expected arrival: 19 December.

Meet Rapunzel – a one-year-old lower medium girl with the grace of a young model and the soft, cautious heart of a dog who has seen little kindness in her early life.

Rescue StoryRapunzel’s world was silence, emptiness, and rejection. She wandered between overgrown paths and locked cottages, seeking scraps of kindness but finding none. For many months she lived alone among summer houses, a forgotten soul left behind when people drove away. Locals pushed her off their plots, unwanting and unwelcome, yet she never lost her gentle hope that one day someone kind would stop for her.

When rescuers finally brought her to safety, she stepped into a world she didn’t understand — where voices were soft, beds were warm, and no one chased her away.

More About RapunzelRapunzel lives in-house at her foster home and is fully housetrained. Indoors she is a calm, polite and easy dog — she doesn’t chew, doesn’t bark excessively, sleeps soundly through the night, and keeps her space clean. She finds comfort in having her own cosy corner and familiar toys, which help her feel grounded.

With people, she can be shy at first, especially with new surroundings. But once she realises she is safe, she becomes affectionate, gentle and incredibly sweet. She enjoys curling up close, happily shares the sofa or even the bed, and forms a deep bond with those who treat her kindly.

She is cautious in busy places or around traffic, but walks comfortably and confidently in quieter, familiar areas. Rapunzel needs time, patience and reassurance — and in exchange she gives heart-melting loyalty.

With dogs she can be selective. With smaller dogs she may test boundaries, can be bossy and dominant, while with dogs her size or larger, she becomes soft, submissive and even a little flirtatious. She currently lives with cats and simply ignores them.

Ideal FamilyRapunzel will flourish in a gentle, calm household in a quiet rural or semi-rural area, somewhere far from loud traffic and hectic environments. A home with a grassy secure garden will help her settle and decompress at her own pace. She is well suited to a peaceful family with older, respectful children aged 12+ who understand sensitive dogs. Rapunzel can be the only dog or live alongside a friendly calm dog of similar or larger size who won’t overwhelm her.

She is not suited for city life or very busy surroundings.

Rapunzel is a shy young beauty waiting for the soft, patient home where she can finally bloom. With kindness and time, she will reward her family with quiet affection, deep loyalty, and the joy of watching a once-forgotten dog grow into the loving companion she always wished to be.

Health InformationRapunzel is fully healthy, spayed, vaccinated and microchipped. All dogs are C.Brucella tested before travel (owners will receive a licensed laboratory test certificate).

RBU, post-adoption support, and 4 weeks free PetPlan insurance provided upon adoption.

name: Lisa
description:
Lisa – The Joyful Sunshine Girl Who Lights Up Every Room

Lisa is a Ukraine war dog in need of a safe haven. Available under a foster-to-adopt. Expected arrival: 19 December.

Meet Lisa – a 7-month-old lower-medium girl bursting with positivity, sparkle, and affection. She is the “sunshine child” of the litter — always cheerful, always ready to greet people, always full of bright, joyful energy.

With her playful heart and loving nature, she is ready to bring laughter and light to her forever family.

HighlightsSIZE: Lower-medium now 47 cm/18 kg /medium-growing (will gain 3-4 cm/kg more)SPAYED: YesCHARACTER: Playful • Happy • Sociable • Brilliantly cleverDOGS: Friendly and playfulCATS: Not testedCHILDREN: Great with older kids 8+

Rescue StoryLisa and her siblings, Lord and Nusha, were discovered abandoned on derelict summer-house grounds when they were tiny puppies. Volunteers rescued them from cold and danger, giving them the safety they desperately needed.

More About LisaLisa is pure sunshine — always happy, always open, always ready to love. She fits into any environment effortlessly and treats every new person like a friend. She absolutely adores toys — so much that even while still a bit sleepy after her spay surgery, she dragged her toy into the recovery basket with her.

She is clever, obedient, affectionate, and wonderfully sociable. She enjoys energetic play outside, but at home she settles beautifully.

Her foster says:“She’s a living spark of joy — so friendly, so clever, so open-hearted. She will suit absolutely any family.”

Ideal FamilyLisa will bloom in an active, loving home that enjoys play, walks, training, and companionship. She would thrive with a friendly resident dog who enjoys fun and games, but could also adapt as the only dog if her people are present, playful, and engaged. Gentle older children would adore her, and she would return that love tenfold.

Lisa is joy in a dog’s body — bright, affectionate, and full of life. A family who welcomes her will gain a daily dose of happiness.

Health InformationLisa is fully healthy. Spayed. Has all core vaccines done and is microchipped. All dogs are C.Brucella tested before the trip (owners will receive a licensed laboratory test certificate).

RBU, post-adoption support, and 4 weeks free PetPlan insurance provided upon adoption.

name: Benny
description:
Benny – The Gentle Hero Who Escaped the Front Line

Benny is a Ukraine war dog in need of a safe haven. Available under a foster-to-adopt. Expected arrival: 19 December.

Meet Benny – a 10-month-old medium boy whose story began in the chaos of war but is now filled with hope for a peaceful future.

With his soulful eyes, short tail, and gentle nature, he’s a picture of resilience and quiet strength. Kind, affectionate, and loyal to the core, Benny is ready to leave behind the shadows of his past and step into a life full of warmth, love, and security.

Rescue StoryBenny’s story mirrors that of his brother, Dan — both were born into a war zone. Found in a ruined house near the front line, their mother had tragically been killed by shrapnel. A kind soldier discovered the litter and took them into the trenches, caring for them amid explosions and danger.

As the puppies grew, the soldier knew he couldn’t keep them safe forever. He reached out for help, and a brave volunteer named Brian drove across the country into active conflict to bring the pups to safety.

That was the start of Benny’s second chance at life — a story written by courage and compassion.

More About BennyBenny has been living with a foster family in a peaceful countryside home, surrounded by love and nature. Well, the word “peaceful” doesn’t really describe any place in Ukraine now, as missiles and drones (see video) are reaching everywhere and already became a routine there. He’s housetrained, gentle, and eager to please.

In his familiar environment, he’s confident and affectionate — following his person, snuggling on the sofa (“a true couch bug,” as his foster calls him, when Benny refuses to go out in dark and cold), and showering them with loving devotion.

At first, Benny may be a little cautious when meeting new people or exploring new surroundings, but give him just ten minutes and his loving personality will shine through.

He’s friendly with other dogs and loves playtime, walks, and his beloved toys. Indoors, he’s calm and well-behaved; outdoors, he’s lively, curious, and joyful. He adores human touch and melts when gently stroked.

Ideal FamilyBenny would thrive in a rural or semi-rural home, away from city noise and traffic. He needs space to run, play, and explore, as well as a secure garden to enjoy his freedom safely.

He would do best with another friendly female dog for companionship and guidance. An adult home or family with older, gentle children would suit him well, especially those who appreciate dogs who enjoy both play and peaceful sofa time.

Benny has known fear but never lost his kindness. Now, he’s ready for a home where love is constant, hands are gentle, and life is steady. If you’re looking for a devoted, affectionate companion who will return every ounce of love you give — Benny could be your perfect boy.

Health InformationBenny is fully healthy. Neutered. Has all core vaccines done and is microchipped. All dogs are C.Brucella tested before travel (owners receive a licensed laboratory test certificate).

RBU, post-adoption support, and 4 weeks free PetPlan insurance provided upon adoption.

name: Dan
description:
Dan is a Ukraine war dog in need of a safe haven. Available under a foster-to-adopt. Expected arrival: 19 December.

Meet Dan – a young, medium-sized boy with a tender heart and the courage of a survivor. Just 10 months old, he’s gentle, affectionate, and sensitive — a dog who feels deeply and loves wholeheartedly.

He’s playful and loyal, yet calm and careful, watching the world with kind eyes that seem to ask only for understanding and love.

Rescue StoryDan’s life began in the middle of war. Together with his brother Benny and a few other pups, he was discovered by a kind soldier among the ruins of a bombed-out house — their mother had been killed by shrapnel. The soldier cared for them as best he could, sharing his food and shelter in the trenches.

Desperate for help, he sent out a plea online. And our partner rescue replied. But it was hard to find a transport ready to go over 1000 km to frontline to collect pups. And a brave British volunteer, Brian, stepped in and drove deep into the war zone to bring the puppies to safety.

Dan’s journey from the battlefield to the safety of foster care is nothing short of a miracle — proof that kindness still survives even in the darkest times.

More About DanNow living with a foster family in a quiet countryside home, Dan has learned to trust again. He’s fully housetrained, affectionate, and calm indoors. He loves his walks, enjoys playtime in the garden, and is very social with other dogs.

Though a little wary in new surroundings and with unfamiliar people at first, he warms up quickly when shown kindness. On his own ground, he’s alert, but outside the gate he greets everyone with cheerful curiosity.

He’s a bright boy who loves learning and thrives on positive attention. Active, loyal, and gentle — Dan is the perfect companion for someone who wants a true friend by their side.

Ideal FamilyDan will flourish in a rural or semi-rural home, away from city traffic and loud noises. He needs a garden, regular exercise, and a patient, loving family who will help him continue building confidence.

Another friendly female dog is essential to guide and reassure him, as he’s happiest with canine company. Older children (10+) would suit his calm yet playful temperament.

Dan’s story began in fear, but it can end in love. With his kind heart and loyal nature, he’s ready to give his whole soul to the people who give him a chance. Somewhere out there is a family meant just for him — could it be you?

Health InformationDan is fully healthy. Neutered. Has all core vaccines done and is microchipped. All dogs are C.Brucella tested before travel (owners receive a licensed laboratory test certificate).

RBU, post-adoption support, and 4 weeks free PetPlan insurance provided upon adoption.

name: Faith
description:
Faith – 5 year old female Spanish Mastin Cross.

Meet Faith. We rescued her about 1 year ago. She’s a wonderful, loving character who adores small children and being a treasured part of a family.

She’s about 4-5 yrs old, 65 cm floor to shoulder, and 36 kg.

Faith is a wise soul, as well as being fun. We’ve had to keep her quiet for months as she needed surgery on her back leg for a luxating patella. The surgery has been successful, but to enable it to last, she should not do strenuous exercise or rough play.

Faith loves her walks and walks beautifully on a lead, never strong, and gets along with most dogs she meets. She’s good with cats too.

She’s a very easy dog to manage and travels beautifully on the back seat of the car. She loves to be near you when you’re driving.

Faith is currently in foster kennels in West Sussex. She can be adopted anywhere in the UK – we can help to arrange transport to get her to you.

She is vaccinated, blood tested, and will have full rescue backup.

If you think that Faith might be your ideal dog, please get in touch!

name: Sky
description:
Sky is a medium English Setter, 5 years old.

Sky’s story, as with so many of our dogs, didn’t begin in the easiest way. Rescued from a hunter in Spain, she arrived at the shelter frightened, overwhelmed and unsure whether people could be trusted.

After spending some time there, one of our wonderful foster homes in Essex offered to foster her in November 2025 and that’s when her new life truly began.

While she is still naturally shy and a little sensitive, every month has brought new milestones. Watching her confidence blossom has been incredibly rewarding, and she’s now ready to find the forever home that will help her continue her journey.

Sky shares her foster home with several resident dogs, and they have been her greatest teachers. She absolutely thrives in their company and has learned that life can be fun.

One of her favourite games is playing tag with the resident English Setter – where she has gone from always being the one chased to proudly becoming the chaser herself! It’s a lovely reminder of just how far she has come.

Although Sky remains nervous around new people and unfamiliar situations, once she feels safe her affectionate nature shines through.

She loves gentle fuss and will often quietly inch closer for a cuddle. When she’s completely relaxed, she’ll happily flop onto her back, inviting you to rub her tummy, a privilege reserved for those who have earned her trust.

Like many sensitive dogs, Sky appreciates having the choice to retreat to her own safe space when she needs a little quiet time.

Giving her the freedom to move at her own pace has been key to her progress, and her future family will need to continue offering her that patience and understanding.

Sky is looking for a calm, quiet and kind home with people who won’t expect too much too soon. A confident, friendly resident dog is essential, as they will give her reassurance and confidence.

She is a truly beautiful girl, inside and out, and while she may never be the dog who greets strangers with instant enthusiasm, she will form an incredibly special bond with the people lucky enough to earn her trust.

Sky will celebrate her sixth birthday this September, and nothing would make us happier than seeing her spend it in the forever home she has waited so patiently to find.

name: Coco
description:
Coco is a 2 year old female Cross-Breed weighing 10.6kg. She is currently located in Swindon and is looking for a calm, understanding home.

Coco is an absolute sweetheart with so much love to give. She adores her people and is happiest when she’s close to them, enjoying cuddles, affection, and simply being part of family life.

She loves spending time in the garden soaking up the sunshine, enjoys her walks, and has a gentle, loving nature with those she knows and trusts.

Coco shares her home with a confident Golden Retriever, and she loves him, though her love is not always returned as he is more of an independent dog.

She takes a lot of comfort from having another dog around, so we’re looking for a home with a confident, playful resident dog who can continue to help her feel secure.

She can be left for a few hours with another dog for company but finds being completely alone much harder.

As Coco has got older, she has become more worried by strangers coming into the home and finds a busy household difficult to cope with.

With the children in her current home now growing up and friends visiting more often, it has become clear that this environment is no longer the right fit for her.

She would thrive in a calm, adult-only home with a predictable routine and few visitors, where she can feel safe and relaxed.

Out on walks, Coco can be a little unsure of unfamiliar people and dogs when on the lead, but she enjoys exploring quieter areas and has good recall in secure spaces.

Coco is looking for kind, patient adopters who will appreciate what a loving companion she is. In the right home, with another friendly dog by her side and plenty of affection from her humans, she will make a wonderfully loyal and devoted best friend.

name: Dixie
description:
Dixie is a 2 year old female medium mixed breed currently in Warwickshire. She is not yet spayed on previous veterinary advice.

Dixie is looking for a new home due to a change in her owner’s circumstances which means she is being left for long periods.

Dixie is an intelligent and active dog who enjoys outdoor environments, particularly countryside walks and time near water. She is playful and energetic, and benefits from regular physical and mental stimulation.

She forms strong bonds with her primary person but can be wary of unfamiliar people. She requires slow, structured introductions and time to build trust. Once comfortable, she is affectionate and loyal.

Dixie walks well on lead but may pull initially or when distracted by wildlife or other dogs. She enjoys the company of medium and large dogs and can play in an energetic manner. She is not suitable to live with small dogs.

She can become overwhelmed in busy environments and may show reactive behaviour towards people approaching her, particularly on lead or near the car. She has been muzzle trained and has undergone training to support her behaviour. An experienced adopter is required.

Dixie is fully housetrained and settles well in the home. She can be left for periods once settled and benefits from a calm, structured routine.

She can show guarding behaviours around food and space, so management and understanding of these behaviours will be important.

Dixie would suit an experienced, adult-only home in a quieter or rural environment. A home with other medium to large, well-balanced dogs may help her confidence.

She will require an adopter committed to ongoing training, clear boundaries and gradual confidence-building.

name: Leah
description:
Leah is a two year old female Terrier Cross who is affectionate, intelligent, and full of curiosity.

Leah didn’t have an easy start in life. As a puppy, she was kept on a balcony by an addict and only survived because kind neighbours managed to throw her food. Soon after, she was abandoned on the streets and quickly became pregnant.

Thankfully, caring neighbours stepped in and had her spayed immediately, but Leah was still struggling to cope. She would follow children around the playground, hoping someone might take her home… but no one ever did.

After a short stay in a public shelter, we took her into kennels and soon afterwards she was adopted by a lovely family. Unfortunately, we have now received the sad news that Leah needs to be rehomed as the family’s other dog is not coping with her and the current dynamics are no longer suitable.

Leah missed out on vital love and care in her early years and had to learn how to survive on the streets. Adjusting to life in a home was a big challenge, but she has come a long way. She has learned how to settle, share, play nicely and how to manage her excitement.

Leah is a funny, affectionate girl full of curiosity and intelligence. She loves mental stimulation, training games and one-to-one attention. She already knows many commands and is patient around food, waiting for instruction before eating or going through a doorway.

Walks are still very exciting for her and she can become overwhelmed in certain environments, especially around other dogs. She does have a few specific triggers that can make her reactive, but with continued support, structure and patience she has already made amazing progress and will continue to do so.

She will thrive in a calm, consistent environment where she feels safe and secure – ideally with one person or a couple who enjoy an active lifestyle and are committed to continuing her training.

Leah adores cuddles and loves to snuggle under a blanket (and occasionally dry herself off in the bedsheets!). She is an energetic, loving girl who is ready for a forever home where she can continue to grow into the best version of herself.

Leah is spayed, vaccinated, healthy and comes with full Rescue Back Up.

To apply for adoption, please complete the form on our website: https://strayswithoutborders.org.uk/adoption-process/.When contacting us, please include a phone number or a non-iCloud email address, as iCloud emails are currently bouncing and we cannot contact applicants using them.

name: Freya
description:
Meet Freya, a 3 year old female Kokoni Cross who is looking for a calm and loving home.

She was rescued as a puppy from the streets of Macedonia and is now seeking a new home due to her family experiencing a very difficult period following a serious illness, meaning they can no longer provide the stable environment she needs.

Freya is a sensitive and intelligent dog with a big personality. She is quirky, funny and very loyal once she learns to trust someone, becoming a sweet and affectionate companion who loves being close to her people.

She enjoys playing and short bursts of running, and her charming circus paws are guaranteed to make you smile.

Due to anxiety and her difficult early life, Freya needs an experienced and patient adopter who can provide calm guidance and consistency.

She can be reactive towards unfamiliar people and some dogs, and would do best in a quieter home without cats, where her confidence can continue to grow at her own pace.

Freya manages well with a mild hip condition and lives a happy, active life with sensible exercise.

She is looking for a committed home that understands sensitive dogs and is willing to give her the time and space she needs to truly flourish.

If you feel you could offer Freya the safe and loving home she deserves, please apply using the organisation’s adoption process.

When contacting them, please include a phone number or a non-icloud email address, as icloud emails are currently bouncing and they cannot contact applicants using them.

name: Toby
description:
Toby is a 4 year old Cross-Breed boy with the look of a white teddy bear and a loving heart. Toby adores women and children, though he can be cautious with men until he learns to trust.

Life hasn’t always been easy, and busy places, traffic, and car journeys can overwhelm him. But with training and patience, he’s making real progress and enjoying calm local walks.

He can be scared of people and dogs he doesn’t know, but with gentle introduction, he can come over his fears.

At home, Toby is affectionate, loves back scratches, can be left for short periods, and relaxes well. He would thrive in a quiet, patient home—ideally countryside—with older children and the companionship of a friendly female dog.

Toby is still young, playful, and full of love, waiting for someone to help him blossom into the wonderful companion he’s meant to be.

We are looking for an experienced family, who won’t mind taking it slow with him, and continuing to work on his progress.

He would love nothing more than to chill in a calm environment and have a confident canine and human friends to help him feel more secure and to play with him.

name: Luna
description:
Meet Luna, a 5-year-old female Border Collie who was adopted in the UK but was later returned due to anxiety and reactivity issues.

After spending time in rehabilitation, she now thrives at Sakima’s Sanctuary in Blackpool, where she has made remarkable progress.

Smart, healthy, and eager to learn, Luna loves agility, obedience training, and long walks.

She needs a calm, understanding adopter who can respect her space, manage her reactivity, and continue her training.

Though affectionate on her terms, she’s not a cuddle bug and prefers gentle, minimal attention.

Luna has made great strides with other dogs and now enjoys quiet walks and car rides with her trusted people.

Her ideal home is a quiet, adult-only environment, ideally as an only dog, with adopters who enjoy rural walks and mental exercises.

Luna is spayed, vaccinated, and microchipped, ready for her forever home.

name: Willow
description:
She only has a few weeks to find a home, and we are a bit desperate. Thank you.

Willow is a sweet and affectionate 6 year old female Cross-Breed dog who thrives in a calm and quiet environment. She prefers a peaceful home with minimal visitors and enjoys a steady routine.

While she can be vocal with new people, she settles well with those she trusts. If unfamiliar guests move too quickly, she may nip at their legs, so a patient and understanding adopter is ideal.

When out on walks, Willow dislikes heavy traffic and crowded areas but does well in open spaces where she can see an exit. She’s indifferent to other dogs but does not appreciate overly excitable or bouncy ones.

At home, she is a loving companion who enjoys her early bedtime at 7:30 PM and sleeps soundly through the night. She is house-trained with very few accidents, knows basic commands like “sit” and “wait,” and has a decent recall. She has become more food-motivated, which helps with training, and she absolutely loves her outdoor walks!

Willow was diagnosed with a thyroid condition about 18 months ago, for which she requires medication (we have a 2-3 months’ supply). She has also been on calming pills due to recent home renovations but is expected to manage fine without them now that things have settled.

Recently, she surprised us by doing exceptionally well in kennels, despite initial concerns. The staff adored her, which was a big win!

name: Hazel
description:
Meet Hazel, a 3 year old female Shepherd Cross who is ready for her forever home.

Hazel has made significant progress in her behaviour thanks to a dedicated foster home, but she still requires a calm, adult-only environment to continue her journey.

Hazel is a playful dog who loves her toys and enjoys cuddles. While she takes time to warm up to new people, she is loyal and intelligent, eager to show off her tricks.

As a large, active dog, she needs around two hours of exercise each day and would thrive with a confident resident dog.

The ideal home for Hazel is one with experienced owners who can provide the ongoing training she needs. A secure garden and access to quiet walking areas are essential, as she may feel anxious in busy environments.

Additionally, her new family should be prepared to help her adjust to new surroundings, as she can be nervous at first.

Hazel is spayed, microchipped, and vaccinated, with lifelong rescue backup and support available.

If you can offer her the understanding and love she deserves, please consider giving her the forever home she’s been waiting for.

To apply for adoption, please complete the form on our website: https://strayswithoutborders.org.uk/adoption-process/.When contacting us, please include a phone number or a non-iCloud email address, as iCloud emails are currently bouncing and we cannot contact applicants using them.

name: Bodie
description:
Bodie is a 2 year old male Labrador Cross currently located in Leicestershire, UK. He is urgently seeking a very special and experienced home after being unable to settle in his current environment.

Bodie is a Labrador-sized dog, weighing approximately 27kg, with a long body and legs.

Bodie had a lively start in a Macedonian rescue, playing freely with his siblings, but he has struggled to adapt to life in his current home, particularly around children and other pets.

He is a nervous boy, which can lead to reactivity toward other dogs on walks, although he improves when on a longer lead. Bodie is also nervous around visitors to the house, sometimes snapping when he feels threatened.

He is being rehomed because his adopters found him too strong and because he is not cat-friendly. Bodie would do best in a semi-rural home with a physically fit adopter who has experience working with large reactive dogs.

He should not be rehomed with cats or children but may benefit from living with a confident resident dog.

name: Dora
description:
Dora is a 3 year old female Labrador Cross. She is looking for a forever home. She is neutered, chipped, and vaccinated. She is now moved to kennels in Preesall.

Dora is a wonderful dog and has brought her owners lots of happiness. She is incredibly clever, learns commands very quickly and loves to play!

Dora is such a playful and happy girl and has her owners laughing every day with her cheeky personality.

Dora travels well in the car and is happy just sleeping when she is left at home alone. She shows can be reactive to humans when out on walks, although has made lots of progress with this recently and is becoming much more relaxed around new people and dogs.

Visitors can be managed once she knows people well, and she does form close bonds with others outside of her family who she adores!

Dora cannot be homed with young children due to her reactivity and general bounciness. She is also very fearful of cats.

Dora can sometimes guard food and spaces but again has shown much improvement with this over recent months.

Dora has excellent recall and always wants to be near her humans. She loves being outside, playing fetch and running about.

Dora’s an absolute joy, and anyone would be very lucky to have her. We are looking for a home with experienced dog owners who can manage fear reactivity and continue on her positive journey with this.

Dora likes to say hello to other dogs but would be happier being the only dog in the house. We would also prefer a calmer household in a rural/semi-rural environment for her.

name: Camila
description:
Camila is an approximately 5 year old female Cross-Breed of medium size, currently in kennels in Macedonia and hoping to find a home in the UK.

Camila is an affectionate, friendly, and social little dog with a very easy-going and loving temperament. She enjoys human company and forms bonds quickly, often seeking closeness and affection from people she meets.

She gets along very well with other dogs and is happy in their company. She has also been assessed as being comfortable around cats. Camila is suitable to live with children and is generally a playful and sociable girl.

Despite spending time in kennel conditions, Camila is still a cheerful girl, always happy to greet people warmly. She shows a bright, affectionate personality even in a stressful environment.

Camila is the type of dog who enjoys companionship and will likely thrive in a home where she can be included in daily life. She enjoys being near her people and would suit a home where she can be part of the family routine.

Camila has tested positive for leishmania but is not displaying any symptoms. Dogs with leishmania can often live long, happy lives, and the condition can usually be managed with appropriate treatment and monitoring.

She is ready to travel to the UK for adoption with full rescue support.

When contacting us, please include a phone number or a non-iCloud email address, as iCloud emails are currently bouncing and we cannot contact applicants using them.

All dogs rehomed via this rescue will be vaccinated, neutered/spayed, and microchipped. Home checks apply, and full post-adoption support is offered.

name: Goldie
description:
Goldie is a 5 year old female Cross-Breed weighing approximately 48kg and is looking for her forever home from Blackpool, UK.

Goldie spent most of her life in a multi-dog household where she was settled and familiar with her routine.

When her family’s circumstances changed significantly, including long working hours and health issues, they were no longer able to meet her needs. Her world changed quickly, and she began a difficult period of instability.

She moved through a couple of foster homes but found the changes and time alone overwhelming and struggled to settle. Because of this, she eventually moved into kennels, where she has now been for several months.

Kennel life has taken time for her to adjust to, but she is gradually learning to feel safe again. With people she knows and trusts, her personality shines through.

She forms strong bonds, seeks affection, and shows a deeply loyal and loving nature once she feels secure.

She enjoys the company of familiar kennel staff and, in those moments of trust, she becomes playful, affectionate, and eager for closeness and reassurance.

She walks well on the lead and enjoys her walks once she has built a bond with her handler.

She can be wary of unfamiliar people and needs time to build trust at her own pace.

She also shows guarding instincts around her home and people, particularly when meeting new individuals, so she will need an experienced, understanding home that can manage this calmly and safely.

Because of this, Goldie is looking for an adult-only home with a quiet, predictable environment and limited visitors, ideally in a rural or low-traffic setting.

She could potentially live with calm, friendly dogs following careful introductions, as they may help support her confidence.

Goldie is not suited to a busy household, but in the right stable and experienced home, she has every chance to build a strong, trusting bond and thrive.

Meets and greets can be arranged following a successful home check.

When contacting us, please include a phone number or a non-iCloud email address, as iCloud emails are currently bouncing and we cannot contact applicants using them.

All dogs rehomed via this rescue will be vaccinated, neutered/spayed, and microchipped. Home checks apply, and full post-adoption support is offered.

name: Molly
description:
Molly is an approximately 2 year old female Cross-Breed of medium size, currently in Blackpool and looking for either a foster placement or a permanent home.

Molly originally travelled to the UK and spent time in a foster home where she settled well and learned the basics of home life.

She lived with another dog, children, cats, and small animals, and was affectionate and well bonded with her family during this time.

When she later moved into an adoptive home, Molly struggled with the change in environment and the lack of consistent structure.

She became increasingly unsettled within the home, including behaviours such as patrolling and guarding areas of the house.

On walks, she also began to show the early development of reactivity. As the family felt unable to continue supporting her through these challenges, Molly was returned to the rescue and moved into kennels.

Since arriving in kennels, Molly has settled well and has shown a much more stable and relaxed temperament. She is friendly with everyone she meets and has shown no reactivity or redirected behaviours in the kennel environment.

She is a firm favourite with staff and is described as affectionate, sociable, and easy to handle.

It is expected that Molly will need a structured, consistent home environment going forward, with continued training, clear boundaries, and patient guidance to help her feel secure and supported. With this in place, she has the potential to thrive.

Molly is an affectionate and loving young dog who enjoys human company and forms strong bonds once settled.

She may need time to build confidence with new people due to her previous experiences, but she is willing to engage and responds well to calm handling.

She is an active dog who will require regular exercise and mental stimulation. She has good recall and walks nicely on the lead when settled.

Molly could potentially live with other dogs and has previously lived with cats and small animals, with appropriate introductions. A secure garden and a stable, predictable home environment will be important for her.

Molly is now ready for a committed home that can offer her structure, patience, and ongoing support so she can move forward confidently and safely.

When contacting us, please include a phone number or a non-iCloud email address, as iCloud emails are currently bouncing and we cannot contact applicants using them.

All dogs rehomed via this rescue will be vaccinated, neutered/spayed, and microchipped. Home checks apply, and full post-adoption support is offered.

name: Brisbane
description:
Brisbane is a young, large crossbreed aged just over 3 year old with a gentle and affectionate nature.

Brisbane is a loving and people-focused dog who forms strong bonds with his humans. He enjoys being close and will happily follow you from room to room, always wanting to be near his people.

Brisbane is a double merle and has some sensory impairments, including limited vision in one eye and reduced hearing. Despite this, he navigates his environment well and lives a happy, full life.

In the home, Brisbane is calm, clean, and well behaved. He is non-destructive, settles well, and can be left alone without issue. He adapts well to everyday life and has shown he can cope in busier environments such as shops and cafés when supported correctly.

Brisbane is dog friendly and has shown he can live alongside other dogs. He is also gentle with children, although due to his sensitivity, a home with older or dog-savvy children would be more suitable.

Brisbane can become overwhelmed in new or busy situations. When this happens, he may become overexcited and struggle to regulate himself. This is not aggression, but a response to feeling unsure, and with calm handling and structure, he settles well.

He walks nicely on the lead and responds well to guidance. With consistency and a calm approach, he continues to grow in confidence.

Brisbane would suit a patient and understanding home that can provide structure, routine, and a calm environment. He needs owners who are willing to manage introductions carefully and allow him time to decompress and feel secure.

Brisbane is a gentle, loyal dog who, in the right home, will form a deeply devoted bond and become a constant companion.

Brisbane is crate trained, clean, and quiet in his crate overnight. He is not destructive at home but does need access to chew toys to keep himself entertained.

He especially enjoys filled Kongs, raw bones, and a game of tug. While he can struggle to self-settle at times, he’s learning the concept of “quiet time” and developing an off switch.

He enjoys accompanying his foster carer to work and confidently navigates busy public spaces such as shops and town centres. Brisbane is calm in loud environments and loves interacting with people. He can be left alone without issue, often just sleeping or chewing his toys.

As a Double Merle, Brisbane comes with some genetic considerations. He can both see and hear, although his left eye, which has a starburst pupil, may have some visual limitations.

Due to his lack of pigmentation, he is sensitive to the sun and can burn easily, so he requires sun protection and careful management.

name: Dorris
description:
Dorris is a 5 year old female American Bulldog Cross with a loving and playful nature who has sadly been waiting in rescue for over 2 years.

In the home, Dorris is calm, clean, and well behaved. She is non-destructive and enjoys a quiet, settled environment where she can relax, play with her toys, and spend time with her person.

She is affectionate and enjoys both playtime and cuddles, forming a strong bond with those she trusts.

Dorris is a fun and engaging dog who brings personality and joy into the home. She is happy to entertain herself with toys or chews but equally enjoys interaction and affection from her humans.

Dorris does struggle around other dogs and will need to be the only pet in the home. Walks and environments need to be carefully managed to ensure she feels safe and comfortable.

Due to her needs, Dorris requires an experienced and understanding owner who can provide structure, calm handling, and appropriate management of her environment.

Kennel life can be particularly stressful for Dorris due to the presence of other dogs, and she is often kept in a quieter area to help reduce this stress.

Dorris would suit a calm, structured home where she can feel safe and settled. She needs an owner who will advocate for her, manage her surroundings, and allow her to live a peaceful life without unnecessary pressure.

When given the right environment, Dorris is a loving, loyal, and joyful companion who simply wants to play, cuddle, and belong.

If they have been around children, what ages were the children?

How does the dog walk on the lead?She does focus on other dogs and will lunge at them, so will need to be walked in quieter areas or exercised in a secure field on her own. When she’s on her own, she’s generally well behaved on the lead, no excessive pulling. She’s quite nosy and likes a good sniff around.

How long can the dog be left at home without issue?7 hours plus. She was left for longer periods when I had to stay at work and was absolutely fine when I got home. No destruction or accidents. My neighbour did say she barked a bit when left, so she may be sorted to shorter periods or a house without many neighbours.

Is the dog destructive at home?Not at all, she is extremely well behaved girl in the house. Fully housetrained and doesn’t chew anything she shouldn’t. She was provided with a variety of chew toys though as she constantly likes to chew or play with balls etc.

Whats are they fed?I fed her raw and she loved it

name: Angela
description:
Meet Angela — a true angel of a dog, and what’s in a name!

Angela is a 8 year old Grand Basset Griffon Vendéen.

After spending some time in a shelter, we took Angela under our wing, and she is now safely staying with one of our regular foster families in Spain.

She has settled in beautifully and is ready to find her forever home. Angela gets along very well with all the other dogs at her foster home and also tolerates cats.

She is now ready to travel, so if Angela is the dog you have been waiting for, please don’t wait too long.

Angela is approximately 8 years old, with an estimated date of birth of 1 June 2018 according to the shelter veterinarian. She is a female Grand Basset Griffon Vendéen, possibly a mix, standing approximately 46 cm tall and weighing around 18 kg.

She is house-trained, gets along well with other dogs and can live with cats. She cannot currently be tested with small children, although Griffons are generally known to interact well with children, so this would need to be considered on an individual basis.

Angela has tested negative for five Mediterranean diseases and brucellosis. She is microchipped, has an EU pet passport, is spayed, fully vaccinated and her parasite treatments are up to date.

Her new home must have a secure, fenced garden with fencing appropriate for her size, so please allow for a height of around 150 cm.

Angela has already been through enough and now deserves a loving, safe and permanent home where she can enjoy the rest of her life surrounded by people who will cherish her.

Could you be the person who gives this very special girl the happy ending she deserves?

name: Nea
description:
Beautiful Nea is an 8 year old female Podenco located in Cornwall, a tan and white, medium-sized, rough coated Podenco lady who is very sweet and calm. Nea is a happy girl, full of beans with a very excited goofy ‘smile’ for you when you get home.

She loves to run, swim and chase a ball. Very cuddly with her humans (especially first thing in the morning) and adores a belly rub. She walks nicely in her harness and enjoys swimming in rivers and the sea.

She is perfect in the home but poor Nea is looking for a change of owner because due to her uncertainly and lack of confidence, her female owner is unable to handle her properly once she meets other dogs on her walks.

Despite walking perfectly on her lead in quiet areas, she feels threatened by other dogs and so reacts. A trainer or a experienced owner used to this would be able to work with Nea and help her feel less threastened when meeting other dogs.

Maybe also a less busy environment where Nea can get her less stressful and more remote walks.

Nea hasn’t lived with young children before, but she has a nice nature with her family so we think children over 14 years.

Nea has lived with another dog in the past (and reactive dogs out are able to live happily with their own pack in a home) but it may be easier to say only dog home. Nea has lived with cats

Loves to cuddle and share love with her family, has a happy, friendly manner about her. Very cute and pretty.

Good with dogs: Only dogGood with cats: YesGood with kids: over 14 years onlyGood with people: YesLocation Cornwall

name: George
description:
Handsome George is a super-friendly, 2 year old, Staffordshire Bull Terrier lad, with an attractive, black and white coat. He is a wonderful all rounder and friendly with dogs, cats, and children over 10 due to his size.

He just adores people as most Staffies do. He loves to sidle up to you and just cuddle and enjoys the stimulation of play. Apparently he has lived short term with a cat – we are waiting on a video to publish.

Poor George was found wandering and this couple with a cat took him in short term to get him off the streets and into safety but sadly they couldn’t keep him.

George walks very well on a lead, knows some commands and ready for his new home and he stands at 46ms.A home with another dog, or no other dog is what we want for him, that can be with or without cats and older children he would love.

Loves to socialise, gets on well with other dogs, loves `people, has a happy, friendly manner about him, lived with cats.

name: Zoey
description:
Zoey is a super-friendly, sweet, affectionate cross-breed puppy girl aged just 4 months old. She has a soft, short, black and white coat, and in some of the photos you can see her with her sister Rumi, who has the same temperament and sweet nature.

They are good all rounders and love other dogs and can be tested for cats. They will both grow to be medium to larger dogs.

Zoey is a wonderful girl, who just adores people. She loves to cuddle and has such a trusting and very nice nature towards people and other dogs, so super social and positive, loves the whole world.

Zoey loves the open space in the shelter to run around and have zoomies. She is a fun baby and we are looking for a family with another friendly dog or she can be on her own if her family are working at home, and children over 9 years.

name: Chicu
description:
Chicu is a large Griffon cross, 1 year old.

Chicu is a very handsome griffon cross, given up by his hunter like most of our dogs.

Chicu is a large boy with an atheletic build. He’s very affectionate with people and adores to be around them.

He comes running when he hears his name at the shelter too, although this will be different on an exciting walk, of course!

Chicu’s ideal home would be as an only dog or with female dogs, as males can worry him a bit at the moment.

We are hoping this will improve in time but he is most comfortable around females at the moment.

Chicu has not been cat tested but can be for the right home.

Currently in Spain, transport available to the UK.

name: Sophie
description:
Pretty Sophie is a petite Breton at 10kg with a lovely gentle nature.

She is currently in a UK foster home in Camberley, Surrey.

Sophie is an affectionate, happy-go-lucky little girl who is easy-going in the home, sleeps through the night, travels beautifully in the car and has been wonderful with everyone she has met.

She is also very polite with other dogs and loves meeting humans.

Sophie has a high prey drive, particularly for cats, squirrels and birds. Her lead walking is improving although remains a work in progress, and her recall has only been tested in secure fields.

Off-lead freedom would therefore need to be introduced gradually in secure areas.

Sophie is a very sweet little dog who has lots of love and fun to give. She just needs someone who understands the needs of a young working-breed Breton and is prepared to continue her training.

Could Sophie be your next adventure buddy?

Sophie would suit an active home that understands the breed and can provide plenty of exercise, enrichment and mental stimulation. She is food motivated and would have great fun with scent work, agility or running.

Sophie could live with older, respectful children.

She could live as an only dog or with another friendly dog.

All of our dogs have an international passport (unless born in the UK) and are microchipped. They are fully vaccinated for standard diseases as well as rabies and kennel cough.

All dogs are blood tested for infectious diseases including Leishmaniasis, Dirofilaria, Ehrlichia, Babesia, Anaplasma, Lyme and Brucella canis.

All dogs, unless there are medical or behavioural reasons to not do so, will be sterilised. Sophie is spayed. Please note that we will advise medical results and treatments upon successful application.

Adoption contract and fee, homecheck and lifetime RBU (rescue back-up) apply as standard.

name: Sugus
description:
Sugus is a medium Beagle cross, 4 years old.

Sugus is a very handsome, medium-sized Beagle mix with a different story to many of the dogs we help. He was originally rescued by one of the shelters we work closely with after spending a whole year in the pound.

He was then lucky enough to find a lovely home with a kind owner, where he spent the next year and a half as part of the family.

Sadly, his owner passed away, and with no one in the family able to take him in, Sugus has found himself back at the shelter and looking for a new home.

Having previously lived in a home, Sugus is already used to the comforts of family life. He was fully toilet trained and had no issues being left home alone.

He gets on really well with the other dogs at the shelter and loves having a run around and playing with them. He’s a happy, sociable and affectionate boy who takes things in his stride, with no obvious fears.

He has a lovely, gentle nature and is good with both adults and children.

Sugus has a moderate energy level. He enjoys getting out and about, having a good run and playing with his dog friends, but he also has a calmer side and is just as happy to settle down and relax.

Sugus has previously had surgery for a disc extrusion. Thankfully, he has recovered well and is currently running around happily with the other dogs without any issues.

He doesn’t require any further veterinary treatment, although ongoing physiotherapy or hydrotherapy could be beneficial in supporting his mobility long term. He can also be cat tested for the right home.

name: Orion
description:
Orion is a large 4 year old male German Shepherd currently living in kennels in Paphos, Cyprus.

He is looking for an experienced and understanding home where he can continue to build confidence and enjoy the stable life he deserves.

Orion is fantastic with other dogs and genuinely enjoys their company, making him an excellent canine companion. His challenges are with unfamiliar people, as he can be unpredictable due to past experiences and several triggers.

He needs patient adopters who are willing to respect his boundaries and allow him time to trust.

Orion loves long walks, enjoys learning new things and forms incredibly strong bonds with the people he loves.

name: Clementine
description:
Clementine is a super-friendly, 4/5 year old, Staffordshire Bull Terrier cross lady, with an attractive, dark brindle and white coat.

She is a wonderful girl, who just adores people. She loves to lick and cuddle and has such a trusting and very nice nature towards people and other dogs.

Celementine is super social and positive and loves the whole world. Which is very surprising if you look at the video and the state she was in when saved. Someone left her like this and no one helped her for a while until the rescue took pity on her.

Clementine came to us a starving dog with a bad infection. Our vet warned us that she was unlikely to survive, but with lots of love and local free-range chicken- survive she did.

In fact, she has thrived and is now a bundle of happiness and joy. Once safe in rescue, Clementine loved the open space to run around and have zoomies.

We think she may have come from someone that had an apartment and didn’t walk her, as she just wasn’t used to open space. Now she has learnt to walk lovely on a lead.

Clementine loves being with other dogs, her best friend is a little podenco called Sydney who she shares her bed with. We have spoilt her a little and she could probably do with losing a few pounds.

We call her ‘pudding’ as she looks like a Christmas pudding with cream on the top!

Poor Clementine, all this has happened to her and it’s not her fault. She is such a loving, happy dog and would make an ideal family pet.

Clementine really is a special girl that has endured so much in her life. She has overcome everything and is now such a joy with the most unbelievable amount of love for anyone she comes into contact with.

We are looking for a family with or without another friendly dog for Clementine to play with and children no younger than 10 years, as she can be a bit clumsy. Would suit a normal family home, not out all day, with NO cats.

name: Nady
description:
This handsome-looking, young lad is Nady, a 12 month old Cross-Breed who is a very sweet and calm, medium-sized boy, with a soft, short, fawn coat. He minds his own business and loves being petted and cuddled and likes other dogs.

Nady was rescued, with his mom and his siblings, from a horrid situation. Some evil men were trying to brick the pups up into a wall as a laugh to starve them to death, so their rescuer pulled them out of that place and took them to safety.

His rescuer needs to move for her work and can no longer stay in the place she keeps her dogs and so is desperate to home them to loving homes.

Nady isn’t tested for cats and we are looking for a family with another friendly dog , if possible, to keep Nady company and play with. Children over 12 please, as Nady hasn’t been around small children.

name: Wilma
description:
Wilma is a medium-sized 2 year old female cross-breed currently living in foster care in Paphos, Cyprus.

She has overcome a difficult past without ever losing her gentle and loving nature.

Wilma is wonderful with both dogs and cats and is affectionate with everyone she meets.

She enjoys a calm home life, loves cuddles and would suit a family looking for a loyal, easy-going companion who simply wants to be loved.

name: Sunny
description:
Sunny is a medium-sized 5 year old female Pointer cross. She is currently living in foster care in Paphos, Cyprus after spending a year surviving alone on the streets.

Despite everything she has endured, Sunny is one of the gentlest dogs you could ever meet. She is quiet, affectionate and wonderful with other dogs.

Sunny is Leishmania positive and is doing exceptionally well on treatment. With routine medication and regular monitoring, she can enjoy a long, happy and normal life.

name: Nicol
description:
Nicol was rescued from a horrendous pound in poor condition however following treatment she is now in perfect health.

She is nearly 6 and a half years old and about 25kg.

She is described as a greyhound cross lady.

She is very sweet dog who is friendly with everyone.

She does still pull a bit on the lead but is obedient and gentle. She loves to be with people and loves company and may suit an older retired couple.

Nicol is currently in Cyprus looking for a home in UK.

She will be vaccinated, chipped, treated for parasites, come with her own pet passport and rescue back up from Saving Souls Animal Rescue.

name: Reyna
description:
Reyna is an eight year old female Border Collie. Reyna was given to the shelter along with her three puppies (Ares, Sena and Zeus) by a family who kept her outside her whole life.

We think she’s been chained up for most of that time and hasn’t had the chance to interact with humans much or other dogs.

Reyna arrived at the shelter very scared with many fears and insecurities.

She is improving in time and allows people to give her attention and be stroked but she will need a patient and caring home that will let her confidence grow in her own time as she is very scared of things that are new to her.

Once she is familiar with people, she’s very sweet and affectionate

Reyna is currently at the shelter we work closely with in Northern Spain.

Reyna’s Spanish passport says she’s almost 8 years old but the vet thinks she might be younger.

If you are interested in giving wonderful Reyna a home, she is available at Setter Brittany Pointer Rescue. Reyna is currently in Spain but she is ready to travel to her forever home in the UK.

name: Manos
description:
Manos is a 6-year-old male Cross-Breed with hound traits. He is a small to medium-sized dog currently in Cyprus. When he first arrived, he was very weak, but he has since recovered well and is now a playful and energetic companion.

He has a friendly and affectionate nature, making him a joy to be around.

Manos is great with other dogs, getting along perfectly with them in social settings. He is also very respectful of children, making him a suitable family pet. One of his endearing traits is his slobbery affection, which adds to his charm.

He is well-behaved on the lead and enjoys travelling, making car journeys stress-free and enjoyable.

He will be neutered soon and is expected to be ready to fly on the May flight. Before travel, he will also undergo blood testing, microchipping, and worming, ensuring he is fully prepared for his new home.

Manos will arrive with his dog passport and full rescue backup from Saving Souls Animal Rescue, guaranteeing support throughout his transition.

name: Tobby
description:
Tobby is a 2-year-old Male Pointer Cross.

Tobby is a stunning young Pointer mix who has had a tough start in life. Initially shy when meeting new people, he is gaining confidence every day and is desperate for love and affection.

He is fantastic with children and other dogs, making him a wonderful companion for a family or an individual looking for a loyal friend.

He was previously in a noisy, stressful pound, but has now moved to a home boarding facility where he enjoys running and playing with other dogs in a more relaxed environment.

Tobby is still young and deserves a fresh start in a loving home. He can live with or without another dog, but his behaviour around cats is unknown.

He will travel to the UK with full rescue backup from Saving Souls Animal Rescue. He will be neutered, vaccinated, microchipped, treated for parasites, and have his own pet passport.

name: Lucy
description:
Lucy is a 3 year old female Staffordshire Bull Terrier Cross.

Lucy came to us a few weeks ago after being rescued from a heavy chain and showing obvious signs of a recent litter and probably several others in her past.

Having given Lucy time to settle into her new routine and environment here at Sunny Shores, we felt the time was right to take her to our vet and get her blood tests, vaccinations, chip and passport sorted.

Our vet aged her at around two years of age.

Her underside is looking much better and her general condition is massively improved thanks to good quality regular food.

Once very hand shy, she handled the journey and the vet’s needles like a pro and returned to Sunny Shores for a walk and a fuss showing off her huge Staffy smile.

Lucy is now very confident around people she knows and loves a fuss and with a proper introduction she will soon adapt to new people and her new life.

name: Valentina
description:
Valentina had her freedom ride from the pound in February where she had spent two years.

She had a chip but her owner never responded to the calls.

That’s all behind her now and as you can see she is glowing!

Valentina is three years old and an English Bulldog cross. She is slight and weighs 20 kgs.

Short walks are best and she enjoys the company of male dogs her own size.

Spayed, fully vaccinated, blood tested and holding an EU passport.

Valentina is ready to travel and will be delivered to your front door.

name: Ripp
description:
A breeder surrender who is very shy but shows no sign of aggression unless pushed unnecessarily outside of his comfort zone. Why would you want to?

He needs a safe, quiet and warm home where he can mooch about inside and outside with a private enclosed garden.

When he feels safe, Ripp will reward you with so much love.

He will then feel safe enough to venture out on rural walks. This is a special boy that needs a very special person.

Ripp is ready to travel, wherever that wonderful home may be.

name: Lacey
description:
Lacey is a 1-year-old female Labrador Retriever. She is looking for an active family home where she can continue to enjoy the happy and energetic lifestyle that suits her best. Lacey has a wonderful character and loves everyone she meets.

She enjoys being out on walks and is always happy to explore with her family. One of her favourite things is spending time around water, and she especially loves lakes. She is also house trained, making her ready to settle into a home.

Lacey was rescued from the meat trade in China alongside her mum and siblings. Her mum and siblings have already found their homes in the UK, and now it is Lacey’s turn to find a loving family of her own.

She has come a long way and is ready to begin the next chapter of her life.

Lacey can live with all dogs, making her a great companion for a home with canine friends. She has not been cat tested, so it is not known whether she could live with cats. She can also live with children aged 10 years and over.

Lacey is currently living in foster care in Buckinghamshire while she waits for her forever home. She is fully vetted and ready to join the right family.

With her affectionate nature, love of people and enjoyment of outdoor adventures, Lacey is hoping to find a home where she can continue to thrive.

name: Batu
description:
Batu is a 3.5-year-old male Cross-Breed. Weighing 30kg and classed as a large dog, Batu currently lives in a shelter in Cyprus after being heartbreakingly surrendered by his previous owner.

Once living in an apartment, he’s now learning how to trust again in the noisy, unpredictable environment of a municipal shelter.

Though understandably wary at first, Batu has a heart of gold and a gentle nature that shines through once he starts to feel safe. He’s calm during vet visits, enjoys car journeys, and shows polite behaviour even when surrounded by barking, stressed-out dogs.

His composed reaction to chaotic situations is impressive and says a lot about his potential in a stable, loving home.

Batu can live with other dogs, particularly those of a similar size, or thrive as an only pet. In the shelter, he’s always curious and keen to say hello to the others, which shows his social side.

He’s already house trained from his previous home, and possibly has some basic training under his belt. Still, like all rescue dogs, he’ll benefit from ongoing support, routine, and positive reinforcement.

He would be happiest in a peaceful home that offers regular walks, space to rest, and most importantly, consistent affection. Batu deserves a second chance—not just at life, but at experiencing the kind of unconditional love and loyalty he’s more than ready to return.

name: Ntina
description:
Ntina is a 3.5 year old female Kangal Shepherd Dog. She would prefer to be the only dog in the home and can live with children over the age of 12. She is currently located in Cyprus.

Kangal Shepherd Dogs often find themselves in shelters, abandoned due to their size. We made a promise to help find them all loving homes. Here are two Kangal Shepherd Dogs who ended up in the same shelter.

Next up is Ntina. She adores people, cuddles, and attention. She is slightly bigger than Keith, weighing approximately 50 kilograms. Ntina is easy to get along with and is much loved by the shelter staff and volunteers.

She was found as a stray, and it is hard to understand how anyone could abandon a dog and leave her to fend for herself, especially a dog of her size and with her thick coat.

Temperatures of 40 degrees on the streets of Cyprus in summer could not have been easy for her.

Ntina is friendly and placid with people and children, but due to her size she will need an experienced handler, and any children in the home must be over 12 years old. She needs a home where she can enjoy plenty of cuddles as well as long walks.

Ntina needs to be the only dog, as she can be selective around other dogs. Given her temperament, she would likely be happiest as the only dog in the home.

name: Kane
description:
Welcome the handsome and friendly gentleman, Kane. Kane is a 6 year old male Black Labrador Retriever with a medium build, weighing around 20 kilograms.

Kane has been in the shelter for over a year now. His best friend, Kahu, was finally adopted last month and now Kane is left behind. They had been together for the past year so now, more than ever, Kane needs to find his happy ever after.

Kane is a good, well-rounded boy and can already respond to basic commands. He is good with dogs of all shapes and sizes and relishes the opportunity for attention and a way to burn off energy.

He is super cuddly and will be a wonderful sofa dog, but will also require decent walks and new adventures.

Kane will need ongoing basic training and some patience to help him settle into home life. He is your typical Labrador Retriever – super friendly with everyone he meets, excitable, and food-oriented.

This lovely boy will suit most home settings – all he asks for is affection, nice walks, a roof over his head, and regular meals.

We have no doubt that he will be the most wonderful companion.

Kane is located in Cyprus and, if adopted in the UK, will travel with a passport and be tested for infectious diseases. He is fully vaccinated and castrated.

name: Harper
description:
Harper is a 3 year old female Chocolate Labrador Retriever currently living in Spain and looking for her forever home due to her current owner’s ill health.

She currently lives with three cats but no children, so a home with older children would be best for her.

Harper is very boisterous and would be better suited to live with a non-dominant male dog or as the only dog in the home.

Harper was born in Spain and can travel wherever her wonderful forever home may be.

She is spayed, fully vaccinated, microchipped, has an EU passport, and has a clean bill of health.

Harper is submissive and cautious around other dogs and needs an experienced home where introductions to other dogs are carefully managed.

name: Rocky
description:
Rocky is a 2 year old male Akita and is looking for his new forever home.

What can we say about Rocky? Isn’t he just gorgeous! He is also a bit of a doofus. Rocky is only a youngster at 2 years of age and hasn’t had much training in his short life. This has meant that he’s ended up like a giant puppy.

Rocky is very strong on the lead, especially around other dogs, bobbing and weaving left and right. Once he has calmed down, he does walk better, but a new owner will need to be prepared to spend time teaching Rocky how to walk nicely so that everyone has an enjoyable walk.

Rocky is only just learning his basic commands like sit. He also gets super excited when he sees his lead and knows he’s going out for a walk.

He likes to jump up to say hello and express his gratitude for getting attention. This is something that will be worked on in our care and needs continued training in a new home.

This lad really does not know his size and will happily walk into you without even flinching; he also came to us as a stray with no history, so we are looking for a home without any children or with children over the age of 12 years who are used to being around large breeds.

We are ideally looking for a home where he can be the only dog in his home. We feel at this stage he will need all of his adopters’ attention whilst he learns his basics.

We cannot place Rocky in a home where there are cats. With the correct training, Rocky is going to make some lucky adopter a fantastic companion; he is affectionate and really enjoys the company of people and making new friends.

name: Captain
description:
Captain is a 4.5 year old, medium-sized, male, lab cross who was abandoned in Cyprus by his owner 9 months ago. We will never know his full story—maybe his family moved away, or maybe they just decided they no longer wanted him.

Whatever the reason, Captain was left behind: alone, confused, and heartbroken. The fact that this boy is so loving and affectionate towards humans is a testament to him.

Perhaps it’s because he knows exactly what he has lost and he longs to find that again. He adores being around humans and is just such a happy boy. He doesn’t deserve to be in a kennel.

Captain has shown to be selective with other dogs so needs to be the only dog. He can be fostered, fostered with a view to adopt, or simply adopted.

Everyone involved in Captain’s plight is desperate to see him happy in a home. He is one of those dogs that it is quite heartbreaking to see him stuck in a kennel for close to 24 hours a day.

Captain will of course need patience and time to settle into a home, as with any rescue dog. We think that he may be house trained, given his past, and he also walks well on the leash.

Overall, we have no doubt this boy will be the best companion and anyone who is lucky enough to have him in their lives will just adore him.

Knowing what he has lost, Captain will be one of those dogs that is eternally grateful and will give back any love you give 10-fold.

Captain is located in Cyprus and, if adopted in the UK, will travel with a passport and be tested for infectious diseases. He is fully vaccinated and castrated.

name: Josh
description:
Little Josh  – 4-month-old cross-breed boy – just under 7 kilos – to be fostered in Gloucestershire

Josh is one of six dogs I met in Spain that I want to help find their forever homes.

I have been helping the Spanish dogs at Noahsarc for 15 years. Although Starfish mainly helps UK dogs these days, Noahsarc is still very much part of the Starfish family.

I visit twice a year to spend time helping the charity and assessing a few dogs that we can bring back to the UK.

Often, these are dogs who have grown beyond the cute puppy stage or older dogs who have been overlooked. When I return next April, I really don’t want to see Jakey, Tessa, Josh and Billybob all grown up and still waiting for their families.

They are beautiful souls, all for different reasons, and far too special not to have families of their own.

Our dogs don’t arrive in the UK and get delivered to their adopters like Amazon parcels! They come into Starfish foster care first, allowing them time to decompress after their long journey.

You will meet them just as you would one of our UK dogs, with all human and furry family members involved, so we can make sure it is the right match for everyone.

So, why little Josh? Because he is such a lovely boy! If you wanted to describe him, a miniature Labrador comes to mind.

Another little soul who was thrown away like rubbish in Spain, he was lucky enough to be picked up by Noahsarc, where he has been loved and kept safe. I’m surprised he was never adopted as a young puppy.

He is a happy little soul with lots of friends he loves to play with, and he is lucky enough to sleep in the house at the centre with Keiron, the kennel manager.

Josh is a fairly confident little soul. I have been out and about with him quite a few times now, and although he is so young, he really does have an old head on his shoulders.

I have spent time with him in lots of different situations and, although naturally cautious at times for such a young dog, he handles new experiences very well, including the beach, cafés, shops and the vets.

I’ve caught most of these adventures on the videos below.

Josh is, quite simply, such a nice dog. I wouldn’t describe him as particularly high energy, although he is still young and developing.

I think he would do better with a doggy friend and someone who has the time to guide him through the rest of his puppyhood.

He has all the makings of a lovely, confident little dog.

I’m not sure what else I can say about Josh. He has never done anything wrong.

He is simply a dog who had a bad start in life, was lucky enough to find himself somewhere safe where he is loved and living his best life, but now it’s time for him to move on and find a forever family of his own.

Josh is well socialised with both people and other dogs. His current home is in a fairly remote setting, surrounded by lots of other dogs and lovely volunteers who help care for them and take them out walking.

What he hasn’t had as much opportunity to experience is everyday life out in the wider world. However, I have now taken him out and about four times, and each time he has absolutely smashed it, as you can see from the videos below.

Josh will be fully vaccinated and microchipped, and his blood tests will be completed before travelling to the UK.

He is too young to be neutered, so his adopter will be expected to arrange this once he has finished growing and maturing. He cannot be homed with an entire dog.

If you have the time, love and commitment to offer a young dog, and you’re looking for a little character who will bring plenty of fun and affection into your life, we would love to hear from you.

name: Peter
description:
Peter, 7 months old, pointer cross, medium-large boy.

Our boy Peter has been in the shelter since he was just 4 months old. He is super loving and friendly and adores people and other dogs.

He shares a yard with both male and female dogs of various sizes without issues. Equally, with children, he is keen to approach them, play, and lap up some attention – just like most puppies.

Peter is just a pup so will of course need some ongoing training, but he is already used to walking on the leash. He takes treats gently and is eager to please so we think he will be a joy to train.

Although he is a puppy, he has quite a calming energy. He will still require an active home dedicated to showing him the way in life.

Peter would be best suited to live with another doggy friend.

Overall, Peter is a joy to be around and will make the most wonderful companion for anyone lucky enough to adopt him.
