Peter can be adopted in Cyprus or in the UK. He is ready to fly. He is vaccinated and has had a full health check and blood tests for infectious diseases.

name: Jessica
description:
Jessica, pointer cross, 4.5 years old, medium/large sized girl.

Jessica is a beautiful 4.5-year-old girl who came to us as a stray from Cyprus, and she’s been winning hearts ever since.

Despite her uncertain start, she has a gentle, trusting nature and a warm, affectionate personality that shines through in everything she does.

She’s a large dog with a balanced, medium energy level—she enjoys her daily walks and exploring the world around her, but she’s just as happy to settle down and relax with her people.

Jessica has a calm and easygoing temperament, which makes her a lovely companion both indoors and out.

Jessica is wonderful with children, showing patience and kindness, and she gets along well with other dogs, happily socialising and sharing her space.

Her friendly and adaptable nature means she could fit into a variety of home environments, whether as part of a busy family or a quieter household.

After her journey, Jessica is ready for a fresh start with a loving family who can offer her stability, care, and plenty of affection. In return, she promises to be a loyal, loving companion who will bring warmth and joy to her forever home.

Jessica is located in Cyprus and, if adopted in the UK, will travel with a passport and be tested for infectious diseases. She is fully vaccinated and spayed.

name: Kabo
description:
Kabo was brought into the shelter as a stray and has been your typical pointer since the day he arrived.

Super people oriented, very loving and cuddly, likely to be a velcro dog in typical pointer fashion!

Overall, Kabo has a lovely friendly nature and will be a wonderful companion for anyone lucky enough to adopt him.

He is a gentle boy so could live with children. He also walks well on a leash. He shares his space with both male and female dogs with no issues.

Kabo is not good with cats due to his prey drive, so a home with no small furries is a must.

We expect he will have medium-high energy levels once in a home and will need decent physical and mental stimulation.

Kabo is located in Cyprus and, if adopted in the UK, will travel with a passport and has been tested for infectious diseases.

name: Conker
description:
Conker- 8 week old male Spaniel cross puppy being fostered in South Gloucestershire.

One of Six Little Bundles of Fun Looking for the Right Homes

Born 29th September 2026 – in foster with their mum in South Gloucestershire.

We believe Rosie is a Sprocker, but Dad is unknown. At five weeks old, the puppies have Spaniel colouring but are looking pretty chunky, so we really cannot say what they will grow into!

We are accepting applications now, but no puppies have been allocated to individual families yet.

Their mum, Rosie, was found as a stray in a terrible state around ten days before giving birth. She was desperately thin, with a body condition score of just 1–2 out of 9, and was suffering from eye infections.

One was so severe that her third eyelid was terribly swollen and she could hardly see out of that eye.

Despite everything she had been through, Rosie was heavily pregnant.

Thankfully, she came into Starfish care, where her eyes were treated and her foster mum, Celia, gave her the intensive one-to-one care she needed.

With nutritious food, kindness and lots of love, Rosie slowly began to regain her strength and, just as importantly, her trust in people.

By the time her puppies arrived, she was in a much better place, both physically and emotionally.

Rosie gave birth to six healthy puppies on 29th September. The birth was straightforward, and she has proved to be an amazing mum, taking everything in her stride and caring for her babies beautifully.

A huge amount of care and love has gone into giving Rosie and her puppies the best possible start. Now we need to make sure each puppy gets the very best chance of a happy, permanent home.

Although they are tiny now, we need to think about the dogs they will grow into.

Rosie is an active, working-type Spaniel, and as she has regained her strength, she has started to show more of her natural energy and enthusiasm. Dad is unknown, so we cannot be certain which characteristics the puppies will inherit.

What we do know is that these puppies could grow into intelligent, busy, active dogs who need much more than a quick walk around the park.

A secure garden where they can safely play, explore and burn off some of that puppy energy.

An active family who will enjoy involving their dog in everyday life and provide appropriate exercise, training and mental stimulation as they grow.

People who are around for much of the day, particularly while they are young, and who understand the time, patience and commitment involved in raising a puppy.

Suitable dog-owning experience, ideally with Spaniels or other active working breeds, and a realistic understanding of their needs.

A commitment to puppy classes and ongoing training, including positive socialisation, learning to settle and developing into confident, well-mannered adult dogs.

A friendly, suitable resident dog would be a lovely bonus. The puppies would enjoy having a canine companion to learn from, provided the resident dog is happy to have a little shadow following them around!

Please don’t be put off by our careful approach. It comes from experience and from wanting to get things right for these puppies for the rest of their lives.

Sadly, Spaniel rescues see far too many dogs needing new homes because their original families underestimated their energy, intelligence and training needs.

These are not dogs who will necessarily be content with a little walk before being left to entertain themselves. They need involvement, guidance, enrichment and an understanding of the dogs they are.

For this reason, we are not looking for first-time dog owners. We want homes with suitable experience, realistic expectations and the time to give a young, potentially working-breed dog the life it deserves.

We will not place the puppies in homes with entire dogs. They are too young to be neutered, and their future families must be prepared to discuss the appropriate timing with their vet and commit to neutering when they are sufficiently grown and mature.

When can the puppies go to their new homes?

The puppies are now five weeks old, so there is still some growing to do first!

At six weeks, they will visit our vet for a health check, begin their vaccinations and be microchipped. Once these checks have been completed and we are happy with their progress, we can begin matching them with their approved homes.

We are accepting applications now, and four puppies have already been reserved. Two puppies are still looking for the right homes.

Please understand that a reservation does not mean a puppy has been allocated to a particular family. We will take the time needed to assess the applications and match each puppy to the home we feel is best suited to their individual needs.

We do not work on a first-come, first-served basis. Our priority is always to get it right for the puppies and their futures, rather than simply finding homes quickly.

One final, important point – Dad is unknown!

If you are specifically looking for a particular breed or a puppy with predictable breed characteristics, these may not be the puppies for you.

We need their future families to be comfortable with that uncertainty and to love them for the individuals they become, rather than for what they might look like or which breed they might turn out to be.

Rosie and her babies have already had enough uncertainty in their little lives. We want to give each puppy the very best chance of a happy, permanent home with a family who understands the commitment they are making.

The right home matters far more to us than finding a home quickly. ??

Starfish Dog Rescue – dogs are family, not numbers.

name: Nancy
description:
Nancy, pointer, 5.5 years old, medium/large sized girl.

Nancy, our sweet 5.5 year old pointer girl, is ready to find her forever home

Judging by Nancy’s breed and appearance, it is quite likely that she belonged to a hunter, bred for puppies, then dumped once she got too ‘old’.

She is the most gentle girl that gets on with everyone—dogs, people, children. She has a kind soul that doesn’t deserve the life she has led so far. Now it’s our chance to turn that around and make sure the rest of her life is worth living.

Since arriving at the shelter she has been loving and friendly, although, of course, cautious at first. She walks really well on the leash and does not pull.

We don’t think she will need an overly active home but will for sure enjoy her walks. Overall she is a well rounded girl and has shown everyone just how lovely she is and how deserving of a loving home she is.

Unfortunately for Nancy, she has leishmania. We are really hoping this doesn’t mean she is overlooked. Please don’t let this disease define her.

It is easily managed with cheap tablets, doesn’t affect how long she will live, doesn’t affect insurance premiums, and cannot be transmitted to other pets or humans.

Many dogs live long and happy lives with leishmania. Nancy is otherwise a healthy girl. We just hope someone sees how wonderful she is regardless of leishmania.

Nancy is located in Cyprus and, if adopted in the UK, will travel with a passport. She will arrive with 6 months supply of leishmania treatment. She is fully vaccinated and spayed.

name: Sophie
description:
Sophie is a beautiful Portuguese Podengo girl, with a long, rough coat in light tan and white. Poor girl is just 4 years old, and has spent a lot of her life living on the streets and giving birth.

Sophie is a very sweet natured and calm girl, but also a little shy (she takes time to blossom and get to trust you, but once she does she’s a super sweet natured and affectionate girl).

Sophie loves her doggy pals, is good on the lead and a clean girl in her pen. She’s learning that people are kind and now enjoys the love and affection she’s shown but needs someone with time and patience to let her blossom.

Sophie is spayed, up to date with vaccinations and had clear blood tests, and tested negative for Brucella.

We are looking for a family with another friendly dog for Sophie to play with and learn from and older calm children no younger than 11yrs to suit her level of confidence. Sophie is ok with cats.

Sophie mixes well with other dogs, not bothered by cats, very calm and relaxed girl, walks well on her lead, needs someone to give her the time and patience to blossom

name: Marly
description:
This lovely, gentle, large lad is Marley- a 3 year old, male Spanish Mastin. He has a beautiful, brown, textured thick coat, with unusual facial markings.

This handsome boy came to our attention because he is being left in a tiny apartment and a tinier balcony for 23 hours per day!

Marly is a very special and well-loved dog since puppyhood that, due to family circumstances, needs a new home.

He is beautifully trained, used to living inside, and a striking looking dog with a beautiful coat, affectionate with people and social with other dogs.

Due to Marley’s size, we think he is better homed with another female or as an only dog. He is used to the lead he will thrive in a rural environment, maybe a farm, small holding or large gardens, and a family used to walking or other outside activities.

He ignores cats and can live with children over 8 years.

He is very clean in his home, very loving and affectionate, and a nice social demeanor. Used to living with a family.

name: Levi
description:
This little, cheeky chappie is Levi: 9 month old male Podenco Cross, a handsome and very friendly cross breed youngster, with a short, tan and white coat and attractive facial markings and a lovely social demeanour.

Just a little dot and he’s a bit of a whirlwind! But what a lovely little boy he is, very happy, friendly and confident little fella. Levi is only young, about 9 months old and about 12kg so just a smaller puppy boy.

Levi recently came into the rescue from a local vet found abandoned along with Raven, he’s very used to people so we think he has previously lived with a family.

Levi has recently been neutered, got his passport and vaccinations and clear blood tests so he’s ready to travel for the right family.

Levi would make a wonderful companion for a young family and equally he would do very well with any outdoor activities.We are looking for a home with or without another dog and children over 8 years old. Levi hasn’t been tested for cats yet

He is very clean in his pen, very loving and affectionate, cheeky and loves his kennel mates and playing.

name: Oliver
description:
Oliver is a 0 month old male Mastin located in Weymouth.

Gorgeous cuddly puppy Oliver is a beautiful-looking Spanish Mastin boy, with a lush, cream coat and darker face.

He has recently been admitted to his foster home and he is proving to be very calm, friendly and affectionate and, as you can see in the videos, he gets on well with his new kennel mates.

He is learning fast how good it is to have human company, after he was abandoned for so long as a puppy on his own.

At the moment he stands at medium height and is approximately 10 months old. He weighs 20kg and he needs to put some weight on, which is looking very good now as he fills out. He is healthy and has a confident personality.

It’s early days in his foster home and as we get more information we can update his page.

Oliver is going to be a big boy once fully grown, and he is large now and playful, so for that reason we need to look for a home with other young dogs (or no dogs) and older children over 12 years old. He hasn’t been tested for cats

Calm and friendly with people and dogs. Still learning to walk on the lead but improving daily. So much potential!

name: Lucia
description:
Lucia is a 10 month old cross breed fostered in Derbyshire .

Lucia is an very pretty, medium-sized puppy girl Cross breed, with a fluffy off white soft coat She is a lovely gentle girl, and at times quite nervous but very affectionate and loves attention from the volunteers and enjoys being cuddled and groomed.

She gets on well with her kennel mate, but definitely prefers to be with people.

Lucia has just started her lead training which is going well, as we don’t think she is used to being walked because she came with chain round her neck and black stains on her fur so we think she’s just been chained up all her life.

Poor girl, but we are happy she is gaining confidence on a daily rate. Lucia is not cat tested yet. We really want a loving home for this girlie with another friendly dog and children over 12 years.

Very friendly with people and dogs. gentle nature, and is obedient, enjoys learning new things and a laid back.

name: Charlie
description:
Charlie is a 6 years old male cross breed located in Ipswich.

This handsome lad is Charlie, he has a glossy, black short, soft coat and he is a medium sized boy standing at only 20 inches from shoulder to paw.

Charlie is castrated and he is outgoing and loves to play. He loves cuddles and praise. Charlie is 2 years

Charlie is coming out of a home and is well trained, used to children and other dogs plus he has been with cats. He is only being rehomed for owners health reasons.

He loves toys and is playful, clean in the house, good on harness….

He needs to live with another dog preferably a quiet rural environment and needs an experienced home. He can live with children over 6 years.

name: Simba
description:
Simba is a medium mixed breed, 8 years old.

Simba turned up in a village on his own, nobody knew where he was come from but the rescue that took him in say he was in such a state he ‘must have lived through hell’.

He arrived very skinny but is putting on weight but sadly had to have half his tail amputated due to a bad infection.

Despite whatever his past may hold, Simba is learning to enjoy life again, rolling in the grass and living with other dogs.

He gets on well with all the male and female dogs he lives with and he’s also passed his cat test, meaning he could live in a home with a resident cat as well.

name: Penny
description:
Penny is an approximately 1.5 year old female Omani village dog. She is a very friendly, energetic personality and a real enthusiasm for life. She is currently living in a boarding facility in Oman, waiting for the chance to find her own loving forever home.

Penny was found in May 2026 outside the gates of the boarding facility. As soon as she spotted one of the rescue volunteers, she ran straight over to them. It is suspected that her previous owners may have deliberately abandoned her there, knowing that the rescue would take her in and make sure she was safe.

Penny is a very friendly girl who is comfortable around people and enjoys their company. One of the volunteers recently took her home for a day away from the boarding facility and was delighted to see how easily she settled into a home environment. She clearly enjoyed the peace and quiet, even falling asleep and making the most of the opportunity to relax somewhere comfortable.

Although Penny enjoys her quiet moments, she is still young and full of energy. She loves going out for walks, exploring new places and discovering everything the world has to offer. She could make a wonderful adventure companion for someone who enjoys getting out and about. She can become overexcited when out walking and tends to pull on the lead, so she will need some continued training, patience and guidance to help her develop better walking manners.

Penny gets along with the other dogs at her boarding facility, although she has become familiar with them over time. Her compatibility with other dogs will depend on the individual dog, and she would also be perfectly happy as the only dog in the home. She can live with cats and would be suitable for a family with older children aged 8 and above.

She also travels well in the car and behaves beautifully when visiting the vets. Penny really is a lovely young dog who has so much to offer. All she needs now is a family who will give her the love, attention and security she deserves.

Penny is fully vaccinated, microchipped and spayed. She will also be tested for Brucella canis before leaving Oman.

name: Choco
description:
Choco is a 6 year old female cross breed, born on 16 February 2020. She is a small, devoted little companion who has had a very difficult start in life but, thanks to patience, rehabilitation and dedicated care, she has made wonderful progress. Choco is now ready to find a special person who will give her the safe, loving forever home she deserves.

When Choco first arrived in foster care, she struggled with fear based aggression. With time, understanding and careful rehabilitation, she has transformed into a gentle and loving girl. She has been fully assessed and is now ready to enjoy life with someone who understands her need to feel secure and cherished.

Choco is not looking for an adventurous lifestyle. She would much rather enjoy the comfort and peace of home than go on long hikes or spend hours playing fetch. Her idea of happiness is being close to her favourite person, relaxing indoors and claiming a comfortable lap as her own. She is not particularly interested in toys, as her greatest pleasure is simply spending time with her human.

Choco is a devoted little companion who really enjoys one to one attention. She can be a little particular about who looks after her, especially when it comes to brushing and grooming. Although she behaves well and is tolerant when visiting the professional groomer, she much prefers having her own person take care of her. Building that special bond with her human is very important to her.

She gets along well with other dogs and cats and could live happily with a resident dog or as the only dog in the household. She is also currently living with both dogs and cats in her foster home. Because she can be a nervous girl, she is looking for an adult home or a family with children over 12 years old, where she can enjoy a quieter and more settled lifestyle.

Choco has been diagnosed with leishmaniasis. This does not affect her quality of life and her condition is managed with one daily tablet. With appropriate ongoing care, she can enjoy a normal and happy life.

Choco is currently in foster care in Crewe, UK. She will be neutered, vaccinated, microchipped and treated for parasites. She will also have her own pet passport and full rescue back up from Saving Souls Animal Rescue.

If you are looking for a loving little companion who wants nothing more than to be close to you, Choco could be the perfect match.

name: Jakey
description:
Lovely Jakey – 5 month old male Cross-Breed

Possibly Spanish Water Dog or Catalan Sheepdog

Coming to the UK in early December – will be fostered in Gloucestershire

Jakey is one of six dogs I met in Spain that I want to help find their forever homes.

I have been helping the Spanish dogs at Noahsarc for 15 years. Although Starfish mainly helps UK dogs these days, Noahsarc is still very much part of the Starfish family, and I visit twice a year to spend time helping the charity and assessing a few dogs that we can bring back to the UK.

Often, these are dogs who have grown beyond the cute puppy stage or older dogs who have been overlooked. When I return next April, I really don’t want to see Jakey, Tessa, Josh and Billybob all grown up and still waiting for their families.

They are beautiful souls, all for different reasons, and far too special not to have families of their own.

Our dogs don’t arrive in the UK and get delivered to their adopters like Amazon parcels! They come into Starfish foster care first, allowing them time to decompress after their long journey.

You will meet them just as you would one of our UK dogs, with all human and furry family members involved, so we can make sure it is the right match for everyone.

So, let me tell you about our lovely Jakey.

Jakey is Cindy’s son and Tessa’s brother. Sadly, after their owner died, Jakey, his mum and his siblings were left to fend for themselves in the countryside, in an empty house.

They were frightened and in poor condition when they were found, but thanks to the wonderful volunteers at Noahsarc, they have gradually begun to thrive.

Two of the puppies found homes quite quickly, but Jakey and Tessa were still waiting, along with their beautiful mum. So we have agreed to help this whole little family find the futures they deserve.

Jakey has had lots of lovely socialisation with other dogs and enjoys plenty of free-running time with them in the grounds of the rescue centre.

They are also lucky enough to have volunteers who come in most days to take the dogs out for walks and spend time with them.

So, although the outside world is still very new to Jakey, he has had lots of positive experiences with other dogs and people, which is a great foundation for his future.

Jakey is a boy who has grown on me every time I have spent time with him. Watching him discover the world outside the rescue centre, gain confidence and show me more of his personality has made him a very easy boy to love.

I’ve now been out and about with Jakey four times, and the progress he has made has been lovely to see.

Everything was new to him at first: travelling in the car, meeting new people, visiting cafés and shops, hearing strange noises and encountering unfamiliar dogs.

He wasn’t a naughty or difficult puppy; he simply hadn’t experienced these things before and needed time to work them out.

Fast-forward to our most recent trip, which included a shop, the vets and a café, and he was a different boy altogether!

He was much more relaxed in the car, walked more calmly on his lead and was less worried by unfamiliar noises.

He was more confident meeting new people, particularly if they happened to have food to offer, and he settled beautifully in the café while we ate.At the vets, where he had his blood tests in preparation for travelling to the UK, he spent most of his time asleep on the floor and barely seemed to notice the needle going into his leg!

He is becoming much more engaged with me, and I am seeing more of the lovely character underneath that scruffy puppy coat.

He really is a little bundle of scruffy love.

I’ve recorded much of our time together on video, which I’ve shared below, so you can see for yourself how he is progressing.

Although Jakey isn’t a manic puppy, he is likely to be a bright, active dog who will enjoy having things to do. If you’re looking for a dog to join you on walks, learn new things and become part of an active family, he could be just the boy for you.

He needs people who understand that his journey is only just beginning.

We have been introducing him to the outside world here in Spain, and his new family will need to continue that work in the UK, gradually building his confidence and helping him become comfortable with all the things a family dog experiences every day.

We would particularly like to hear from people with rescue experience who understand that confidence develops at different speeds and who can guide him patiently through the rest of his puppyhood and into adulthood.

A home with another friendly, well-adjusted dog could be lovely for Jakey, as he has always been surrounded by other dogs.

However, this isn’t essential if his family can offer him the companionship, time and support he needs and he isn’t going to be left for long periods.

For a little more reassurance, his mum and sister are lovely dogs too and aren’t particularly manic, although, of course, every dog has their own individual personality.

Jakey has already shown me what a lovely boy he can be. He doesn’t need someone to turn him into a different dog; he needs someone to help him continue growing into the dog he is capable of becoming.

With the right family, patience, experience and guidance, I believe he has all the potential to become a wonderful companion and enjoy the life every young dog deserves.

Could you be the family Jakey has been waiting for?

He will be arriving in the UK in early December and will be fostered in Gloucestershire. If you have the experience, time and understanding to help this lovely boy continue his journey, we would love to hear from you.

Jakey is too young to be neutered, so we cannot home him with any entire dogs. His new family will need to arrange his neutering once he has finished growing and maturing.

He will be fully vaccinated, microchipped, have his own Pet Passport and have been blood tested for all Mediterranean diseases.

Out with his mum & sister (he is bigger than Tessa)

name: Cindy
description:
Cindy  – Approx. 2-year-old Collie/Shepherd cross, possibly younger, around 28kg – – Fostered in Gloucestershire

Cindy is one of six dogs I met in Spain that I want to help find their forever homes.

She may not be the sort of dog who immediately throws herself at you for attention, but having spent time getting to know her, I think there is a very special dog here just waiting for someone to discover her.

I have been helping the Spanish dogs at Noahsarc for 15 years. Although Starfish mainly helps UK dogs these days, Noahsarc is still very much part of the Starfish family.

I visit twice a year to help the charity and spend time with the dogs, getting to know them so I can decide which ones we can help bring back to the UK.

Often, these are dogs who have grown beyond the cute puppy stage or older dogs who have simply been overlooked.

Black dogs are particularly easy to miss in rescue, and when I return to Spain next April, I really don’t want to find Cindy still waiting for her chance.

So, let me tell you about this lovely girl.

Cindy had a terrible start in life. She was left trying to survive at a property alongside a small group of other dogs and her four young puppies.

When the rescue team took them in, she was severely emaciated, extremely weak and suffering from a serious infection that had left her with a very high temperature. She had also been shot.

We believe she may have been trying to catch rabbits to feed herself and keep her babies alive when this happened.

With medication, veterinary care and support from Keiron, who runs the kennels, Cindy slowly began to recover. Even when she was desperately weak, her maternal instincts were remarkable.

When she managed to eat, she would try to regurgitate the food for her puppies rather than keep it for herself. She was still putting her babies first, despite having so little left to give.

It is a sad story, but Cindy is so much more than her past. Her puppies have lovely temperaments, and now it is Cindy’s turn to have someone looking after her.

I have been out with Cindy on four occasions, as well as spending time with her at the centre, so I feel I have got to know her pretty well.

She is still a little nervous in the car, but she has made lovely progress. If she is sitting next to someone, she will now settle and fall asleep.

We have been out and about to cafes and shops, and she is happy to settle down and relax. She walks well on the lead, too.

Around other dogs, she is very good. She mostly ignores them, and the younger puppies at the centre love her. She is lovely with them and takes everything in her stride.

With people, Cindy is friendly but a little reserved if she doesn’t know you. She isn’t a dog who immediately gives her heart away to everyone she meets. But she absolutely adores Keiron, who runs the kennels, and is very affectionate with him.

Watching her with him tells me so much about the dog she can be. Once Cindy trusts you, I think that bond will mean everything to her.

There is nothing about Cindy’s temperament that worries me. She is calm around the centre, a lovely, biddable girl who takes things in her stride.

I don’t know whether people have been unkind to her or whether she has simply been ignored for much of her life, but I suspect she hasn’t experienced very much love or individual attention.

She is still a young dog, yet there is something about her that makes her seem much older. She has a quiet acceptance of life, as though she has never expected very much from it.

And that is what I want to change for Cindy.

I want to see her discover that life can be fun. That she can have her own comfortable place in a home, her own person to love, walks to enjoy and all the little things that make a dog’s life special.

I want to see her become excited about life, rather than simply accepting whatever comes her way.

That is why I am looking forward to bringing her to the UK. At the moment, she has to share her space and the attention of the people around her with lots of other dogs.

In a home, with more one-to-one attention, I think we may see a very different side to her.

The home we are looking for is someone who can see what I see in Cindy.

Someone who understands that not every dog arrives ready to shower you with affection. Some need a little time to feel safe, to learn to trust and to discover that they really do matter to someone.

Cindy needs a best friend. Someone kind and patient who will let her settle at her own pace and help her discover all the good things she has missed. After spending so much of her young life looking after her babies, it is finally her turn to be looked after.

Getting the right home for Cindy is particularly important to me. I think she would find it very difficult if she settled into a home and then had to start all over again, so we will take our time finding the right match for her.

We don’t yet know what her recall is like, as she lives in an enclosed area at the centre, but the videos below will give you a good idea of her nature. I am also very happy to share more videos and answer any questions.

Our Spanish dogs don’t arrive in the UK and get delivered to their adopters like Amazon parcels! They come into Starfish foster care first, giving them time to decompress after their journey.

You will meet Cindy just as you would one of our UK dogs, with all human and furry family members involved, so we can make sure it is the right match for everyone.

Cindy is spayed, vaccinated, blood-tested for Mediterranean diseases and has her own Pet Passport.

Could you be the person who shows Cindy how lovely life can be?

Cindy out with her two babies Tessa & Jake

How good is she with the other young dogs melts your heart

Out and about with Josh & BillyBob at the Charity Shop

With some of the other dogs at the centre

name: Jensen
description:
Jensen is a 6-year-old male Cross-Breed. He has been in foster care since arriving in the UK last December and is now ready to find his forever home.

Described as a handsome boy, Jensen has a sweet-natured and friendly personality that makes him very endearing to the people around him.

He is a medium-sized dog with a strong, stocky build, giving him a sturdy and solid appearance. Jensen clearly enjoys human company and thrives on interaction, showing a loving and sociable temperament.

His fondness for people makes him a great companion in a home where he can receive plenty of attention.

Jensen is good with children, although a home with older children aged 12 and above would be more suitable for him.

This recommendation likely reflects his strength and energy levels, ensuring safe and comfortable interactions for everyone involved. He is an active dog who enjoys his walks and benefits from regular exercise to keep him happy and healthy.

His lead training is still ongoing, but he is an intelligent dog who is already beginning to pick up new commands. With continued consistency and patience, he is expected to improve further and become even more well-mannered on the lead.

He is also doing well with recall, which is a promising sign of his responsiveness and willingness to learn.

Jensen would do best as the only dog in the home, as he prefers not to share his space with other dogs. Additionally, he is not suitable to live with cats.

These preferences should be considered carefully to ensure he is placed in an environment where he can feel secure and relaxed.

He is currently in foster in Fleet, giving potential adopters in that area or nearby regions the opportunity to meet him. Jensen is looking for a home that can match his energy, continue his training, and provide him with the companionship he clearly enjoys.

name: Laika
description:
Liaka is a ten year old female Brittany. Laika is quite a small Brittany, very active and energetic for her age. She is very sociable with other dogs and lives in a kennel with a Setter, with whom she shares space and food without any problems.

Laika is very obedient when called within the confines of the shelter (it could be different on an exciting walk), she likes to lie quietly in her bed, and also enjoys running in the enclosure.

Laika has a cheerful temperament and is very affectionate and attached to people. She is a great all round dog.

Laika is a beautiful girl. She was given up by a hunter when no longer any use to him. Laika is now at the shelter we closely with in North Spain ready for a new life in the UK

If you are interested in giving wonderful Laika a home, she is available at Setter Brittany Pointer Rescue. Laika is in Spain and ready to travel to her forever home. Will that be with you?

name: Gomez
description:
Gomez moved into private boarding kennels in July 2025 where he has resided ever since.

After months in a busy kennel block Gomez was becoming stressed. He was reactive to other dogs when walking the kennel line with staff. He was moved to a quieter area where he has now relaxed more and has become a much calmer dog.

Gomez accepts collar/harness and lead but he can try and bite the lead sometimes. He walks really well on the lead with no pulling. He can be a little scared of some people and does bark at dogs he sees. He has not met any children on his walks.

Gomez has been known to tear up his bed with boredom so he will need lots of toys and brain games to keep him busy in his new home. He will also need to get daily physical exercise on walks.

Gomez has probably been left without food in the past so he snatched food and treats from your hand. The kennels have tried to teach him to be gentle. This is something that his new home will need to be aware of and work with him to continue this training.

As Gomez has been living in kennels his toilet training will need a refresher in his new home which will be easily done with a clear, scheduled toileting routine.

As he has spent a long period of time in kennels Gomez will need someone around most of the day. This is so that he can build a bond with his new family.

Any alone time will need to be built up very gradually over time and monitored to ensure Gomez is comfortable being left alone. He may be susceptible to separation anxiety once he has settled in.

Gomez will need an experienced home who can offer him what he needs but take things at his own pace as he will need some adjustment time when he comes out of the kennels.

Gomez will need to be walked on a harness and be given some additional positive training with sights and sounds he hasn’t seen for a while.

Gomez has a lot of love to give and is a good boy. He is now ready to find his forever home where he will be given patience, time, reassurance and be allowed to decompress after a long period in a kennel environment.

He needs someone with experience to guide him, show him what is expected of him using positive reinforcement and give him all the love he has missed out on.

He needs to go at his own pace to ensure he is comfortable with the positive life changes he is experiencing.

name: Harry
description:
Harry is a 9 year old male Cross-Breed who came into care after being rescued from a wild plot of land, where he was living under some bushes.

He was extremely scared and presented with various infected wounds. After some months in care, he has lost his initial fear (he was also helped greatly by the amazing ladies who found him).

Though he is still shy with people until he realises they are not going to hurt him, once he knows you, he will not leave your side.

Harry is medium active. He loves to run but in moderation. He is good with the other dogs at the shelter and enjoys playing and digging.

Harry loves his food and will need to be on a controlled diet to maintain his weight. He is 48 cm tall and weighs approximately 18 kg.

All of the dogs have an international passport (unless born in the UK) and are microchipped. They are fully vaccinated for standard diseases as well as rabies and kennel cough.

All dogs are blood tested for infectious diseases including Leishmaniasis, Dirofilaria, Ehrlichia, Babesia, Anaplasma, Lyme, and Brucella canis.

All dogs, unless there are medical or behavioural reasons not to do so, will be sterilised. Harry is neutered. Medical results and treatments will be advised upon successful application.

An adoption contract and fee, home check, and lifetime rescue back-up apply as standard.

name: Rico
description:
Rico is a 4-year-old male Spanish Bodeguero. This handsome and lively boy comes from a breed originally known for guarding Spanish bodegas, where families stored wine, sherry, and cheeses.

The Bodeguero’s role was to keep the area safe and free from rats — a task that shaped them into intelligent, alert, and loyal companions.

True to his breed, Rico is hardy, active, and full of personality, making him an excellent pet for anyone who loves an energetic and affectionate dog.

Once someone’s cherished pet, Rico was sadly abandoned and found himself in a pound. Thankfully, he’s now safe and cared for, showing just how adaptable and resilient he is.

He’s lead trained, house trained, and wonderfully social with both people and other dogs. Rico’s friendly and confident nature shines through in every interaction, and he’s eager to please those around him.

Rico is fully vaccinated, health checked, microchipped, and neutered, and he also holds a full EU passport, meaning he’s ready to travel to his new home.

He’s an affectionate, outgoing dog who thrives on human connection and activity — whether that’s a long walk, playtime in the garden, or simply spending time with his people.

Rico deserves a loving family who’ll give him the security and companionship he’s been missing and who’ll let his bright, loyal personality truly shine.

name: Serena
description:
Serena is a 5 year old Staffordshire Bull Terrier located in Spain.

Lovely gentle Serena is a five year old small tan SBT girl, weighing 20.2kg, with a tan soft coat and lovely temperament towards humans and other dogs.

She arrived at the pound with her sister Venus who has the same colouring but slightly bigger and they are best of friends and kennelled together.

Serena is a calm girl who already knows how to walk very well on a lead and even sit! Serena is the quieter of the two.

You can see both girls walking together with another dog on the video, and on the other video it shows Serena being hassled by another dogs and she’s not reactive

Poor girls had been abandoned together and they get comfort from being kenneled together, but if they get home offers they can be split

She just loves her walks and just wants love and fuss so the sooner we can get her into a loving home the better.

She can live with children over 10 years old and other gentle placid dogs.

name: Venus
description:
Lovely, sweet Venus is a five year old female Staffordshire Bull Terrier located in Spain. She weighs 23.6 kg and has a soft tan coat with a lovely temperament towards humans and other dogs.

She arrived at the pound with her sister Serena, who has the same colouring but is slightly smaller. They are best of friends and are kennelled together.

Venus is a bit more boisterous and gets excited to be out of the kennel, so staff are giving her a bit of work on the lead.

Because they are always together, they often get put in the park for a mooch, but when taken out on lead, they are very well behaved around other dogs.

Venus is a lovely girl and already knows quite a few commands. You can see both girls walking together with another dog on video, and both are non-reactive.

The poor girls had been abandoned together and find comfort in being kennelled together, but if they get home offers, they can be split.

Venus loves her walks and just wants love and fuss from everyone she meets — a typical Staffordshire Bull Terrier!

She can live with children over 10 years old and other gentle, placid dogs.

Happy, affectionate, friendly, and a fast learner.

name: Zaara
description:
Zaara — 13 Months Old, Energetic, Dog?Social, Ready for an Active Home

Zaara is a 13?month?old young female bursting with life, confidence, and playful energy. She’s a bright, social girl who absolutely thrives around other dogs and needs a home where she can enjoy regular dog?to?dog interaction.

Friendly, affectionate, and eager to learn — she’s a fantastic match for an active family looking for a fun, engaging companion.

Lively, playful, and full of youthful energy • Affectionate once she’s settled • Confident, curious, and switched on • Loves other dogs (male and female) and gains confidence from them • Loves water and outdoor adventures

Zaara is not suited to a quiet or low?activity home — she’s happiest when she has things to do and canine friends to interact with.

Zaara must live with another friendly, playful dog.

She reads dog body language well, enjoys proper play, and settles beautifully after social time. A home with one or more dogs will help her continue developing into a balanced, confident adult.

Zaara is car?friendly but still learning.

She can travel, but it’s a bit scary for her at the moment, so adopters should expect gentle reassurance, short positive journeys, and patience while she builds confidence. Another dog in the car would reassure her.

• An active home • A family with at least one resident dog• People who enjoy walking, enrichment, and training • A secure garden for play • A home willing to continue her routine and guidance An active home

She is still young, so adopters should expect normal puppy?teen behaviors and be ready to support her through them.

Zaara is fully vaccinated and spayed.She is healthy, vet?checked, travels well once settled, and bonds quickly with her people. She is ready for her new start.

name: Nica
description:
Nica is an approximately 3 year old female medium sized cross breed, born around 2023. She is a beautiful girl with a super friendly and affectionate nature, and she is now looking for a loving forever home in the UK where she can enjoy the happy life she deserves.

Nica was recently rescued in Romania after being found abandoned at the roadside with her litter of puppies. Thankfully, they were all brought to safety and are now being cared for in a shelter. Having looked after her little ones, Nica is now ready to find a family of her own.

She is described as a very friendly and affectionate girl, and we hope she will soon have the opportunity to leave shelter life behind and settle into a loving home. Nica would make a lovely companion for someone who is ready to welcome her into their family and give her the care, attention and affection she deserves.

Nica will be able to travel to the UK in January 2027, once her puppies are old enough to be rehomed and travel. She is fully vaccinated and has been blood tested.

Her adopters will receive full rescue back up and ongoing support from PennyPaws Rescue. A home check is required, which can be carried out by video.

name: Rocky
description:
This stunning boy is Rocky, a Casgoine Cross, approximately 2 years old and weights 15kg. He is neutered.

He is the first of the 10 confiscated dogs from the hell hole hoarder.

He’s is the most gentle loving soul despite his passed and horrendous living conditions he still has trust in humans and loves human company and gives lovely cuddles.

Rocky is currently in a foster home with other dogs both male and female small and large. He prefers the quieter home.

Rocky does walk on a lead but he will need more encouragement to feel more relaxed.

Rocky is looking for a family who will give him the time and love to show you his wonderful character

He has meet children and is very friendly.

Rocky is neutered and his free of all Mediterranean diseases.

He will fly to the UK with a negative Leishmania test and a UK APHA Brucella Canine laboratory.

name: Blake
description:
Blake is a 3 year old male Labrador Retriever Cross, currently being fostered in Bulgaria and ready to travel to his forever home.

Medium-to-large in size at around 27 kilograms, Blake has the soulful eyes and gentle nature that make him instantly lovable.

He had a rough start in life, but you’d never guess it from his joyful personality. Blake greets every day with enthusiasm — always up for a walk, a game, or a cuddle.

He’s playful, social, and full of positive energy. His goofy side shines when he’s running around with his doggy friends or flopping over for belly rubs.

This clever boy is quick to learn and loves both mental stimulation and human attention. He’s great on the lead, good in the car, and loves outdoor adventures — the perfect fit for an active person or family who enjoys spending time outside.

Blake gets along wonderfully with other dogs and is friendly with children. Cats can be tested on request. His ideal home would be one where he’s included in daily activities, given plenty of exercise, and surrounded by love and structure.

With the right family, Blake will grow into an extraordinary, loyal companion.

He is neutered, fully vaccinated, microchipped, vet-checked, and travels with an EU pet passport and full DEFRA-approved paperwork.

Blake is patiently waiting for a family to see the wonderful dog he truly is — and to give him the loving forever home he deserves.

name: Morits
description:
What’s worse than seeing puppies growing up in the shelter cage?….older dogs living out their days in the shelter cage, when time on this planet is running out for them.

Meet Morits – A Gentle Soul Ready for His Second Chance

Morits has spent eight long years longing for something many of us take for granted: love, warmth, and a place to call home.

Morits was found living in a field with his brother about 3 years ago and they were taken in by Roberts Dog Sanctuary. His brother has since been rehomed but Morits now waits alone in a shelter in Cyprus, his big heart full of hope.

At his age he should be living in comfort, not sleeping on cold concrete floors.

This handsome boy may be 8, but he still has so much life and love to give. He walks beautifully on the lead and would make the perfect companion for peaceful strolls or quiet afternoons by your side.

Morits is gentle with female dogs and, with the right introduction, could share his space with a calm male friend.

Because of his size, he’s best suited to a home with older children who will respect his need for kindness and calm.

Morits is healthy, ready to travel, and most importantly ready to love. After years of surviving in the shadows, he deserves a retirement filled with soft beds, gentle hands, and a family to call his own.

Give Morits the ending he deserves. Let him show you just how deeply a rescued heart can love.

Morits is currently in Cyprus looking for a home in UK. He will be neutered, vaccinated, chipped, treated for parasites, have his own pet passport and rescue back up from Saving Souls Animal Rescue.

name: (Deceased) Holly
description:
Holly – 8 year old female American Bulldog is a gorgeous girl with striking eyes!

Holly came to us as a welfare case, so we have very little history available on her. She has shown herself to be a laid-back and friendly girl with people, good with her basic commands, and walks nicely on lead.

She enjoys a treat and especially playing ball. Sadly, she is very stressed in kennels and is currently reacting to other dogs in that environment. We may find this improves in a home environment.

Holly would be best suited to being an only dog in a household with experience of large breed dogs. Given her size and the limited background we have on her, we’d prefer older children only. She is not cat tested.

Holly is neutered and microchipped and is currently completing her vaccinations.

If you would like to meet Holly, she is currently situated just outside Sheffield. We’d love to hear from you.

name: Oshi
description:
Oshi is an 18-month-old male Belgian Shepherd Malinois. He was found wandering near a highway in Cyprus, and despite his uncertain past, he has shown signs of being accustomed to home life.

His clean kennel habits suggest he was previously house-trained, as he waits to be let out before relieving himself.

Oshi is a new arrival, so his full temperament is still being assessed. However, he has shown no signs of reactivity to other dogs. He could be rehomed as an only dog or with a resident dog, depending on the adopter’s circumstances. His calm nature and adaptability indicate that he has the potential to thrive in a loving home.

Due to his size and strength, Oshi is best suited for a household with children aged 12 years and above. He has not been tested with cats, so his compatibility with feline companions is unknown. Any potential introductions to cats would need to be done carefully and gradually.

Oshi walks well on the lead, making him an excellent companion for an active adopter who can provide him with regular exercise and mental stimulation.

As a Belgian Shepherd Malinois, he will need an owner familiar with the breed’s intelligence and energy levels to ensure he remains engaged and well-balanced.

Oshi is fully vaccinated, microchipped, wormed, and comes with a pet passport. He is ready to fly to the UK and will arrive with full rescue backup from Saving Souls Animal Rescue, ensuring support for his adopter.

name: Rosheen, Milo and Betsy
description:
The puppies are approximately 3 months old, small to medium sized cross breeds, born around August 2026. Their mother, Nica, is a medium sized cross breed, so the puppies may grow to a similar size. There are 14 puppies from the same litter, all described as gentle, loving and playful. They are now looking for special families who can offer them a loving home in the UK.

The puppies and their mum were found abandoned at the roadside in Romania. They were crying, cold and starving, and thankfully a rescue stepped in to save them all. They are now safe in a shelter, but shelter life is far from ideal for young puppies. It can be cold, noisy and busy, with limited opportunities for the socialisation and everyday experiences that are so important at this age.

The brothers and sisters are sweet natured and playful little puppies. They are at an important stage in their development and would benefit from a loving home where they can begin discovering the world around them, learning new things and growing into happy family companions.

The puppies are fully vaccinated and have been blood tested. They are available to be adopted or reserved now and will be able to travel to the UK in January 2027. The rescue is hoping to find homes for all the puppies so they can leave the shelter and begin their new lives.

Their adopters will receive full rescue back up and ongoing support from PennyPaws Rescue. A home check is required and this can be carried out by video.

name: Willow
description:
Willow is an approximately 6 year old female Hound cross. She is a beautiful girl at the smaller end of medium size, weighing just 13kg and measuring 15 inches from shoulder to paw. Willow was found abandoned on the streets and has been in the rescue’s shelter in Cyprus for the past two months. She is now ready to find a loving home where she can enjoy the comfort and security she deserves.

Willow is an extra special girl with so many wonderful qualities. She is an absolute lady, with a lovely combination of style, grace and elegance. There is something quite special about her personality, and she has a wonderful air of wisdom and understanding. She is a very pleasant and gentle natured dog who makes a lovely impression on everyone she meets.

Willow walks beautifully on her lead and is a pleasure to accompany. She looks to her person for guidance as she walks, showing just how lovely and endearing she can be. She is a calm and agreeable companion who seems to take everything in her stride when out and about.

Her appearance is every bit as lovely as her personality. Willow has a beautiful classic black and tan coat that shines, along with gorgeous ears that add to her charm. She really is a dog who could capture someone’s heart at first sight.

Willow appears to mix very well with other dogs, cats and children, making her a lovely potential addition to a family with existing pets. Her adopters will be very lucky to welcome this special girl into their lives. After being abandoned and spending time in a shelter, Willow deserves the chance to enjoy a home of her own, surrounded by kindness and love.

name: Moose
description:
Moose is a 7 month old male Beagle Hound cross who is currently being cared for in Cyprus. Sadly, he is another young dog who was dumped by hunters. As hunting season begins in Cyprus, unwanted puppies from litters bred for hunting are often abandoned. Fortunately, Moose was lucky enough to find his way into the garden of an animal lover, who gave him the chance of a new beginning.

When Moose was found, he was terribly thin and just skin and bones. With plenty of love, care and good food, he has gradually gained weight and is now growing into a very handsome boy. He is currently living in a foster home with other dogs and cats, and gets along very well with them all.

Moose has had a difficult start to life. Before being rescued, he was kept in a cold, dirty cage, without enough food and without knowing the kindness and affection every young dog should experience. He is now beginning to discover that his past is behind him and that life can be very different.

He is still a little nervous when walking outside on a lead, so he will need a patient home that is happy to give him the time and encouragement he needs to build his confidence. With understanding, consistency and plenty of kindness, Moose can continue learning and enjoying all the new experiences that come with family life.

All Moose wants is a safe home, a cosy bed, kind hands and people who will never give up on him. He has so much love to give and the potential to become a wonderful companion. He simply needs someone willing to give him the patience and affection he deserves, allowing him to grow into the happy and confident dog he has the potential to be.

Moose will be available to travel to the UK in mid December. Could you be the person who gives this lovely young boy the chance of a completely new life?

name: Jasper
description:
Jasper is an approximately 8 year old male cross breed weighing around 25kg. He came into the rescue’s care in July after being one of 10 dogs seized from a hoarding situation. Sadly, he had not experienced much kindness, love or affection during his earlier life, but over the months the rescue has watched this beautiful boy gradually blossom and begin to enjoy the attention he deserves.

Jasper absolutely adores human affection. He is a calm senior dog who is in excellent health. He is neutered and has undergone full blood tests, all of which were negative. Although he does have a few visible battle scars, including small pieces missing from his ears, we will never know exactly what he has endured in the past. What matters now is that he is ready to find a loving home where he can enjoy the comfort, security and affection he may have missed out on for so long.

Jasper enjoys the simple things in life. He loves lying in the sunshine, having gentle walks and spending time with people. He is gradually getting used to walking on a lead, and the rescue is continuing to work with him on this. He also loves his food and has a rather endearing habit of lying down with his bowl between his front legs while he takes his time eating.

Given his past, Jasper would probably be happiest as the only dog in the home. He may possibly be able to live with another dog, but this would need careful and managed introductions. He cannot live with cats. Having potentially spent much of his life competing for food and affection, he now deserves the chance to enjoy both without having to share them.

Jasper would be particularly well suited to a quieter adult home, perhaps with a retired person or couple who would enjoy having a gentle companion by their side. Although he has met many children and has been very gentle around them, an adult only home is preferred so that he can enjoy the peaceful lifestyle he deserves in his senior years.

Please consider giving Jasper the opportunity to experience the loving home every dog deserves. He does not ask for much, just kindness, comfort and someone who will make him part of their life. In return, he has so much love and companionship to offer.

name: Bonnie
description:
Bonnie is a 1 year old female cross breed. She is a beautiful little girl currently living in Cyprus, where she was found by a kind couple who took her into their home to keep her safe. She is now looking for a loving forever home in the UK and, once she has found the right family, she will be able to travel in early December.

Weighing just 10kg, Bonnie is expected to remain a small dog, but she certainly has a huge personality. She loves other dogs and gets along very well with all the dogs in her foster home. She is also cat tested and currently lives happily alongside cats, making her a lovely option for a home with existing pets.

Bonnie is crate trained and is quite happy to take herself off to bed in her crate without any fuss. She is an intelligent girl who is eager to learn and keen to please. She will need a little patience and encouragement with her lead training as she continues to develop her skills.

Above all, Bonnie is looking for people who will offer her kindness, patience and plenty of love. She will need a secure garden where she can enjoy her outdoor time safely. With the right home to help her learn and grow, Bonnie has the potential to become a wonderful family companion, bringing plenty of affection and companionship to those around her.

name: Pluto
description:
Pluto is a 7 month old male Pointer cross who is currently in Cyprus, waiting to find his forever family. He is a gorgeous puppy who is thought to have a little Pointer and possibly some Labrador in his mix, along with a huge amount of lovely personality. Pluto was originally found all alone at the side of a village road, but thankfully he is now in a wonderful foster home. He has blossomed into an incredibly loving, happy and affectionate young dog. He is a well behaved puppy who is already showing just how much potential he has to become a fantastic family companion.

Pluto is an obedient puppy who seems keen to learn and enjoys being around people. He is not interested in trying to escape and is happy to follow his people around, making sure he is never too far away from the action. He also comes back when called, which is a lovely start for such a young dog.

att.PU7nR5VpH8IlFLozJl5c9vqcfYqOY723prTzufKxqJ4

Pluto has already learnt to sit and catch his treats, showing that he is bright and responsive to training. He is not a fussy eater and is happy with his food, and he has also learnt to do his business outside. He sleeps well throughout the night, making him a lovely young dog to welcome into a home.

Pluto is very sociable and gets along wonderfully with other dogs. He also loves children and would be particularly suited to a family with children aged over five who enjoy spending time with dogs. He is equally happy around cats and has shown no problems with them. He has even met chickens and showed no interest in them. These are lovely qualities for a young dog and make him suitable for a household with a variety of existing pets.

Pluto also travels well in the car, which will make trips out and future adventures much easier for his new family. As he is still young, he will need his new owners to continue with his training and socialisation as he grows, helping him develop into a confident and well mannered adult dog. His ideal home would have a securely fenced garden where he can enjoy some playtime and burn off his puppy energy with a few happy zoomies. He would also benefit from having someone at home for much of the day, giving him plenty of companionship, attention and opportunities to continue learning.

Pluto has already made a wonderful start thanks to the care of his foster volunteer, and he has so many lovely qualities to offer. He is affectionate, sociable, eager to learn and happy around children, dogs and cats. With a loving family willing to continue his training and give him the attention he deserves, Pluto has all the potential to become an amazing family dog. Now he just needs someone to offer him the safe and happy home he has been waiting for.

name: Rusty
description:
Rusty is an approximately 5 year old male Rottweiler cross who is currently in a shelter in Cyprus. He is a big, handsome boy weighing around 38kg, with a wonderful personality and a rather infectious permanent smile that has completely won over the people caring for him. In fact, Rusty genuinely believes he is a lap dog and would happily climb onto your lap for a cuddle if given the opportunity.

Rusty is an affectionate boy who loves human attention. While he enjoys playing fetch and going for walks, his favourite thing is receiving cuddles. Given his past, he may not have experienced much affection. Now that he has discovered how wonderful it is to receive love and kindness, he cannot get enough. Even when someone puts just one finger through the gap in his kennel, Rusty will press his whole body against it to enjoy the contact.

Rusty enjoys his walks and walks beautifully on the lead. He also takes treats incredibly gently, which is lovely considering his size and strength. In a securely fenced area, he is fantastic off lead and walks nicely to heel. Rusty keeps his kennel area extremely tidy, preferring to wait until he is outside to go to the toilet. He is not destructive, which is another positive aspect of his personality.

Rusty is a highly intelligent dog with plenty of potential, and his rescuers believe he would benefit enormously from professional training. He will need an experienced owner who understands large and powerful dogs, ideally someone with previous Rottweiler experience who is patient and committed to continuing his training, to provide him with the exercise, mental stimulation and interaction he needs. With the right guidance and consistency, Rusty has plenty of opportunity to develop into an even more wonderful companion.

Rusty needs to be the only pet in the household. Although he is able to walk alongside another dog from the pound without any problems, he is not considered suitable for living with other dogs. His compatibility with cats has not been assessed, and he has not been cat-tested. He has also not been properly assessed around children, so due to his considerable size and strength, his rescuers are looking for an adult only home.

His ideal home would have a medium to large securely fenced garden with safe gates, giving him somewhere to enjoy time outdoors. Rusty has so much affection to give and clearly treasures every moment of human attention. After what may have been a life with very little affection, he is now looking for someone who will make sure he never has to go without love again.

name: Nikki
description:
Nikki is an approximately 2 year old female small to medium sized cross breed who is currently waiting for her forever home in a shelter in Cyprus. She is a delightful little girl weighing just 10kg and measuring approximately 10 inches from shoulder to paw. Nikki was found abandoned on the streets and, thankfully, was taken into the safety of the shelter, where she has been waiting for the past six weeks.

Despite her uncertain start, she has a wonderfully cheerful personality and is now ready to find a family who will give her the love and security she deserves. The rescue manager describes Nikki as energetic, fun loving and very affectionate. She has an incredibly friendly nature and an endearing personality that quickly draws people towards her.

Nikki is a bright and attentive girl who is alert to everything going on around her and approaches life with plenty of enthusiasm. She has a lovely way of bringing happiness into a room and enjoys nothing more than receiving attention, snuggling up on a lap and sharing a cuddle with someone she trusts. She is a very affectionate little companion who will undoubtedly bring plenty of love and personality to her new home.

Nikki is also a very pretty girl with a striking appearance. Her beautiful black coat is low maintenance, making her relatively easy to care for in terms of grooming, and her almost permanent smile gives her an especially charming expression. With her bright personality and affectionate nature, Nikki is sure to bring plenty of enjoyment to the family lucky enough to adopt her.

Nikki walks nicely on her lead, although she would benefit from a little additional training to help her develop her skills further. She appears to mix very well with other dogs and children, so she could be considered for a family home with canine companions or children. However, Nikki does have a tendency to chase cats, so she will need a home without cats.

Nikki has already come such a long way since being found abandoned, and now she needs someone to give her the chance to enjoy life as a much loved family member. She is a happy, energetic and affectionate little girl who has so much to offer and will surely make a wonderful companion.

name: Clement
description:
Clement is a 7 year old male Hound cross who is currently waiting for his forever home in a shelter in Cyprus. He is a rather large and handsome boy with a striking appearance and plenty of character. Sadly, Clement has spent 5 of his 7 years waiting in the shelter for someone to give him the loving home he so thoroughly deserves.

Despite having spent such a large part of his life in rescue, he remains an easy going and affectionate boy who has won the hearts of the shelter staff. He is a firm favourite with everyone who knows him, thanks to his lovely temperament and charming personality.

Clement has great presence and charisma, with a kind and loving disposition that makes him such a special boy. He is an affable and good natured dog who has so much affection to offer and simply wants to be loved and appreciated for the wonderful companion he is. He is also wonderfully undemanding and is likely to be happy with the simple pleasures of family life. His beautiful tri colour coat attracts plenty of attention, with particularly striking brindle markings across his chest, making him a very handsome and distinctive looking dog.

Clement is currently a little overweight, weighing approximately 32kg. Although he is a rather large dog, he has relatively short legs, measuring around 13 inches from shoulder to paw, which adds to his unusual appearance and charm. His coat is also low maintenance, making him a relatively easy dog to look after in terms of grooming.

He enjoys his walks and walks nicely on the lead, which should make daily outings an enjoyable part of life with him. His new family can help him work towards a healthier weight through an appropriate routine and regular exercise.

Clement appears to mix very well with other dogs and children, making him a possible addition to a family with existing dogs or older and younger children. However, he does have a tendency to chase cats, so he would need a home without cats.

After spending so many years waiting for his chance, Clement is now hoping that someone will finally look past the fact that he is no longer a young dog and recognise the wonderful qualities he has to offer. He deserves a comfortable home, a loving family and the opportunity to enjoy all the things that have been missing from his life.

name: Lily
description:
Lily is an approximately 4 year old female medium sized cross breed who was born around 2022. She is currently in a safe shelter in Romania, waiting for the opportunity to travel to the UK and find a loving forever home. Sadly, Lily has endured a very difficult and traumatic past after being rescued from a horrific kill shelter. Her experiences have understandably left her feeling frightened and unsure of the world around her.

She is a very worried and scared girl who will need someone willing to look beyond her initial fear and give her the opportunity to discover what it means to feel safe and loved. Lily has been through so much, and now she deserves a chance to leave her difficult past behind.

Lily will need plenty of time, patience and understanding to help her gradually recover her confidence. She is not a dog who will immediately settle into a new environment or feel comfortable with unfamiliar people, so her adopters will need to be prepared to take things slowly and allow her to progress at her own pace.  She needs a family who understands that helping a frightened dog overcome her past can take time, but who will be willing to offer her the consistency, kindness and affection she needs.

Lily has always lived with other dogs and would particularly benefit from having a calm, confident canine companion in her new home. Having another settled dog around could help reassure her and show her that she is safe, providing a positive example as she gradually adjusts to her new surroundings. Her compatibility with cats is currently unknown and has not been established.

Lily will need an experienced home with adopters who have the time, patience and understanding to help her work through the effects of her traumatic past. A peaceful and predictable household would be important, as she needs an environment where she can feel secure and gradually learn to trust the people around her. She is looking for a home with children aged twelve and over, or an adult only household, where her need for space and a gentle approach will be respected.

Lily is fully vaccinated and has also been blood tested. She will come with full rescue back up and ongoing support from PennyPaws Rescue, so her adopters will have assistance throughout the adoption process and beyond. A home check will be required before adoption, although this can be conveniently carried out by video.

Lily has had a very difficult start to life, but there is now an opportunity for her to experience something very different. She needs a special person or family who will not expect too much too soon and who understands that trust must be earned. With time, patience and a safe environment, Lily can hopefully begin to discover the happier life she deserves.

name: Hannah
description:
Hannah is an approximately 3 year old female small cross breed who weighs between 8 and 10kg. She was born in 2023 and is currently waiting in a shelter in Romania for the opportunity to travel to the UK and find her forever family. She is a very loving girl who has plenty of affection to give to the family lucky enough to welcome her into their lives.

Hannah is a lovely little girl who may be a little shy when meeting new people, but don’t let her initial shyness put you off. Once she has had the chance to get to know you and feels comfortable in your company, her affectionate personality begins to shine through.

Hannah is friendly with other dogs and would be perfectly suited to a home where there are already canine companions. She is also cat friendly, making her a possible addition to a household with existing cats. Her gentle and loving nature makes her a lovely little companion, although she may need a little time and patience when settling into a new home and getting used to her new surroundings. Allowing her to build trust at her own pace will help her develop a strong bond with her new family.

Hannah would be looking for a home with children aged twelve and over, or alternatively an adult only household. Her new family should be prepared to give her the reassurance and understanding she needs while she adjusts to life outside the shelter. Once settled, they will have a sweet and affectionate little companion who will be very happy to enjoy the security of a home of her own.

Hannah is fully vaccinated and has also been blood tested. She will come with full rescue back up and ongoing support from PennyPaws Rescue, so her new family will have support throughout the adoption process and beyond. A home check will be required before adoption, although this can conveniently be carried out by video.

After waiting in a shelter in Romania, Hannah is now ready for the next chapter of her life. She is hoping to find a loving family who will look beyond her initial shyness and give her the chance to show just how affectionate and loving she can be.

name: Trixie
description:
Trixie is an 8 plus year old female small to medium sized cross breed who is currently living in a safe shelter in Romania. She is a lovely, super friendly older girl who has plenty of affection to offer and is now hoping to find a special family to spend her retirement years with. Although she is currently still in Romania, Trixie has her bags packed and is ready to travel to the UK as soon as the right home comes along. After spending time waiting for her chance, she is now looking forward to finding a permanent home where she can enjoy the comfort, security and companionship of family life.

Trixie has a wonderfully friendly nature and gets along well with people, making her a lovely companion for someone looking for a sociable and affectionate dog. She is also cat friendly, which is great news for households that already have cats. She is good with other dogs too and would be suitable for a home where there are existing canine companions. Her easy-going and friendly nature means she has the potential to fit into a variety of households, provided her new family can offer her the care, kindness and attention she deserves.

As an older girl, Trixie is looking for a home where she can enjoy a comfortable and settled lifestyle. She would be suitable for a household with children aged twelve and over, or alternatively an adult only home. Her new family will need to appreciate that she is an older dog and give her the time, understanding and affection she needs to settle into her new surroundings and enjoy her life as a much loved family member.

Trixie is fully vaccinated and has also been blood tested. She will come with full rescue back up and ongoing support from PennyPaws Rescue, giving her new family reassurance throughout the adoption process and beyond. A home check will be required, although this can conveniently be completed by video.

Trixie has so much love to give and is ready to leave shelter life behind for a home of her own. If you are looking for a friendly, sociable older companion who can share her home with cats and other dogs, Trixie could be the lovely addition you have been waiting for.

name: Russo
description:
Russo is a 1 year old male cross breed who is currently enjoying life in his foster home in Cumbria. Despite having so much to offer, Russo has sadly been waiting a very long time for someone to notice him, and despite originally being advertised when he was just a young puppy, he has yet to receive a single enquiry. There is nothing wrong with Russo; he simply hasn’t found his person yet. All he wants is a loving home of his own where he can finally settle down and become part of a family.

Russo can be a little shy when first meeting new people, but once he has had some time to get comfortable, his confidence quickly begins to shine through. He develops into an affectionate, outgoing boy with plenty of personality and lots of love to give. He enjoys the comforts of home, particularly a cosy bed where he can curl up and sleep peacefully throughout the night.

Russo is also house-trained, making him a little easier to settle into a new household. Russo walks nicely on the lead and is comfortable around traffic and busy streets, so everyday walks and trips out should be something his new family can enjoy together.

Russo is a clever and willing young dog who loves his food and treats, making him particularly keen to learn. He enjoys having the opportunity to discover new things and should respond well to continued training and encouragement.

Russo absolutely adores other dogs and would particularly thrive in a home with a friendly, playful canine companion who could share his adventures and provide him with company. He is good with children and could make a lovely addition to a family environment. His compatibility with cats has not yet been assessed, so he is currently untested around them.

Russo has already made wonderful progress during his time in foster care, developing his confidence and learning all the things that will help him become a fantastic family companion. Perhaps this Christmas could finally be his turn to experience the happiness of having a family to call his own.
